The SDK executor normally requires one wallet that matches every supplied step; this example supplies only the single step the current signer reviewed. [SDK builders and executor](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/fee-proxy-builders.ts)

## Check the result

For each step, verify the receipt’s status and original hash. An approval receipt establishes a permission change. For the routed transaction, compare FeeProxy’s creation or deposit event with the intended user, affiliate, gross amount, affiliate fee and forwarded amount. Check the expected MultiVault creation or deposit logs and the resulting term or receiver position. [FeeProxy implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/periphery/FeeProxy.sol)

Send the plan’s exact value. FeeProxy attempts to return any excess to the caller, crediting `pendingRefund(user)` only if the transfer fails. `feeProxyClaimRefundIfAny(feeProxyConfig, { user, recipient })` returns either `null` or a claim transaction for the ledger owner to review and send separately. Select a payable recipient distinct from the proxy and zero address. [Refund helper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/fee-proxy-claim-refund-if-any.ts)

## Troubleshooting

If a fee rises above the encoded guard, the proxy pauses, the recipient rejects a fee transfer, or a deposit misses its share minimum, the routed transaction can revert. A previous approval remains effective. If a receipt is missing or the transaction was replaced, look up the saved hash and replacement in the signing wallet. Reconcile events and current permissions before building and reviewing only what remains. Replaying a successful deposit would fund the vault twice.

## Related

[Deposit and redeem](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/deposit-redeem) · [Batch writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/batch-writes) · [Affiliate profile fields](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/fee-proxy-affiliate-profile)

# Build guides

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build

Choose a guide for the part of your application you are building. You can model identities and inspect candidate atoms offline before choosing a network.

## Set up

- [Install and pin the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) your project needs.
- [Connect to a network](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/connect) and verify the chain ID and deployed contract address.

## Model data

- [Derive IDs and IIDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/derive-ids) from your input and its chosen representation.
- [Build creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles) from the fields in a Creation Profile.
- [Suggest relationships and pick predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/suggest-relationships) for an ordered triple.
- [Link identities with sameAs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/link-identities) after reviewing the evidence that two atoms represent the same entity.

## Process atoms

- [Parse user input](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/parse-input) into candidates and inspect any warnings.
- [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) and trace where a field value came from.
- [Compose an atom runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/atom-runtime) with local plugins, caches, and concurrency limits.

## Write on-chain

- [Create atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/create-atoms) from exact bytes and check the creation receipt.
- [Create triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/create-triples) from three existing term IDs.
- [Deposit and redeem](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/deposit-redeem) with a quote for the chosen vault and curve.
- [Batch writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/batch-writes) when later transactions depend on newly created terms.
- [Route writes through the FeeProxy](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/fee-proxy) and review the required approvals and payments.
- [Build action plans and envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) for a human to inspect before execution.

## Read the graph

- [Check the scope of SDK reads](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/read-with-sdk) when migrating an existing integration.
- [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) you run to read indexed V2 atoms and relationships.

## Apps

- [Use React hooks](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/react) to connect wallet state, contract reads, and transaction feedback.
- [Test locally](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/test-locally) using your own development chain or a funded testnet account.

# Install and pin the packages

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

Install the smallest package set that supports your task and keep its exact versions in your lockfile.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.18 or newer for these examples, which run TypeScript directly; Node 22.21.0 and TypeScript 5.9.3 match these examples. The processing libraries declare Node 20 or newer. Use ESM (`"type": "module"`) and a TypeScript configuration with `module` and `moduleResolution` set to `NodeNext` and `strict` enabled.

V2 names the documentation generation, not a package major version. Use the [package chooser](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/choose-packages) to match a task to its dependencies, or browse all 21 packages in the [package index](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages). The [compatibility reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) records peers and contract artifact boundaries.

## Steps

### 1. Create an ESM project

```sh
mkdir intuition-example
cd intuition-example
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
```

### 2. Install for your task

Choose the relevant command; you do not need every package.

**Build atom identities and triples:**

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

**Read creation fields and relationship suggestions:**

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/classifications@0.1.0 @0xintuition/predicates@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

**Parse, classify, and enrich in a controlled host:**

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/atom-parser@0.1.0 @0xintuition/atom-classification@0.1.0 @0xintuition/atom-enrichment@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

**Prepare contract operations and action envelopes:**

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0 @0xintuition/protocol@4.0.0 @0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

**Use React integration:**

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/react@0.1.0 @0xintuition/protocol@4.0.0 @0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0 react@19.1.0 react-dom@19.1.0 wagmi@2.15.4 @tanstack/react-query@5.90.2 viem@2.31.4
```

Install packages that your code imports directly, even if another dependency currently installs them transitively. Keep React and its renderer on matching versions. Use each package's published entry points; internal `src` paths are not public imports.

### 3. Record the resolved dependency graph

Commit `package.json` and `package-lock.json`; use `npm ci` on subsequent installs. For a TypeScript project:

```sh
npm install --save-dev --save-exact typescript@5.9.3 @types/node@22.20.5
```

For React TypeScript code, also install matching type packages:

```sh
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @types/react@19.1.10 @types/react-dom@19.1.11
```

At the November 17, 2026 registry check, `@0xintuition/sdk@alpha` still resolves to `4.0.0-alpha.0` and `@0xintuition/protocol@alpha` to `3.0.0-alpha.0`. The range `@0xintuition/protocol@3` selects `3.0.0`, not the pinned stable release. Avoid copying those older install selectors. `latest` currently matches the stable pins, but exact pins keep future installs reproducible.

## Check the result

Run `npm ls --depth=0` to inspect direct versions, then compile your project with `npx tsc --noEmit`. Resolve peer errors before running examples. Installing packages does not start a backend: follow [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) to read indexed V2 data from your own source-built Core node.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Import not exported | Use an entry point listed on that package's reference page. |
| CommonJS import error | Set ESM and use a compatible Node runtime. |
| Missing peer | Install the package's declared peers in your application. |
| Provider returns nothing | Inspect runtime support, provider configuration, and result diagnostics; installation alone does not enable a provider. |

## Related

[Build a music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog), [creation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles), and [action envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) use these pins. Source: [release policy](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/release.md).

# Link identities with sameAs

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/link-identities

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

Prepare a `sameAs` triple when two existing atoms refer to the same recording and a reviewer has checked the evidence.

## Before you start

Retain the exact original bytes for both atoms, their entity levels, and the source records used to identify them. Read [sameAs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as) and [triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples).

For your own project, follow [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). To run the [offline example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/blob/84242e8f4399ac758c942e85b343e0512245a6cf/examples/v2/identity-linking/src/link-identities.ts), install its locked dependencies from the documentation repository root with Node.js 22.21.0.

```sh
npm ci --prefix examples/v2 --ignore-scripts
```

## Steps

### 1. Compare the two source records

In the synthetic catalog, the older atom stores a JSON payload with a title and a catalog URL in its `sameAs` field. The newer atom stores the bare IID `int:isrc:USRC17607839`. The catalog editor has verified that both source entries describe the recording with that ISRC. The URL in the older payload is a reference the editor can inspect. Adding another URL would change those serialized bytes and produce a different atom ID.

### 2. Screen the candidates and record the review

Check what each candidate identifies before comparing its identifiers. A review article can quote the exact ISRC while identifying a different entity. A second recording can share a title while carrying a different ISRC. Leave candidates with missing evidence for later review. This catalog requires a matching canonical ISRC and explicit approval for this particular workflow. Other domains need evidence appropriate to their entity level.

```ts
import type { Hex } from 'viem';
import { inspectIntuitionId } from '@0xintuition/iid';
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { sameAsId } from '@0xintuition/predicates/sameAs';
import { buildTriple } from '@0xintuition/primitives/triple';

type CatalogRecord = {
  atomData: Hex;
  level: 'recording' | 'article';
  recordingIid?: string;
};

export function planLink(
  left: CatalogRecord,
  right: CatalogRecord,
  reviewerApproved: boolean,
) {
  if (left.level !== 'recording' || right.level !== 'recording')
    return { reason: 'Different entity level' };
  if (!left.recordingIid || !right.recordingIid)
    return { reason: 'Missing recording identifier' };
  const a = inspectIntuitionId(left.recordingIid);
  const b = inspectIntuitionId(right.recordingIid);
  if (
    !a.valid ||
    !b.valid ||
    a.scheme !== 'isrc' ||
    b.scheme !== 'isrc' ||
    a.iid !== b.iid
  ) {
    return { reason: 'Recording identifiers do not match' };
  }
  if (!reviewerApproved) return { reason: 'Awaiting review' };
  const subjectId = calculateAtomId(left.atomData);
  const objectId = calculateAtomId(right.atomData);
  if (subjectId === objectId) return { reason: 'Already the same atom' };
  const claim = buildTriple(subjectId, 'sameAs', objectId);
  if (!claim.success) throw new Error(claim.errors.join(', '));
  return { claim: claim.value };
}
```

### 3. Review the edge before creating it

Supply each original payload as hex-encoded bytes in `atomData`. For UTF-8 text, call `stringToHex` on the exact stored string, including any spaces. For example, the six literal characters `0x6162` encode as `0x307836313632`. If the archive already gives the two binary bytes as `0x6162`, pass that hex value directly. Compare the printed subject, predicate, and object IDs with the intended terms. The locally built triple is a proposal. To publish the reviewed edge, follow [Create triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/create-triples). Both original atom IDs continue to identify their respective payloads.

## Check the result

```sh
node examples/v2/identity-linking/src/link-identities.ts
```

The accepted fixture prints two distinct atom IDs and the claim ID `0x84c9260e71757e9c7d5e33fa8bd370a7794160910b8e59ced21cb4e27911402f`. The article produces “Different entity level,” the title alone produces “Missing recording identifier,” and the second recording produces “Recording identifiers do not match.” A matching pair without approval remains “Awaiting review.”

## Related

[Identity ladders](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder), [equivalence and candidate review](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/08-equivalence.md), [IID inspection](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/src/parse.ts), and [triple blueprints](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/triple.ts).

# Parse user input

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/parse-input

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0

Turn a pasted URL, IID, or text label into a local candidate that your application can inspect before classification.

## Before you start

Choose how many input bytes your host can accept and apply that limit at the transport boundary. This example also sets a 64-byte parser limit to make the oversized case easy to try. See [atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing).

For your own project, follow [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). To run the [offline example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/blob/c3b1eaa91a822bb59b20cb6de2bc9b874a00b7b0/examples/v2/music-catalog/src/parse-input.ts), install its locked dependencies from the documentation repository root with Node.js 22.21.0.

```sh
npm ci --prefix examples/v2 --ignore-scripts
```

## Steps

### 1. Make local parsing explicit

Pass `remoteFetch: false` for pasted input. The package default allows remote inspection for eligible URLs and IPFS inputs. With inspection disabled, URL detection only interprets the supplied text. The parser trims outer ASCII whitespace for detection and measures the original input in UTF-8 bytes for the size limit.

### 2. Use the result kind and preserve warnings

For a URL, take `canonicalUrl`. For an IID, check `valid` before using `canonicalIid` and keep the reason when validation fails. A `plain_string` is a label you can offer for classification or manual entry. The helper preserves the parser’s warnings for all returned candidates and handles `ParseError` codes separately.

```ts
import { parseAtom, ParseError } from '@0xintuition/atom-parser';

export async function parseCandidate(input: string) {
  try {
    const result = await parseAtom(input, {
      remoteFetch: false,
      maxInputBytes: 64,
    });
    const { kind, warnings } = result;
    if (result.kind === 'iid') {
      return {
        kind,
        warnings,
        valid: result.valid,
        iid: result.canonicalIid,
        anchorEligible: result.anchorEligible,
        reason: result.reason,
      };
    }
    return {
      kind,
      warnings,
      value:
        result.kind === 'url' ? result.canonicalUrl : result.normalizedInput,
    };
  } catch (error) {
    if (!(error instanceof ParseError)) throw error;
    return { error: error.code };
  }
}
```

### 3. Decide what to retain

Present a canonical identifier to the caller for review. Keep free text available for correction or [classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich). Even a syntactically valid identifier still requires evidence that it belongs to the intended entity.

## Check the result

```sh
node examples/v2/music-catalog/src/parse-input.ts
```

| Input | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| ` https://example.org/catalog ` | `url` with canonical URL `https://example.org/catalog` |
| `INT:ISRC:US-RC1-76-07839` | `iid`, valid, with `int:isrc:USRC17607839` |
| `int:unknown:example` | `iid`, invalid, with reason `unknown_or_malformed_iid` |
| `A catalog label` | `plain_string` |
| Spaces only | `EMPTY_INPUT` |
| 65 ASCII characters | `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` |

All four returned candidates in this run have an empty warnings list, including the invalid IID. Use the IID’s `valid` field for the decision.

## Related

[Atom parser package](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser), [detection order](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/detect.ts), [remote inspection and byte checks](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/parse.ts), and [IID result fields](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/iid.ts).

# Query a Core node

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core

Run your own Core node from source and read its indexed graph through the Query API.

## Before you start

Read [indexing and querying](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/indexing-and-querying) to see how chain events reach the API. Core is an application you fork and build from its repository. Install Git, Docker with Compose v2, Bun 1.3.11, Node 20 or newer, and `curl`; keep at least 5 GiB free. The initial setup downloads dependencies and supporting images. No wallet or API key is required for default public reads.

Core source: [a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/tree/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420). Supporting image tags can move; the source pin is not a promise of identical container artifacts.

## Steps

### 1. Fork and pin the source

Fork [Intuition Core](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core), replace the username placeholder, and select the documented source revision:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/intuition-core.git
cd intuition-core
git remote add upstream https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core.git
git fetch upstream a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420
git switch -c local-node a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420
git rev-parse HEAD
```

Verify that the final command prints the selected commit. A fork lets you maintain your own changes while keeping this baseline identifiable.

### 2. Build locally and wait for health

```sh
scripts/bootstrap.sh --no-start
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d --build
COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml scripts/bootstrap.sh --skip-install
curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health
```

The first command creates `.env` if needed and installs the frozen Bun lockfile. The second explicitly rebuilds Core services from source. The third reuses installed dependencies and waits for API health. Explicit Compose selection avoids inheriting a published-image override.

The default stack starts databases, migrations, the Query API on port 3000, atom services on port 4010, and parse/classification/enrichment workers. It does **not** start chain ingestion or projections automatically. API liveness does not prove chain indexing or provider completion.

### 3. Read a bounded page

```sh
curl -fsS 'http://localhost:3000/api/atoms?limit=10&offset=0'
curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/api/predicates
curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/api/stats
```

Atom lists return `data` and `pagination`. `pagination.count` counts rows in that response, not all matching records. The default limit is 25, with a maximum of 100. Public reads return active, public rows; an empty page is a valid result on a fresh node. Substring `q` filtering is not semantic ranking, and offsets can shift as rows arrive.

This typed helper validates only the contract fields it uses and keeps processing state distinct from chain presence:

```ts
type AtomSummary = {
  id: string;
  isOnchain: boolean;
  classificationType: string;
  parseStatus: string;
  classificationStatus: string;
  enrichmentStatus: string;
};

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

export async function readAtoms() {
  const response = await fetch(
    'http://localhost:3000/api/atoms?limit=10&offset=0',
    {
      method: 'GET',
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000),
    },
  );
  if (!response.ok)
    throw new Error(`Core request failed: HTTP ${response.status}`);
  const payload: unknown = await response.json();
  if (
    !isRecord(payload) ||
    !Array.isArray(payload.data) ||
    !isRecord(payload.pagination)
  ) {
    throw new Error('Unexpected Core list response');
  }
  const atoms: AtomSummary[] = payload.data.map((row: unknown) => {
    if (
      !isRecord(row) ||
      typeof row.isOnchain !== 'boolean' ||
      ![
        'id',
        'classificationType',
        'parseStatus',
        'classificationStatus',
        'enrichmentStatus',
      ].every((key) => typeof row[key] === 'string')
    ) {
      throw new Error('Unexpected Core atom summary');
    }
    return {
      id: row.id as string,
      isOnchain: row.isOnchain,
      classificationType: row.classificationType as string,
      parseStatus: row.parseStatus as string,
      classificationStatus: row.classificationStatus as string,
      enrichmentStatus: row.enrichmentStatus as string,
    };
  });
  return { atoms, pagination: payload.pagination };
}
// Call readAtoms() only after starting your own Core node.
```

Import and call `readAtoms()` after your node is running. It has no top-level request.

| Operation | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/atoms/{id}` | One public atom and its documented processing fields. |
| `GET /api/atoms/{id}/triples` | Triples touching the atom in any subject, predicate, or object position. |
| `GET /api/atoms/{id}/artifacts` | Provider artifacts and their statuses. |
| `GET /api/triples` | Filter by `subject_id`, `predicate_id`, or `object_id`; use `expand=terms` for term summaries. |
| `GET /api/stats/pipeline` | Processing-stage counts. |
| `GET /api/schema` | Local knowledge-graph table metadata; this remains unauthenticated even in gated mode. |

Use complete term IDs from your own records. The pinned OpenAPI does not specify every optional semantic extension returned by the implementation; this guide makes no guarantee about additional identity, context, resolution, or display payloads. Predicate-list records also need checking before protocol use: a node's seeded vocabulary is not a substitute for the packages' canonical predicate bytes and IDs.

### 4. Choose how records reach your node

**Index a chain.** Set `INTUITION_RPC_URL`, `CHAIN_ID`, `MULTIVAULT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS`, and `MULTIVAULT_START_BLOCK` for your chosen deployment in `.env`. `MULTIVAULT_END_BLOCK` optionally bounds the range. Then explicitly enable indexing:

```sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile indexing up -d --build
COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml scripts/bootstrap.sh --indexing --skip-install
```

A successful chain receipt can precede the projected Core record. Check network selection, indexing scope, and ingestion/projection progress before concluding a record is missing. The source commit does not choose a chain deployment for you.

**Insert off-chain records.** In default `API_AUTH=public-read`, writes require an operator-issued writable key. Keep it on the server and send `Authorization: Bearer <your key>`. `POST /api/atoms` accepts an `input` string; `POST /api/triples` accepts `subject_id`, `predicate_id`, and `object_id` for existing terms. Send an anchor's exact `data` as `input`, without serializing that string twice or reformatting its bytes. First creation returns 201; an existing record returns 200, with the response's `created` flag indicating the outcome.

These writes change only that node's off-chain graph. They do not submit a chain transaction or register URI context on-chain. Creating chain terms and waiting for indexing is a separate workflow. Processing after insertion is asynchronous and may be skipped or fail; do not promise completion merely because insertion succeeded.

## Check the result

A healthy `/health` response has `status: "ok"`; a degraded response reports `status: "degraded"` and `database: "unreachable"`. Read results reflect your node's data, so this guide does not prescribe graph counts. Inspect `isOnchain` separately from parse, classification, and enrichment statuses.

The optional semantic API flag `API_ATOM_SEMANTIC_READS_ENABLED` and worker flags `WORKERS_IID_READ_ENABLED` and `WORKERS_IID_RESOLUTION_ENABLED` default off independently. Enabling the API flag alone does not activate worker resolution or guarantee provider artifacts.

## Troubleshooting

| Result | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Connection refused | Compose status, API logs, and host port configuration. |
| 401 `api_key_required` or `invalid_api_key` | Correct node, bearer header, and active key. |
| 403 `api_key_not_writable` | A writable key for the authorized mutation. |
| 400 `invalid_input` or `invalid_term_id` | Valid input and complete 32-byte term IDs. |
| 413 `input_too_large` | Input size; store large assets separately. |
| 404 `not_found` | The requested term may be absent or not public. |
| Empty or pending metadata | Worker configuration, diagnostics, provider support, and credentials. |

Auth modes are `open`, `public-read`, and `gated`; choose the policy for your deployment deliberately. Use `make status`, `make logs SERVICE=api`, and `make down` for routine operations. `make down` preserves data volumes.

## Related

[Build a music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) produces exact local atom and predicate data. [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains the separate on-chain boundary.

Pinned sources: [OpenAPI contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/openapi.yaml), [API reference](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/api-reference.md), [bootstrap script](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/scripts/bootstrap.sh), [Compose services](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docker-compose.yml), and [configuration](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/configuration.md).

# Use React hooks

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/react

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0

Use the same MultiVault deployment for a wallet-free atom lookup and a wallet-approved creation in your React application.

## Before you start

Install the pinned packages and peers in a React host. The [worked React app](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/react-app) includes the dependencies, connector, mount and browser bundle instructions. Have a testnet RPC URL and an existing 32-byte atom term ID for the read. Creation also requires an injected wallet on Intuition testnet and native funds for the creation cost and gas. [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) · [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms) · [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes)

## Steps

### 1. Match the providers to your deployment

Give wagmi the chain and the reader's RPC endpoint. Keep one query client for the lifetime of the provider. The testnet preset resolves the MultiVault address from the deployments package. For a custom deployment, supply a verified chain, chain ID and MultiVault address through the provider’s `config` prop and configure the same chain in wagmi. [Provider implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/provider.tsx)

```tsx
function Providers({
  endpoint,
  children,
}: {
  endpoint: string;
  children: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [config] = useState(() =>
    createConfig({
      chains: [intuitionTestnet],
      connectors: [injected()],
      transports: { [intuitionTestnet.id]: http(endpoint) },
    }),
  );
  const [client] = useState(() => new QueryClient());
  return (
    <WagmiProvider config={config} reconnectOnMount={false}>
      <QueryClientProvider client={client}>
        <IntuitionProvider network="testnet">{children}</IntuitionProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>
    </WagmiProvider>
  );
}
```

### 2. Read the atom by term ID

Mount the reader after validating the term ID. `useAtom(termId, { enabled, curveId, chainId })` reads the contract through wagmi. The provider supplies the chain and the contract supplies the default curve when you omit those overrides. The result includes the atom bytes and vault totals when all component reads succeed. Treat a missing result as an incomplete read. Only an explicit false `isAtom` establishes the negative result returned by this hook. [Read hook implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/hooks/use-atom.ts)

```tsx
function AtomResult({ termId }: { termId: Hex }) {
  const query = useAtom(termId, { enabled: true });
  const cache = useQueryClient();
  if (query.isLoading) return <p role="status">Reading the atom…</p>;
  if (query.isError || !query.data)
    return (
      <>
        <p role="status">
          Could not read all atom fields. Check the term ID and RPC.
        </p>
        <button onClick={() => void cache.refetchQueries({ type: 'active' })}>
          Retry reads
        </button>
      </>
    );
  if (!query.data.isAtom)
    return <p role="status">No atom exists for this term ID.</p>;
  return (
    <dl>
      <dt>Atom bytes</dt>
      <dd>
        <code>{query.data.atomData}</code>
      </dd>
      <dt>Curve ID</dt>
      <dd>{String(query.data.curveId)}</dd>
      <dt>Total assets (wei)</dt>
      <dd>{String(query.data.totalAssets)}</dd>
      <dt>Total shares</dt>
      <dd>{String(query.data.totalShares)}</dd>
    </dl>
  );
}
```

### 3. Review and submit one creation

Call `useCreateAtomFlow()` inside the component. Enable review only after the wallet connects on the selected chain and the hook returns an atom cost. Prepare the UTF-8 data, one asset allocation in native wei and the encoded call. Display the sender, target, chain, arguments and value before enabling submission. An account, chain, payload or cost change requires a new review.

Only the submit button calls `createAtom({ data, assets })`. It invokes ordinary MultiVault `createAtoms` with value equal to the sum of allocations. The example assigns the exact creation cost to its single atom. Additional deposits change the amount the user must review. URI context registration uses a separate protocol operation. [Creation flow](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/hooks/use-create-atom-flow.ts) · [Create atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/create-atoms)

## Check the result

While the wallet is open, show that approval is pending. After broadcast, display the submitted hash from the hook. Keep the wallet on the selected chain while the flow polls. Compare that attempt’s submitted hash with `receipt.transactionHash` once `createAtom` resolves. A wallet replacement can produce a successful receipt with a different hash. Show both hashes and ask the reader to inspect the replacement before retrying.

For the original hash, check receipt success, sender and MultiVault target. This one-atom example also requires one `AtomCreated` event from that transaction and MultiVault. Check its creator, exact atom bytes and term ID derived from those bytes. Only then select the term for a contract read on the same chain. [Creation flow tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/__tests__/use-create-atom-flow.test.tsx)

## Troubleshooting

If the cost is unavailable, retry the contract read and keep submission disabled. If the user declines the wallet request, let them start a fresh review. A reverted receipt rejects the flow. If you already have a hash and receipt polling fails, inspect that hash on the selected chain before retrying. [Transaction flow implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/hooks/use-transaction-flow.ts)

## Related

[Build the React app](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/react-app) · [React package reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/react) · [Query indexed data on your Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core)

# The SDK read client

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/read-with-sdk

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

For indexed V2 reads, run a Core node and use its [Query API](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). The pinned SDK read client calls the hosted V1 GraphQL API and is not a V2 read path.

There is no V2 GraphQL endpoint yet; one is planned for Intuition Core. The V1 GraphQL API is documented in the [V1 docs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1/graphql-api/overview).

## Endpoint mapping

`getIntuitionApiUrl('mainnet' | 'testnet')` selects these V1 endpoints:

| Selection | Endpoint |
| --- | --- |
| `mainnet` | `https://mainnet.intuition.sh/v1/graphql` |
| `testnet` | `https://testnet.intuition.sh/v1/graphql` |

The `@0xintuition/sdk/api` client remains part of the pinned package's public exports. Its endpoint mapping does not change when you start Core, whose Query API has a separate HTTP contract. V1 endpoints remain supported through the V1 documentation.

## Scope

The client exposes atom lookups by ID, label, or data and triple lookup by ID. It is not a general search, traversal, or write API. A label is not a unique identity. Missing rows return `null`; HTTP and GraphQL failures throw. See the [generated API reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/api) for the exported types and signatures.

Source: [SDK endpoint constants and client interface](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/api/index.ts). This page describes that pinned implementation; it does not promise a future endpoint migration.

# Suggest relationships and pick predicates

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/suggest-relationships

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0

Build a relationship picker that proposes a recording’s artist using the Creation Profile and the predicate registry.

## Before you start

Start with a recording atom ID and a candidate target atom whose classification your application has checked. The example derives both IDs from synthetic payloads. Read [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications) and [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates).

For your own project, follow [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). To run the [offline example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/blob/c3b1eaa91a822bb59b20cb6de2bc9b874a00b7b0/examples/v2/predicate-picker/src/suggest-relationships.ts), install its locked dependencies from the documentation repository root with Node.js 22.21.0.

```sh
npm ci --prefix examples/v2 --ignore-scripts
```

## Steps

### 1. Read the recording’s recommendations

Look up the selected key in `musicRecordingCreationProfile.relationships`. Each entry describes the subject classification, predicate and expected objects. For `byArtist`, the recording is the subject. An artist goes in the object slot. A picker can display the predicate label and suggest targets classified as a music group or a person.

### 2. Check the target and resolve the predicate

This picker handles classification hints. It omits a recommendation when the key is absent or the candidate’s classification falls outside those hints. After checking the target, resolve the profile’s predicate ID through the registry and keep the registered spelling, ID and status together.

```ts
import { musicRecordingCreationProfile } from '@0xintuition/classifications/creation/music-recording';
import { getPredicateById, getPredicateId } from '@0xintuition/predicates';
import type { Hex } from 'viem';

export function suggestRelationship(
  recordingId: Hex,
  key: string,
  target: { id: Hex; classification: string },
) {
  const relation = musicRecordingCreationProfile.relationships.find(
    (entry) => entry.predicate.key === key,
  );
  if (!relation) return { reason: 'No profile recommendation' };
  const allowed = relation.expectedObjects.some(
    (hint) =>
      hint.kind === 'classification' && hint.slug === target.classification,
  );
  if (!allowed)
    return { reason: 'Target falls outside the recommended classifications' };
  const predicate = getPredicateById(relation.predicate.id);
  if (!predicate || predicate.key !== key)
    return { reason: 'Unknown predicate' };
  return {
    subjectId: recordingId,
    predicateId: getPredicateId(predicate.key),
    objectId: target.id,
    label: predicate.name,
    status: predicate.status,
  };
}
```

### 3. Present the proposed relationship

Display the recording, “by artist,” and the selected group for review. The registry’s `proposed` status describes the predicate vocabulary. The application still needs to verify that this particular group performed this recording and that the terms exist before it submits a claim.

## Check the result

```sh
node examples/v2/predicate-picker/src/suggest-relationships.ts
```

For the group, the helper prints the recording ID as subject, the group ID as object, the label `by artist`, and status `proposed`. The predicate ID is `0x13d5d4ad6ae3a4e1b5043141b6ce4633c2df4646eaefc9e45eba899c45ce235b`. The album yields “Target falls outside the recommended classifications.” An empty key yields “No profile recommendation.”

## Related

[Build creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles), [recording relationship definitions](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/metadata-predicate-matrix.ts), and [predicate registry lookups](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/predicates.ts).

# Test locally

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/test-locally

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0

Test a contract interaction on Intuition testnet, or deploy on your own Anvil chain and trace a new atom into Core.

## Before you start

Choose testnet to exercise a shared deployment or Anvil to control the chain, deployment and indexing start block. Review [package installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) and [how indexing works](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/indexing-and-querying). Testnet writes require a throwaway account you control. For Anvil, use a trusted development machine with Git, Docker Compose v2, Bun 1.3.11, Node 20 or newer, `curl`, `jq`, and at least 5 GiB free. The first build needs network access for dependencies and images.

## Steps

### 1. Choose your test route

**Testnet.** Check that your client reports chain 13579 and resolves the published testnet MultiVault using [Connect to a network](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/connect). For a write, request tTRUST for your test account's public address, then follow the first-write walkthrough to review the atom, payment and gas before confirming. Check for a successful receipt and record its term ID. If you also index testnet, use a start block verified for that exact contract. Core's upstream smoke-test window uses a historical deployment. [Testnet faucet](https://testnet.hub.intuition.systems/) · [First testnet write](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/first-write) · [Deployment definitions](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/packages/contracts/src/addresses.ts).

**Local Anvil.** Continue below for chain 31337. The deployer sends transactions only on your local chain when run with these Compose services. Keep this development chain accessible only to trusted callers.

### 2. Fork Core and prepare the pinned source

Fork the Core repository, replace `YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME` with the owner of your fork, and run these commands in the directory where you want to keep the clone. Verify the printed commit before proceeding. Bootstrap creates `.env` from `example.env` if needed and installs the frozen Bun lockfile. [Pinned bootstrap script](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/scripts/bootstrap.sh).

```sh
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/intuition-core.git
cd intuition-core
git remote add upstream https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core.git
git fetch upstream a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420
git switch -c local-devnet a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420
git rev-parse HEAD
scripts/bootstrap.sh --no-start
```

### 3. Deploy the local MultiVault and read its state file

Start Anvil, then run the source-built deployment job in the foreground. Continue only after it prints `==> DONE` and exits successfully. It writes its state file before running the acceptance transaction, which creates a local atom and checks its events. Rerunning the job can create another acceptance atom even when it reuses the contracts. [Deployer](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/packages/contracts/src/deploy/cli.ts) · [Acceptance transaction](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/packages/contracts/src/deploy/acceptance.ts).

```sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile devnet up -d anvil &&
  docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile devnet run --build --rm devnet-deploy
```

Compose mounts `./devnet` from the host at `/state` in the deployer. Inspect the generated proxy and the block where it was deployed.

```sh
jq -e 'select(.chainId == 31337) | {chainId, MultiVault, deployBlock}' \
  devnet/deployments-devnet.json
```

### 4. Index that deployment

In the Core checkout's `.env`, edit the existing entries shown below. Replace the two placeholders with the exact `MultiVault` address and decimal `deployBlock` from step 3. Keep `MULTIVAULT_END_BLOCK` empty to follow the local head. The indexer runs inside Compose and reaches Anvil by service name. Host-side RPC clients reach the same chain at `http://localhost:8545`. [Environment settings](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/example.env).

```dotenv
INTUITION_RPC_URL=http://anvil:8545
CHAIN_ID=31337
MULTIVAULT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS=<your generated MultiVault>
MULTIVAULT_START_BLOCK=<your generated deployBlock>
MULTIVAULT_END_BLOCK=
USE_TYPED_READER=true
```

Enable both profiles and build the graph services from the pinned Compose file. Naming the services starts their datastore and migration dependencies and leaves the completed deployment job out of this step. From the host, check the API once the database migrations finish. [Source Compose file](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docker-compose.yml).

```sh
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml --profile devnet --profile indexing up -d --build \
  anvil api indexer projections
curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/health
```

## Check the result

A healthy API can still be catching up to Anvil. Request one public atom. This command uses port 3000, the default host mapping. If the page is empty, expect `count: 0` and `firstId: null`.

```sh
page=$(curl -fsS 'http://localhost:3000/api/atoms?limit=1&offset=0') &&
  printf '%s\n' "$page" | jq '{pagination, firstId: .data[0].id}'
```

Once the page contains a term ID, fetch that record. Compare its ID with the term ID in the deployer's acceptance output when inspecting the same atom. Look for `isOnchain: true` on the atom projected from Anvil. The parse status can remain pending with the processing workers stopped.

```sh
atom_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$page" | jq -er '.data[0].id | strings | select(test("^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$"))') &&
  curl -fsS "http://localhost:3000/api/atoms/$atom_id" | jq '.data | {id, isOnchain, parseStatus}'
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Next check |
| --- | --- |
| Deployment job exits with an error | Read the error and verify the Anvil service is healthy. A state file may already exist even if acceptance failed. |
| Empty page after the API becomes healthy | Inspect `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml logs indexer projections`. Check the configured chain, proxy address and start block against the active deployment. |
| Testnet receipt succeeds but the local API has no record | Confirm that this Core instance is indexing the testnet contract and that its configured range covers the transaction's block. |

## Related

[Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) covers host ports, read policies and graph operations. The pinned [local devnet guide](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/local-devnet.md) describes Anvil state persistence.

# Atom classification

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0

Atom classification interprets an input using plugins. A classifier recognizes a pattern, such as a tagged term or a service URL. An eligible resolver can then describe the entity and the evidence for its type. A type match may tell you how to display an input while leaving the identity of a particular recording or artist unresolved.

**Builds on:** [Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing), [Classifications and Creation Profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications).

**Implemented by:** [@0xintuition/atom-classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification).

## How it works

A classifier matches the input. The engine selects an eligible resolver for the match and execution mode. For a local resolver to run in `client-only` mode, declare its `executionMode` as `deterministic` and implement it with local data. Register any type the resolver emits. [Classification README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-classification/README.md), [plugin authoring](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-classification/docs/plugin-authoring.md), [resolver eligibility](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-classification/src/engine.ts).

When resolution succeeds, `resolved.classifications` contains canonical envelopes. Each has a `type`, its `data`, and `meta` identifying the plugin, provider, and fetch time. `resolved.publishable` projects the fields eligible for publication. Identity fields are eligible by default, richer public fields depend on their source policy, and volatile fields stay out. The application still chooses the representation and whether to publish it. [Canonical output contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-classification/docs/canonical-output-contract.md).

## Atom classification - Example

The local plugin in [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin) recognizes the prefix in `idea: semantic grounding`. Its classifier recognizes an idea with a nonempty name. Its deterministic resolver trims the text after the prefix and emits a registered `DefinedTerm` whose `data.name` is `semantic grounding`. An app can now show the term using the canonical result and inspect the publishable projection before preparing atom bytes.

Compare the title `One More Time` in the [catalog example](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich). The plain-text plugin can interpret it as a `Thing`. The title alone gives the app no basis for selecting a particular recording IID.

## Common mistakes

- Reading `resolved.atoms` as the canonical contract. That array is a compatibility projection. Read the canonical envelopes and their metadata when evaluating evidence.
- Assuming a matching classifier guarantees a usable resolver result. Check for a resolved envelope and a usable type before handing data to enrichment.
- Marking a resolver deterministic while it calls a provider. Keep network-dependent resolution in a suitable server mode.

## Next

[Enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment) uses classification and identifier hints to gather provider evidence. [Atom runtime and pipelines](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime) shows how to reuse engines and bound their work.

# Atom parsing

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0

Atom parsing turns a raw input string into a candidate that an application can inspect. The parser keeps the original input, trims outer ASCII whitespace for detection, and returns a kind with fields specific to that kind. A catalog can use those fields to decide whether to validate an identifier, inspect a URL, or ask the user what a title refers to.

**Builds on:** [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms), [The Intuition Identifier (IID)](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid).

**Implemented by:** [@0xintuition/atom-parser](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser).

## How it works

Call `parseAtom` with `remoteFetch` set to `false` for local detection. Branch on `kind` before reading kind-specific fields. For an IID candidate, inspect `valid` and `canonicalIid`. A malformed candidate still has kind `iid` and carries a reason. Parsing a valid IID returns locally. [Parser README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/README.md), [local detection](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/detect.ts), [IID validation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/iid.ts).

URL and IPFS inputs enable remote inspection by default. When a fetch is permitted and a target is available, the parser can inspect response bytes to distinguish a webpage, an image, or another content type. Set a request deadline and a byte limit for this work. For untrusted URLs, enforce destination restrictions at your network boundary as well. [Parsing and fetch policy](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/parse.ts), [remote transport policy](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/README.md#remote-transport-policy).

## Atom parsing - Example

A catalog import has three cells. With remote fetching disabled, their results call for different decisions.

| Input | Local result | Catalog decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://example.com/catalog` | `kind` is `url`, with a canonical URL and no remote inspection | Keep the link as a lead. Its contents are still unknown. |
| `int:mbid:recording:b1a9c0e9-d987-4042-ae91-78d6a3267d69` | `kind` is `iid`, with a valid canonical recording IID | Pass the canonical value to the registry to learn which providers support that scheme. |
| `One More Time` | `kind` is `plain_string` | Retain the title and ask for an identifier to distinguish recordings with the same name. |

The second row uses the synthetic recording in [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich). Normalization helps interpret a cell. When deriving an atom ID, use the exact bytes of the representation you choose to publish.

## Common mistakes

- Treating every `int:` prefix as a valid identifier. Check the validation fields before using a candidate as an anchor.
- Reporting a recognized URL as a verified recording. Local detection established its syntax. Even with remote inspection enabled, a denied request or timeout can leave the content unknown.
- Replacing the original atom bytes with trimmed input when looking up an existing atom. A change in bytes can change its ID.

## Next

[Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification) explains how plugins use evidence to assign a type.

# Atom runtime and pipelines

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0

An atom runtime supplies configured classification and enrichment engines for a host application. The host can parse inputs, pass the results through those engines, and choose when to cache, cancel, or retry work. Pipeline helpers bound concurrent requests and isolate repeated provider failures. Core adds the workers and durable records a self-hosted node needs.

**Builds on:** [Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification), [Enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment).

**Implemented by:** [@0xintuition/atom-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-runtime), [@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime).

## How it works

Choose the plugins, provider credentials, cache adapter, and time limits for a workload. Parse the input under your network policy. Use classification and identifier hints to select the next stage when enough evidence is available. The runtime reuses its classification engine and caches enrichment engines by preset and identity capability. A memory cache belongs to the process. [Atom runtime](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/README.md), [engine lifecycle](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/src/runtime.ts).

Use bounded concurrency when processing independent inputs. `forEachBounded` returns outcomes in input order even when callbacks finish in a different order. A circuit breaker wrapped around a provider call can refuse new work after a failure threshold. After its reset interval, it admits one probe. A successful probe closes the circuit. [Pipeline runtime](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/pipeline-runtime/README.md), [circuit breaker](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/pipeline-runtime/src/circuit-breaker.ts).

## Atom runtime and pipelines - Example

Suppose a catalog queues a recording, an artist, and a release with a concurrency limit of two. The recording and artist can start together. If the artist finishes first, the release can start while the recording is still running. The caller still receives the recording's outcome first in the result array. It can retain the artist's successful outcome even if the recording's callback rejected. [Bounded catalog example](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime).

If the caller cancels the import, the parent abort signal stops queued work and signals active callbacks. Each callback must pass the signal to its underlying I/O. During shutdown, abort or finish outstanding work, then call `dispose()` on the runtime. Disposal prevents future engine lookups. An engine reference already held by a callback can outlive it. [Runtime example](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-runtime).

## Common mistakes

- Creating a new runtime per row. This discards the opportunity to reuse engines and their caches across the batch.
- Assuming a timeout or disposal stopped a provider request that ignored cancellation. Forward the request signal and check the outcome.
- Treating a cached classification as a durable graph record. Core workers claim stages and persist their results separately. [Core architecture](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/architecture.md).

## Next

[Indexing and querying](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/indexing-and-querying) follows chain events and processing results into a Core node's Query API.

# Atoms

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

An atom gives an app something to refer to. A catalog might need to refer to a recording, its artist, or its liner notes. For each one, the app chooses data, encodes it as bytes, and derives a 32-byte atom ID. Other apps can refer to those same bytes by ID. The real-world recording, the chosen bytes, and the resulting ID play different roles.

**Builds on:** Nothing; this is the base of the ladder.

**Implemented by:** [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol).

## How it works

Suppose a catalog calls a recording “Night Ferry.” Another catalog could use the same title for a different recording, or use a different title for the same recording. Choosing a representation comes first. An app can store the title as text, encode a structured description, or use a canonical identifier for the recording. A short title alone carries no catalog or artist information.

The protocol hashes the exact payload bytes with an atom-specific salt. The ID fits in a Solidity `bytes32`. Copying the bytes preserves the ID. Adding a trailing space to plain text, or changing the field order in serialized JSON, changes what gets hashed. To recover the payload of an existing atom, read its stored data by ID on the intended deployment. [Atom ID derivation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/atom-id.ts) · [MultiVault atom reads](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVaultCore.sol)

## Atoms - Example

A historical record contains the ten characters `0xdeadbeef`. The same spelling can describe two distinct inputs.

| Meaning | Bytes passed to the hash, in hexadecimal |
| --- | --- |
| Literal text, encoded as UTF-8 | `0x30786465616462656566` (10 bytes) |
| A hexadecimal byte sequence | `0xdeadbeef` (4 bytes) |

`calculateAtomId` accepts both strings and hex. When the original field meant text, encode it explicitly. This local helper keeps the payload, its byte encoding, and its ID together. The same `dataHex` can later be reviewed as the creation payload.

```ts
import { calculateAtomId as atomIdFromData } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { stringToHex as encodeData } from 'viem';

export function preserveAtom(data: string) {
  const dataHex = encodeData(data);
  return { data, dataHex, id: atomIdFromData(dataHex) };
}
```

## Common mistakes

- **Hashing the displayed title to look up a structured atom.** Use the exact serialized payload or the ID supplied by its publisher.
- **Using an ID as the payload for a new atom.** Hashing those 32 bytes makes another identifier.
- **Assuming a locally calculated ID already exists.** Creation on the selected MultiVault checks that the payload is nonempty, fits its configured length limit, and is new. [Creation checks](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol)

## Next

- [Triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples) connect atoms. [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids) explains how to reproduce their IDs.
- [Vaults](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults) hold positions in a term.
- [Intuition Identifiers](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid) name entities. [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) determine which identifying bytes reach the protocol.
- [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications) define shared fields for an entity type. [Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing) begins with an input whose format may be unknown.

# Bonding curves

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

A bonding curve answers two questions for a vault at a particular moment. How many shares will a deposit buy? How many assets will a redemption return? The curve defines the conversion rule. Some curves also charge fees that depend on how much is already in the vault or when a holder acquired shares.

**Builds on:** [Vaults, shares and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults).

**Implemented by:** [curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol).

## How it works

On an initialized **linear curve**, the asset value of one share is proportional to the ratio of total assets to total shares. Depositing at that ratio need not raise the price. If a vault receives additional assets without minting shares, each existing share represents more assets. A **progressive curve** uses a different rule. Its marginal price grows with total share supply according to its slope. [Linear pricing](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/linear-curve.ts) · [Progressive pricing](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/curves/ProgressiveCurve.sol)

The **dynamic-fee flat-price curve** keeps the underlying conversion at par and varies the fee. A deposit spanning several tiers pays each band’s configured rate on the portion in that band. The contract tracks a holder’s shares in lots according to their entry tiers, and redeems the highest-tier lots first. To estimate a holder's redemption, account for those lots as well as MultiVault’s fees. A vault-wide preview uses the current tier for the account-less curve fee. [Dynamic-fee curve and holder quotes](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/curves/DynamicFeeFlatPriceCurve.sol)

## Bonding curves - Example

Imagine an initialized linear vault with 3 asset units and 2 share units. To find the shares for a deposit of 2 net asset units, multiply by the share supply and divide by the asset balance. The result, `2 × 2 / 3`, rounds down to **1 share unit**. To acquire exactly 1 share unit at that state would require `1 × 3 / 2` rounded **up to 2 asset units**. To acquire exactly 2 share units requires 3 asset units.

```ts
import { createLinearCurve, type CurveState } from '@0xintuition/curves';

const curve = createLinearCurve();
const state: CurveState = { totalAssets: 3n, totalShares: 2n };
export const preview = {
  depositShares: curve.previewDeposit(2n, state),
  mintAssets: curve.previewMint(2n, state),
};
console.log(preview); // 1n share for a deposit; 3n assets to mint 2n shares.
```

The `n` suffix denotes a JavaScript `bigint`. These small values illustrate integer rounding using only the curve. For a proposed transaction, a MultiVault preview also applies the relevant fees and initialization costs. [Deposit calculation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol)

## Common mistakes

- **Choosing a curve by a familiar number.** Check the selected deployment’s curve registry and configuration before interpreting a curve ID.
- **Applying the last tier’s fee to the whole deposit.** A deposit can cross several fee bands even while the underlying asset-to-share price stays flat.
- **Deriving minimum proceeds from a curve quote alone.** A holder-specific curve quote can still exclude MultiVault's protocol and exit fees.

## Next

[Signals](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/signals) interprets positions priced by these curves. [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards) distinguishes the charges on a transaction from a holder’s eligibility for emissions.

# Classifications and Creation Profiles

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0

A classification describes a kind of entity in Intuition. It gives that kind a stable slug, a type and a set of fields, and can declare an identity ladder. A Creation Profile brings together the fields an app should show and the relationships it can suggest when someone enters an entity of that kind.

**Builds on:** [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms), [The Intuition Identifier](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid), [The identity ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder).

**Implemented by:** [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications).

## How it works

Start with what a row represents. A track can be modeled as a `music-recording`, whose schema.org type is `MusicRecording`. Its identity ladder looks for an ISRC, then a MusicBrainz recording reference, then a name. The form can collect more facts than the ladder needs. [Music recording classification](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/generated/specs/music-recording.ts)

The generated Creation Profile carries a label, type and required flag for each field. Its relationship suggestions identify a predicate and the expected object types. For example, `byArtist` accepts a `music-group` or a `person`. Typing an artist name records text. Making a graph claim takes a recording ID, a predicate ID and an artist ID. [Music recording Creation Profile](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/generated/creation/music-recording.ts)

## Classifications and Creation Profiles - Example

For a recording called “Night train”, the profile exposes five fields in this order.

| Field key | What the form collects | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | The track title, such as “Night train” | Yes |
| `byArtist` | An artist credit | No |
| `inAlbum` | An album title | No |
| `isrc` | A recording code when known | No |
| `sameAs` | A list of URLs identifying this recording | No |

With just the title, the name field satisfies the form’s required-field rule. The identity ladder can still yield a weak name-derived IID. If an artist is known only by a shared display name, keep the credit as text until you can identify the intended object. [Creation Profile field and target tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/creation-profile.test.ts)

## Common mistakes

- Treating every available schema.org property as a required form field. Use the profile’s field list and its required flags.
- Inferring an edge from a suggested relationship or from a `sameAs` URL in form state. Those values can guide a later claim.
- Confusing a Creation Profile, which describes input, with a representation profile, which describes stored bytes.

## Next

- Look up field meanings in [schema.org vocabulary](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/schema-org) and relationship terms in [Predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates).
- Use [The IID registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry) to classify an identifier, or [Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification) to classify parsed input.
- Follow [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) when a reviewed result is ready to submit.

# Deterministic IDs

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0

An ID is deterministic when anyone following the same rule with the same inputs gets the same result. Two catalogs can derive the ID of a recording independently and agree on which claim to reference before either opens a connection to a chain.

**Builds on:** [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms), [Triples, counter-triples and nested triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples).

**Implemented by:** [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives).

## How it works

The protocol uses Keccak-256, a hash that returns 32 bytes. It gives atoms, triples and counter-triples distinct salts. A salt here is a fixed public value, the Keccak-256 hash of the UTF-8 text `ATOM_SALT`, `TRIPLE_SALT` or `COUNTER_SALT`. “Followed by” below means concatenating the raw bytes in that order. [Salt definitions](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/hash.ts) · [Solidity derivation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVaultCore.sol)

| ID | What to hash |
| --- | --- |
| Atom | The atom salt followed by the 32-byte hash of the payload bytes. |
| Inline registry predicate | First serialize a JSON-LD `DefinedTerm` in the order `@context`, `@type`, `name`, `description`. Apply the atom rule to that document. |
| Triple | The triple salt followed by the 32-byte subject, predicate and object IDs, in order. |
| Counter-triple | The counter salt followed by the positive triple ID. |

For a registry predicate, use the package’s exported ID or its exact atom data. For instance, the key `byArtist` looks up a record whose name is “by artist.” Changing its description changes the serialized bytes even if the displayed name stays the same. [Predicate serialization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/predicate-id.ts)

## Deterministic IDs - Example

This offline example uses plain text for three invented atoms, including a deliberately local relationship. Compare the results of a trailing space, a swapped pair and a counter-triple.

```ts
import {
  calculateAtomId,
  calculateCounterTripleId,
  calculateTripleId,
} from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { toHex } from 'viem';

// Synthetic bytes, with no claim about a real recording or artist.
const data = 'example:recording';
const recordingId = calculateAtomId(data);
const artistId = calculateAtomId('example:artist');
const predicateId = calculateAtomId('example:relationship');
const tripleId = calculateTripleId(recordingId, predicateId, artistId);
const reverseId = calculateTripleId(artistId, predicateId, recordingId);
const counterId = calculateCounterTripleId(tripleId);
console.log({
  sameBytes: recordingId === calculateAtomId(toHex(data)),
  changedBytes: recordingId !== calculateAtomId(`${data} `),
  reverseDiffers: reverseId !== tripleId,
  counterDiffersFromReverse: counterId.toString() !== reverseId.toString(),
});
```

All four comparisons print `true`. The text and its UTF-8 encoding describe the same bytes. The space adds a byte. Reversal changes the order of the hash inputs. The counter rule hashes the original triple ID with its own salt.

## Common mistakes

- **Hashing printed hex characters by accident.** Match the meaning of your input. An original text field containing `0xdeadbeef` needs explicit UTF-8 encoding. Raw bytes represented in hex can go directly to the ID helper.
- **Using a wallet address or transaction hash to look up a term.** The caller, chain and transaction do not enter these ID formulas. Creation and balances still belong to a particular deployment.
- **Treating a calculated ID as proof of identity.** It lets you reproduce a reference to bytes. Establishing which real-world entity those bytes describe requires the identifier and its evidence.

## Next

[Intuition Identifiers](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid) addresses the real-world naming problem. [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains how a known ID becomes part of an on-chain operation.

# Enrichment

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0

Enrichment adds evidence to a classified atom. A provider adapter can return an artifact, such as a catalog record with a title and artist credit. A separate extraction step selects fields for the classification and records their sources. An application can refresh these descriptions while retaining the IID and exact atom bytes it already uses.

**Builds on:** [Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification), [The IID registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry).

**Implemented by:** [@0xintuition/atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment).

## How it works

1. **Plan.** Use the IID registry to find candidate providers for the identifier. A plan describes capabilities. No provider has run at this point.
2. **Execute.** Give the enrichment engine a classified input, identifier hints, and the plugins you selected. A matching adapter can return an artifact with provider metadata. Inspect the artifacts, errors, and skipped providers together. For example, Core documents keyless MusicBrainz access and separate credentials for Spotify. [Enrichment engine](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/README.md), [Core provider configuration](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/enrichment-providers.md).
3. **Extract.** Apply the field extractor for the classification. Keep accepted values with their field provenance, dropped fields with their reasons, and the list of missing required fields. Some extraction paths can make additional requests. The catalog fixture supplies a fetcher that rejects remote requests. [Field extraction](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/src/extraction/extract.ts), [field result types](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/src/extraction/types.ts).

## Enrichment - Example

The [recording fixture](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) runs a local adapter with the synthetic recording's MusicBrainz ID. The adapter returns one artifact containing the name `One More Time` and an artist credit. Its metadata identifies the provider as `local-synthetic-fixture` and supplies the fetch time and source URL.

The recording extractor returns an empty `values` object and lists `name` in `missingRequired`. Although the name is present in the artifact, the pinned extractor does not map this artifact into recording fields. A catalog can keep the artifact available for review and leave the required name unfilled. If the identifier hint is removed, the same adapter is skipped. [MusicBrainz artifact format](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/docs/musicbrainz/index.md).

## Common mistakes

- Showing a provider listed in a plan as the source of a fact. Attribute a value to the artifact or extraction result that actually supplied it.
- Dropping successful artifacts because another provider failed. Save the available evidence and its errors so the caller can decide whether to retry.
- Rebuilding an existing atom's bytes after a display title changes. Store refreshed evidence separately when the atom should keep its ID.

## Next

[Atom runtime and pipelines](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime) explains how a host shares engines, limits concurrent work, and releases resources.

# Fees, epochs and rewards

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0
