Creating a term, depositing assets and redeeming shares have different costs. Routing a transaction through FeeProxy can add an affiliate fee. Epoch rewards come from a separate contract, TrustBonding, which uses locked balances and protocol utilization to allocate emissions over time.

**Builds on:** [Vaults, shares and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults), [Bonding curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves).

**Implemented by:** [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk), [curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves), [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery).

## How it works

**Creation.** MultiVault’s `getAtomCost` and `getTripleCost` expose configured creation costs. Each includes a fixed creation protocol fee and a minimum share seed. A triple seeds both positive and counter vaults. The creation preview estimates how much of a proposed payment remains available for the creator’s shares after costs and applicable fees. [Creation costs](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVaultCore.sol) · [Creation previews](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVault.sol)

**Deposits and redemptions.** MultiVault applies a protocol fee to the applicable asset base, rounding the fee up using the configured denominator. Depending on the operation and term, entry or exit fees, atom-wallet fees, a fraction allocated to component vaults, or a curve’s own fee may also apply. Read the deployment’s configuration and preview the specific operation before deciding on a minimum output. [Fee calculation and allocation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol)

**Affiliate routing.** FeeProxy forwards deposits and creations for a registered active affiliate. The affiliate’s schedule may include a percentage and a fixed amount. The proxy checks the fee caps, caller's fee guard, and required approvals. It deducts the affiliate fee before forwarding the remainder to MultiVault, where protocol rules still apply. [FeeProxy routing and previews](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/periphery/FeeProxy.sol)

**Epoch rewards.** TrustBonding uses a token lock to establish a bonded balance. An epoch is a time interval defined by the emissions controller. The contract uses the account’s share of total bonded balance at epoch end and the available epoch emissions to calculate its raw reward. System utilization adjusts the emissions from epoch 2 onward. Personal utilization adjusts the account’s reward. A vault deposit alone does not establish a bonded balance. [TrustBonding reward calculation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/emissions/TrustBonding.sol)

## Fees, epochs and rewards - Example

Suppose a FeeProxy deposit has 20,100 asset base units gross, a hypothetical affiliate rate of 50 basis points, and a fixed fee of 3 units. One basis point is one ten-thousandth. The percentage component is `20,100 × 50 / 10,000`, rounded down to 100 units. Adding the fixed 3 gives **103 units to the affiliate** and **19,997 units forwarded to MultiVault**. Quoting shares uses the forwarded amount and the vault’s own costs. [Affiliate fee formula](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/periphery/FeeProxy.sol)

For rewards, suppose the current epoch is 8. A claim in that epoch targets epoch 7. The caller needs a positive adjusted reward for epoch 7 and must still be eligible to claim it. The contract checks for an earlier claim, a nonzero recipient, an unpaused claim path, and remaining epoch budget. The budget can cap the payout. Use `getUserCurrentClaimableRewards` to read the account’s estimate before reviewing any claim transaction. [Claim checks](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/emissions/TrustBonding.sol)

## Common mistakes

- **Treating gross assets as the share purchase amount.** Follow the deductions from the gross payment to the assets actually priced by the vault.
- **Treating an affiliate fee as the protocol fee.** Each layer has its own base, settings and rounding.
- **Saving up several old epoch claims.** The claim path targets only the immediately preceding epoch and cannot pay a claim during epoch zero.

## Next

Use the [FeeProxy reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/fee-proxy) for routing and the [TrustBonding reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/trust-bonding) for locks and claims.

# The identity ladder

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

An identity ladder is an entity type’s ordered list of ways to identify one of its members. Start at the strongest rung for which all required facts are valid. A registered identifier can distinguish recordings with the same title. A fallback recipe based only on that title gives the same result for both.

**Builds on:** [Schemes and canonical form](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes).

**Implemented by:** [iid-ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

## How it works

For each scheme rung, extract the input and apply that scheme’s canonicalization rules. Missing or invalid values let the next rung try. A `gen1` rung requires every field in its recipe. If no rung can fire, `deriveIntuitionId` returns `undefined`. [IID spec §5.2](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/05-identity-ladders.md#52-selection-algorithm) · [Derivation implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/src/derive.ts)

A `gen1` IID carries the classification slug, a stable recipe tag and the first 16 bytes of the Keccak-256 digest. The hashed input contains the slug and normalized recipe fields. The tag identifies the recipe even if its position in the ladder changes. A P1 payload carries the evidence needed to repeat the derivation. [IID spec §6.3](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/06-gen1.md#63-derivation) · [IID spec §6.6](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/06-gen1.md#66-mandatory-p1-representation)

For provider imports, `projectIdentifierLadder` in the ladder package takes strong identifiers, provider identifiers and a canonical URL. It returns a selected IID or an envelope fallback with `iid: null` and a reason. Its fallback is distinct from deriving a classification’s `gen1` recipe. [Projection ladder](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-ladder/README.md)

## The identity ladder - Example

Follow the recording ladder for three possible catalog rows.

| Available evidence | First usable rung |
| --- | --- |
| A valid ISRC and a MusicBrainz recording reference | The ISRC identifies the recorded performance. |
| An invalid ISRC and a valid MusicBrainz recording reference in `sameAs` | The second rung selects the recording’s MusicBrainz ID. |
| Only the title “Night train” | The `gen1` recipe tagged `r3` uses the normalized title. Another recording called “Night train” gets the same weak IID. |

Artist credit and album title are useful catalog fields. Neither enters this name-only recipe. [Canonical music recording ladder](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/entity-types/music-recording.md)

## Common mistakes

- Adding a timestamp to distinguish two name-only matches. This breaks repeatability. Keep the ambiguity visible until stronger evidence arrives.
- Replacing an old atom’s bytes when you discover an ISRC. A stronger identifier can be represented separately and linked to the earlier atom.

## Next

See how [Classifications and Creation Profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications) tell a recording form which fields to collect and which identity ladder to use.

# The IID registry

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0

The IID registry package interprets an identifier for an application. Given an IID, it can return a classification, an ordered list of provider capabilities and hints extracted from the value. Each answers a different question about what an application could do next.

**Builds on:** [Schemes and canonical form](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes), [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications).

**Implemented by:** [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry).

## How it works

The canonical scheme registry defines the names admitted in an IID and freezes each scheme’s canonicalization rules. The package’s lookup tables supply an additional mapping from an IID to a classification and possible enrichment providers. Both lookups work offline. [IID spec §9.1](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/09-registry-governance.md#91-the-registry) · [Canonical scheme registry](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/registry.json) · [Registry package](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/README.md)

`classificationForIid` can return `undefined`, including for a valid identifier without a supported classification. For a bare Wikidata QID the identifier alone gives insufficient type information. `providersForIid` lists potential capabilities in order. `identifierHintsForIid` supplies canonical values a provider could use if one is configured. Neither an available capability nor an identifier hint establishes that a record was found.

## The IID registry - Example

For the standalone fixture `int:isrc:USRC17607839`, the three results serve different consumers.

| Lookup | Result | What it tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Classification | Slug `music-recording`, type `MusicRecording` | Which entity type to display. |
| Provider plan | `musicbrainz`, `spotify`, `apple-music` | Which capabilities an enrichment engine can consider, in order. |
| Identifier hints | An `isrc` entry with value `USRC17607839` | Which exact value to supply to an adapter. |

Now compare a composition identifier, `int:iswc:T0345246801`. It is valid, but the pinned registry has no classification mapping for its scheme. Preserve that unknown result instead of labeling it a recording. [Classification tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/src/__tests__/classification.test.ts) · [Identifier hint tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/src/__tests__/hints.test.ts)

## Common mistakes

- Treating a provider plan as a fetched artifact. An enrichment engine must select an enabled adapter and run it before reporting any external facts.
- Treating an empty provider list as a validation error. It means the package has no identifier-driven capability for that input.

## Next

Read [Enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment) to see how a configured provider can return fields with provenance.

# Schemes and canonical form

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

A scheme owns the rules for one kind of identifier. It defines which raw values are acceptable, how to spell them canonically and what they identify. Once the scheme has produced a canonical IID, equality is a byte-for-byte comparison.

**Builds on:** [The Intuition Identifier](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid).

**Implemented by:** [iid-spec](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

## How it works

Split an IID at the first two colons. The prefix is exactly `int:`. A registered scheme name contains 1–32 lowercase ASCII letters, digits or hyphens. Its value contains 1–220 visible ASCII characters, including any further colons. The entire IID is limited to 256 bytes. Reject unknown schemes. [IID spec §2.2](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/02-grammar.md#22-requirements) · [IID spec §2.3](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/02-grammar.md#23-parsing)

| Class | Source of identity | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | An authority assigns the value. | An ISRC names a recording. |
| B | The entity supplies an intrinsic key. | A content digest identifies file bytes. |
| C | A `gen1` recipe uses the available facts. | A title alone can match several recordings. |

Within Class A, T1 is an open standard with offline format validation, T2 is a community registry with open data, and T3 is a proprietary registry. Ladders prefer T1 and T2 over T3. These tiers describe access and verifiability. [IID spec §3.2](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/03-identity-classes.md#32-the-three-classes) · [IID spec §3.3](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/03-identity-classes.md#33-openness-tiers)

Apply the scheme’s canonicalization rules. For text in a `gen1` recipe, `NORM-1` first applies Unicode NFKC, folds punctuation, applies full Unicode case folding, then trims and collapses whitespace. Accents survive. Scheme-specific values can be case-sensitive. [IID spec §4.2](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/04-normalization.md#42-the-algorithm) · [IID spec §4.6](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/04-normalization.md#46-requirements)

The package accepts typed `wd` values and adds the `apple-podcasts`, `letterboxd` and `podcast-index` schemes. Both sources define weak `acct` handles. Because handles can change owners, the package requires at least P1 for them. This changes P0 eligibility while preserving the canonical identifier bytes. The packaged copy also omits §7.8 and differs in chapters 00, 01, 04, 05 and 09. [Canonical account scheme](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/schemes/acct.md) · [Packaged amendments](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/spec/09-registry-governance.md#97-pre-publication-amendments)

## Schemes and canonical form - Example

To canonicalize an ISRC, remove hyphens, spaces and dots, convert letters to uppercase, then validate the format. The canonical vectors `us-sm1-00-07459` and `US SM1 00 07459` both yield `int:isrc:USSM10007459`. The shorter `USSM1000745` fails validation. A successful format check cannot establish that the issuing authority assigned the code to a particular recording. [ISRC scheme and test vectors](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/schemes/isrc.md)

By comparison, the text recipe maps `"  Inception  "` to `"inception"`. These are normalization steps on inputs. Compare the final IIDs exactly as emitted. [IID spec §2.4](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/02-grammar.md#24-comparison)

## Common mistakes

- Splitting `int:hash:sha256:…` at every colon. The value starts at `sha256:`.
- Lowercasing an entire IID or stripping accents from all names. Both can change which values compare equal.
- Inferring a `sameAs` claim from a spelling match. A real-world identity claim needs its own evidence.

## Next

Use [The identity ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder) to select the strongest usable scheme. Use [The IID registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry) to interpret the resulting value.

# The Intuition Identifier (IID)

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

An Intuition Identifier (IID) is a string of the form `int:<scheme>:<value>` that names an entity. An atom can carry that string in its data. The protocol derives a separate 32-byte atom ID from the entire payload. You can compare IIDs to check whether two records carry the same name, and compare atom IDs to check whether they address the same atom.

**Builds on:** [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms), [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids).

**Implemented by:** [iid-spec](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

## How it works

First decide **what you are identifying**. An ISRC names a particular recorded performance. A studio take and a live take can share a composition and a title while having different ISRCs. An ISWC names the composition. Picking the entity level determines which identifiers make sense. [IID spec §5.5](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/05-identity-ladders.md#55-abstraction-levels)

The scheme tells you how to turn a source value into its canonical spelling. Two importers following the same rule can produce identical text offline. A valid identifier tells you what the supplied value names. Checking whether a catalog attached that value to the right record requires evidence about the record. [IID spec §0.4](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/00-overview.md#04-the-core-claim-stated-precisely)

## The Intuition Identifier (IID) - Example

The [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) builds a bare recording anchor from the standalone ISRC fixture `US-RC1-76-07839`.

| Value | Fixture result | Where to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical IID | `int:isrc:USRC17607839` | Compare the identifier across catalogs. |
| Atom data | The exact UTF-8 bytes of `int:isrc:USRC17607839` | Reproduce this bare anchor. |
| Atom ID | `0xd3368a8190d3afd5fb05abd01db8141c09a77c3f290bb7a0ef2ffb2b5acab8d8` | Refer to this atom in a triple. |

Encoding the same IID inside a JSON object adds bytes. That representation has its own atom ID even though a reader can extract the same IID. [IID spec §0.5](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/00-overview.md#05-what-an-iid-is-not)

## Common mistakes

- Supplying the IID string when a triple builder expects a `bytes32` subject or object ID.
- Treating two recordings with matching titles as the same performance. Check the recording-level evidence before linking them.

## Next

- Read [Schemes and canonical form](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes) to compare source spellings and [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) to choose the stored bytes.
- See how [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications) select identity rules and how [Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing) handles raw input.
- Use [sameAs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as) to express a claim about two existing atoms.

# Concept map

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts

Choose a question to start with. To represent a recording and its artist, begin with atoms and triples. To decide whether a provider supplied enough evidence to display a title, follow the reading path to enrichment.

## How to read the map

Read each arrow from the prerequisite toward the concept that uses it. For example, start with atoms to understand term IDs, then learn how a triple connects existing terms. A subject, predicate, or object can itself be a triple. The branches show where you can pursue a different question without finishing every page.

```mermaid
graph BT
  atoms["Atoms"]
  triples["Triples"]
  deterministic_ids["Deterministic IDs"]
  vaults["Vaults"]
  bonding_curves["Bonding curves"]
  signals["Signals"]
  fees_and_rewards["Fees and rewards"]
  iid["IID"]
  iid_schemes["IID schemes"]
  representation_profiles["Representation profiles"]
  identity_ladder["Identity ladder"]
  classifications["Classifications"]
  schema_org["schema.org"]
  predicates["Predicates"]
  iid_registry["IID registry"]
  same_as["sameAs"]
  atom_parsing["Atom parsing"]
  atom_classification["Atom classification"]
  enrichment["Enrichment"]
  atom_runtime["Atom runtime"]
  protocol_writes["Protocol writes"]
  indexing_and_querying["Indexing and querying"]
  atoms --> triples
  atoms --> deterministic_ids
  triples --> deterministic_ids
  atoms --> vaults
  triples --> vaults
  vaults --> bonding_curves
  vaults --> signals
  bonding_curves --> signals
  vaults --> fees_and_rewards
  bonding_curves --> fees_and_rewards
  atoms --> iid
  deterministic_ids --> iid
  iid --> iid_schemes
  iid --> representation_profiles
  atoms --> representation_profiles
  iid_schemes --> identity_ladder
  atoms --> classifications
  iid --> classifications
  identity_ladder --> classifications
  classifications --> schema_org
  triples --> predicates
  classifications --> predicates
  iid_schemes --> iid_registry
  classifications --> iid_registry
  iid --> same_as
  triples --> same_as
  predicates --> same_as
  atoms --> atom_parsing
  iid --> atom_parsing
  atom_parsing --> atom_classification
  classifications --> atom_classification
  atom_classification --> enrichment
  iid_registry --> enrichment
  atom_classification --> atom_runtime
  enrichment --> atom_runtime
  deterministic_ids --> protocol_writes
  vaults --> protocol_writes
  representation_profiles --> protocol_writes
  classifications --> protocol_writes
  protocol_writes --> indexing_and_querying
  atom_runtime --> indexing_and_querying
```

The shortest reading path to enrichment covers 11 pages.

[Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms) → [Triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples) → [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids) → [IID](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid) → [IID schemes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes) → [Identity ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder) → [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications) → [IID registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry) → [Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing) → [Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification) → [Enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment).

## Read by tier

### Tier 1 · Protocol primitives

[Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms) represent entities as exact data bytes. [Triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples) express ordered relationships between terms. [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids) let a catalog derive the same identifiers from the same inputs before any write.

[Vaults, shares and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults) explain where deposits go. [Bonding curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves) explain what the next share costs. Continue to [Signals](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/signals) to interpret a position or [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards) to understand its economics.

### Tier 2 · Identity

[The Intuition Identifier](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid) names an entity independently of its atom representation. [Schemes and canonical form](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes) explain how to compare names. Use [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) to choose what bytes to publish and [The identity ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder) to choose among candidate identifiers.

### Tier 3 · Meaning

[Classifications and Creation Profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications) describe what a recording is and what its form should collect. [schema.org vocabulary](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/schema-org) supplies shared types and properties. [Predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates) turn a relationship such as “by artist” into an explicit graph edge when used in a triple.

[The IID registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry) connects identifier schemes to classification and provider plans. Use [sameAs and identity linking](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as) when two distinct atoms represent the same entity.

### Tier 4 · Processing

[Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing) recognizes the form of an input. [Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification) interprets it using plugins. [Enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment) collects provider evidence and extracts supported fields. [Atom runtime and pipelines](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime) brings these stages into an application with explicit resource limits and cleanup.

### Tier 5 · Data flow

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) separates planning, submission and receipt. [Indexing and querying](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/indexing-and-querying) follows the resulting chain events into a self-hosted Core node and its Query API. An off-chain insert can also put a recording into that node's graph.

# Indexing and querying

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/indexing-and-querying

Indexing makes chain events available to readers of a Core node you run. Its indexer records events, projections turn them into graph records, and workers can parse, classify, and enrich the atoms. V2 applications read the resulting graph through that node’s Query API. A receipt can arrive before the node has ingested and projected the corresponding atom event.

**Builds on:** [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes), [Atom runtime and pipelines](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime).

**Implemented by:** [Intuition Core](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## How it works

Fork and clone Intuition Core and build the pinned source. The default Compose stack serves the off-chain graph. To ingest chain events, configure the chain RPC, chain ID, MultiVault address and start block, then enable the `indexing` profile. That profile runs ingestion and projections. [Source setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core), [Compose services](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docker-compose.yml).

The indexer decodes events into the TimescaleDB event store. Projections record their progress in checkpoints as they populate read models and copy atoms and triples into the Postgres knowledge graph. Workers claim atom processing stages and persist outcomes there. The API reads from the knowledge graph, so an atom can be visible while enrichment is pending or has failed. [Architecture](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/architecture.md), [data model](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/data-model.md).

The node also accepts off-chain inserts. Under its default public-read policy, a writable key authorizes `POST /api/atoms` with an `input` string. A successful insert creates a node-local record. Registering the same bytes on-chain requires a separate protocol write and indexing its event. [Query API contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/openapi.yaml).

There is no V2 GraphQL endpoint yet; one is planned for Intuition Core. The V1 GraphQL API is documented in the [V1 docs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1/graphql-api/overview).

## Indexing and querying - Example

A catalog derives an atom ID for its chosen recording bytes. Keep that ID throughout the following checks.

| Observation | What the catalog knows |
| --- | --- |
| A wallet returns a transaction hash | It can track the submitted transaction on the chosen chain. |
| A successful receipt for the creation includes the atom event | The write executed. The catalog's node might still be behind that block. |
| `GET /api/atoms/{id}` returns the atom | The node can serve that record. Inspect `isOnchain` to distinguish an indexed chain record from an off-chain insert. |
| The atom has processing statuses | Read `parseStatus`, `classificationStatus`, and `enrichmentStatus` separately. Inspect available artifacts at `GET /api/atoms/{id}/artifacts` before displaying provider evidence. |

If the receipt is successful and the atom is absent, check the node's chain, MultiVault address, block range, and projection progress. Repeating the chain write would address none of these causes. [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## Common mistakes

- Assuming an off-chain insert will publish itself. The API response records what happened on that node. A chain submission requires separate authorization.
- Expecting semantic fields after enabling one flag. `API_ATOM_SEMANTIC_READS_ENABLED`, `WORKERS_IID_READ_ENABLED`, and `WORKERS_IID_RESOLUTION_ENABLED` each default to false. The API setting controls presentation. The worker settings control IID reads and provider resolution. Use the documented response fields and inspect the actual processing state. [Configuration](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/configuration.md), [worker defaults](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/services/workers/src/shared/config.ts).
- Using a seeded predicate's label to prepare a protocol triple. Verify the canonical predicate data and ID before constructing the triple. [Predicate registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates).

## Next

[Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) walks through building the source, selecting the indexing profile, and reading your own graph.

# Predicates

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0

A predicate names the relationship between a triple’s subject and object. In Intuition it is itself an atom. The predicate registry connects a stable lookup key and a human-readable label to the canonical atom data and its deterministic ID. A triple uses that ID in the middle position.

**Builds on:** [Triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples), [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications).

**Implemented by:** [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates).

## How it works

For a recording credit, the registry key is `byArtist` and the label is “by artist”. The predicate’s canonical data is a serialized schema.org `DefinedTerm` containing `@context`, `@type`, `name` and `description` in a fixed order. The exported predicate ID is the atom ID of those serialized bytes. [Predicate specification](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/generated/specs/byArtist.ts) · [Predicate serialization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/predicate-id.ts) · [Published subpath source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/standalone/byArtist.ts)

A UI can translate a display label and still use the registry key to select the same predicate. Serializing that translation into new atom data creates a different predicate ID.

## Predicates - Example

This local fixture computes the ordered claim “recording → by artist → artist”. The output includes the key, label, exact atom data and both IDs so you can inspect what goes into the claim.

```ts
import { calculateAtomId, calculateTripleId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import {
  byArtist,
  byArtistAtomData,
  byArtistId,
  byArtistSpec,
} from '@0xintuition/predicates/byArtist';

// Synthetic local fixture atoms; these strings claim no external identity.
const recordingId = calculateAtomId('example:recording');
const artistId = calculateAtomId('example:artist');
const byArtistTripleId = calculateTripleId(recordingId, byArtistId, artistId);
console.log({
  key: byArtistSpec.key,
  label: byArtist.name,
  data: byArtistAtomData,
  predicateId: byArtistId,
  tripleId: byArtistTripleId,
});
```

For the pinned predicate, `byArtistId` is `0x13d5d4ad6ae3a4e1b5043141b6ce4633c2df4646eaefc9e45eba899c45ce235b`. Switching the two endpoint IDs changes the claim. [Recording relationship metadata](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/generated/creation/music-recording.ts)

## Common mistakes

- Hashing the string “by artist” or `byArtist` to construct the predicate ID. Use the exported ID or compute it from the canonical predicate data.
- Reversing subject and object because the UI starts with the artist. The recording is the subject of `byArtist`.

## Next

Use [sameAs and identity linking](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as) to see how another registered predicate connects two representations.

# Protocol writes

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0

A protocol write changes on-chain state through a signed transaction. Building atom bytes or an action envelope can happen locally; reading a quote needs contract state; submission requires an authorized signer. A prepared request is not a transaction, a transaction hash is not a successful receipt, and a receipt does not prove a Core node has indexed the change.

**Builds on:** [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids), [Vaults](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults), [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications).

**Implemented by:** [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery), [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments), [cli](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/cli).

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant App
  participant SDK
  participant Wallet
  participant Chain
  participant Core
  App->>SDK: Exact bytes, IDs, receiver, amounts
  SDK->>Chain: Reads for quotes and readiness
  SDK-->>App: Plan and transaction requests
  App->>App: Human review and authorization
  App->>Wallet: Approved request
  Wallet->>Chain: Signed transaction
  Chain-->>App: Receipt or revert
  Chain->>Core: Events, when indexing is configured
  App->>Core: Query projected records
```

| Operation | Runtime boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Primitive builder, calldata encoder, client-free envelope | Local computation; envelope inputs include caller-supplied read context |
| SDK quote, readiness, or preparation action | May perform RPC reads; no submission merely because a plan is returned |
| Protocol write wrapper or `feeProxyExecutePlan` | Can simulate and submit using wallet clients |
| Receipt parsing | Confirms success or failure and filters expected contract events |
| Core query | Reads that node's projected state, which may lag chain confirmation |

A quote is a snapshot, not a reservation. Before signing, review the chain, deployment, calldata, value, receiver, required signer, minimum output, and ordered steps. Recheck stale state and deployment capabilities. [Contract artifacts](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility#contract-artifacts-and-deployments) describe an interface, not a guarantee that every deployment implements it.

FeeProxy plans can route creation and deposits and require different signers for approvals. `feeProxyExecutePlan` submits and waits for receipts; a later failure can leave earlier steps completed. Record those receipts and reread state before resuming. A refund helper can return `null` when nothing is claimable.

## Protocol writes - Example

This helper builds an ordinary descriptive atom and asks the SDK for a create-and-seed plan. **Calling it makes contract reads; it does not submit.** Its caller supplies a configured MultiVault, receiver, name, and amount in base units.

```ts
import { buildThing } from '@0xintuition/primitives';
import { multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm } from '@0xintuition/sdk/actions';
import type { WriteConfig } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import { stringToHex, type Address } from 'viem';

export async function prepareNamedAtom(
  config: WriteConfig,
  receiver: Address,
  name: string,
  assetsIn: bigint,
) {
  const result = buildThing({ name });
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  return multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm(config, {
    receiver,
    atomsToCreate: [
      {
        termId: result.value.id,
        data: stringToHex(result.value.data),
        assetsIn,
      },
    ],
    seedDeposits: [],
  });
}
```

The caller must handle an existing atom and current creation costs. The same name and serialized data produce the same ID; deriving it does not reserve it. This ordinary creation plan does not register companion URIs. Use `multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris` or a URI-aware FeeProxy preparation path when those entries must be registered, after reading live URI limits.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming a helper's name proves it submits: `multivaultCreateAndSeedTerm` returns a plan.
- Calling a write wrapper while intending only an offline preview.
- Treating a transaction hash as a receipt or a receipt as indexed visibility.
- Assuming a hook reset cancels a pending wallet request or transaction.
- Treating an off-chain Core API insert as on-chain registration.

## Next

[Build action plans and envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) for review. After confirmation, [Indexing and querying](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/indexing-and-querying) explains how the write becomes visible to readers who [query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Its default source stack requires explicit indexing configuration before it ingests chain events.

Sources: [Action-plan ownership](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/docs/action-plans.md), [MultiVault actions](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts), [FeeProxy execution](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/fee-proxy.ts).

# Representation profiles

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0

A representation profile describes the atom data that carries an IID. P0 stores the bare canonical identifier, P1 adds the evidence needed to interpret or re-derive it, and P2 adds descriptive fields. The IID names the entity; the atom ID identifies the exact stored bytes, so different representations of one IID can have different atom IDs.

**Builds on:** [The Intuition Identifier](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid), [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms).

**Implemented by:** [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives).

## How it works

The canonical rules are [IID spec §7.2](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#72-the-profiles), [IID spec §7.3](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#73-scheme-typing), and [IID spec §7.5](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#75-requirements).

| Profile | Identity payload | When to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 — anchor | Exact canonical IID text | Class A or B identifiers whose scheme is unambiguously typed |
| P1 — identity context | Type, IID, identity-recipe fields, and corroborating evidence | Required minimum for Class C or polymorphic identifiers |
| P2 — enriched | P1 plus descriptive data | Opt in when that description must be part of the atom |

Both P0 eligibility conditions must hold. A `gen1` identifier carries an entity type, but its Class C derivation still requires recipe evidence at P1. A plain name can be ambiguous; deterministic derivation cannot establish that two people with the same name are one person.

When deriving an IID from input fields, the pinned builder defaults to P0 if eligible and P1 otherwise. Requesting P0 for ineligible input returns errors on this path. Check the result’s `success` field before reading `value`. On success, `iid`, `scheme` and `class` can still be `null` when no identifier was derived. On the derived-IID path, explicit P1 and P2 serialize the same identified envelope. When you supply `candidateIid`, the builder ignores the requested profile and selects P0 for an eligible candidate or P1 for any other accepted candidate. [Builder source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/anchor.ts)

The packaged specification omits §7.8 on companion metadata. Both sources define weak `acct` handles. The package gives those handles a P1 floor, making them ineligible for bare P0 anchors while preserving their canonical bytes. It also accepts typed `wd` values and the additional `apple-podcasts`, `letterboxd` and `podcast-index` schemes. [Canonical account scheme](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/schemes/acct.md) · [Packaged amendments](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/spec/09-registry-governance.md#97-pre-publication-amendments)

### Keep companion metadata outside identity

[IID spec §7.8](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#78-the-atom-creation-model-data-and-companion-metadata) separates the identity payload from companion URI entries: leads for resolution, provenance, or richer descriptions. Identity validation and comparison must work without those entries.

For `buildIidAnchor`, changing only `contextUris` preserves `data`, `dataHex`, and `id`. A JSON-LD `@context` field **inside** the atom is different: changing it changes serialized bytes and can change the atom ID. The builder normalizes companion entries, but registering them still requires a URI-aware write; it does not fetch or upload them.

The specification's identity-canonical and display-canonical roles describe an equivalence architecture. They do not establish a cluster or election API in Core. Choosing a richer display source must not rewrite original atom IDs or move existing claims and positions.

## Representation profiles - Example

A name-derived person needs P1 evidence. This offline check confirms the default and the rejected bare-anchor request:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

const fields = { givenName: 'Ada', familyName: 'Lovelace' };
const contextual = buildIidAnchor('person', fields);
if (!contextual.success) throw new Error(contextual.errors.join('; '));
assert.equal(contextual.value.profile, 'p1');
assert.equal(contextual.value.class, 'C');

const forcedAnchor = buildIidAnchor('person', fields, { profile: 'p0' });
assert.equal(forcedAnchor.success, false);
```

This uses the package's fixture fields to demonstrate representation selection, not to verify a real person's identity. The [quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) separately proves that equivalent ISRC spellings and changed companion URIs preserve P0 bytes and IDs.

For a recording identified by title alone, the builder retains the title as recipe evidence. The artist credit is a descriptive field outside that recipe. Compare the returned profile labels with the bytes actually produced.

```ts
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

const values = { name: 'Example recording', byArtist: 'Example artist' };
const p1 = buildIidAnchor('music-recording', values, { profile: 'p1' });
const p2 = buildIidAnchor('music-recording', values, { profile: 'p2' });
if (!p1.success) throw new Error(p1.errors.join('; '));
if (!p2.success) throw new Error(p2.errors.join('; '));
console.log(p1.value.profile, p2.value.profile);
console.log(p1.value.data === p2.value.data, p1.value.id === p2.value.id);
```

The labels are `p1` and `p2`. Both comparisons return `true`, and neither payload contains the artist credit.

## Common mistakes

- Passing an IID where a protocol call expects a bytes32 term ID.
- Rebuilding an existing atom with a different profile and expecting its ID to stay unchanged.
- Treating companion `contextUris` as the JSON-LD `@context` inside atom data.
- Treating P2 selection as a provider fetch, or a valid IID as proof of a description.
- Requiring companion metadata to validate identity; missing context means unknown, not invalid.

## Next

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) uses the selected bytes in a transaction plan. Keep them unchanged through review and submission.

# sameAs and identity linking

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0

A `sameAs` triple asserts that two atoms refer to the same real-world entity. Each endpoint keeps its own atom ID, payload and history. The edge records a claim that others can evaluate. It takes evidence about the entity to decide whether to accept that claim.

**Builds on:** [The Intuition Identifier](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid), [Triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples), [Predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates).

**Implemented by:** [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives), [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates).

## How it works

First check that both atoms name the same thing at the same level. Two catalog entries for one specific recorded performance can qualify. An album containing the track, a different live performance, or an article reviewing it represents a different thing. [IID spec §8.1](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/08-equivalence.md#81-why-identifiers-are-not-enough)

A URL in a new atom’s `sameAs` data field is part of its serialized payload. To assert equivalence after two atoms already exist, use their original IDs as the subject and object of a separate triple with the registry’s `sameAs` predicate. The intended meaning is symmetric, but the triple ID is computed from ordered endpoints. [Predicate specification](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/generated/specs/sameAs.ts) · [Identity-linking example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/identity-linking.ts)

An application may group representations for display under its acceptance policy. The equivalence discussion in the spec describes that grouping as a projection over accepted claims. The original terms still carry their claims and positions. [IID spec §8.4](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/08-equivalence.md#84-merges-are-reversible)

## sameAs and identity linking - Example

Assume two entries in a local test catalog refer to the same recording. Their different reference URLs produce different atom IDs. Build the relationship and inspect its three ordered terms.

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildAtomData } from '@0xintuition/classifications';
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { sameAsId } from '@0xintuition/predicates/sameAs';
import { buildTriple } from '@0xintuition/primitives/triple';

// Both catalog entries describe the same recording in this local fixture.
const recording = { name: 'Example recording' };
const left = calculateAtomId(
  buildAtomData('music-recording', {
    ...recording,
    sameAs: ['https://example.org/catalog/a'],
  }),
);
const right = calculateAtomId(
  buildAtomData('music-recording', {
    ...recording,
    sameAs: ['https://example.org/catalog/b'],
  }),
);
assert.notEqual(left, right);

const claim = buildTriple(left, 'sameAs', right);
if (!claim.success) throw new Error(claim.errors.join('; '));
assert.equal(claim.value.subjectId, left);
assert.equal(claim.value.predicateId, sameAsId);
assert.equal(claim.value.objectId, right);
```

This computes a triple blueprint in memory. Neither URL is fetched, and a successful build only checks how the claim is constructed.

## Common mistakes

- Using `sameAs` for a cover, a remix or a review just because it mentions the track. Check the recording-level evidence.
- Overwriting one atom ID with the other when accepting a claim. Record or display the link so consumers can retain provenance and revisit the decision.
- Expecting the claim to prove its own truth, merge balances or submit a transaction.

## Next

Follow the [music catalog example](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) to compare recording, artist and album terms and their directed claims.

# schema.org vocabulary

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/schema-org

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0

The schema.org vocabulary gives applications a shared meaning for names such as `MusicRecording`, `byArtist` and `name`. Intuition packages use a pinned copy so two applications using the same release can look up the same definitions offline. A classification chooses which of those properties its Creation Profile exposes.

**Builds on:** [Classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications).

**Implemented by:** [schema-org](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org).

## How it works

The package is generated from the vendored schema.org V30.0 vocabulary. A type record stores the properties declared directly on that type and its parent chain. `getType` reads the type record. `getPropertiesFor` resolves inherited properties and records which type each one comes from. [Vocabulary package](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/schema-org/README.md)

A property’s range lists the kinds of values the vocabulary describes. A form can present a simpler input. For instance, schema.org describes `byArtist` in terms of a person or music group, while the recording Creation Profile accepts an artist credit as text. [Generated recording type](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/schema-org/src/generated/types/MusicRecording.ts) · [Recording Creation Profile](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/generated/creation/music-recording.ts)

## schema.org vocabulary - Example

Suppose a form offers a track title and an ISRC. The two labels reach the vocabulary by different paths.

| Form field | Schema property | Where it is declared | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | `Thing`, inherited by `MusicRecording` | `Text` |
| `isrc` | `isrcCode` | `MusicRecording` | `Text` |
| `byArtist` | `byArtist` | `MusicRecording` | `MusicGroup` or `Person` |

Reading only the recording’s direct properties would miss the inherited title field. Looking up the form key `isrc` literally would miss the schema property `isrcCode`. The profile records the mapping.

## Common mistakes

- Interpreting a missing property on the direct type record as missing from the vocabulary. Check inherited properties.
- Taking a range such as `Person` as evidence that a particular person performed a recording. That fact requires its own evidence.

## Next

Explore the [schema.org package reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org) for the lookup functions and generated type modules.

# Signals

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/signals

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0

A deposit makes a signal observable by putting assets behind a particular term. A position on an atom can draw attention to an entity. A position on a triple or its counter-triple can back one side of a specific claim. Its economic weight depends on the amount and the vault. Establishing the claim itself takes evidence.

**Builds on:** [Vaults, shares and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults), [Bonding curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves).

**Implemented by:** [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk), [react](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/react).

## How it works

Choose what the deposit refers to. Depositing on Mira’s artist atom backs that representation of Mira. Depositing on the credit “Night Ferry, by artist, Mira” backs a particular relationship. The counter-side is another term with its own vault. In the pinned MultiVault, a receiver with shares on one side cannot deposit on the other side of that triple **on the same curve**. [Deposit checks](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol)

To interpret a signal, keep the side, curve, deployment and observation block. A deposit records an action at a point in time. A current position records the shares still held after subsequent deposits and redemptions. The SDK exposes `multivaultGetUserPositionSnapshot` for an account, term and curve. In React, `usePosition` reads shares and estimates their asset value. [SDK position reads](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/multivault.ts) · [React position reads](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/hooks/use-position.ts)

## Signals - Example

At one block on one curve, suppose an app finds positions on the recording credit with an estimated gross asset value of 90 units on the positive side and 30 on the counter-side. Of these 120 units, 75% back the positive side. Label that figure **share of observed asset value backing the credit** and name the curve and block.

The same figures could arise from one large positive position or several smaller ones. They tell you neither the number of independent people who agree nor the probability that Mira performed the recording. To evaluate the credit, inspect the source for that claim, such as the cited liner notes.

## Common mistakes

- **Counting deposits as people.** An account can deposit repeatedly or redeem later. A single person can also control multiple accounts.
- **Combining raw shares across curves or sides.** Convert the positions using their own vaults and identify the measure you summed.
- **Mistaking an empty counter-side for verification.** Zero observed opposition supplies no evidence about who played on a recording.

## Next

To show a holder the position behind a signal, see the [React package](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/react). To read indexed terms and relationships, see [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

# Triples, counter-triples and nested triples

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

A triple expresses a claim in three ordered parts. The **subject** is what the claim concerns, the **predicate** names the relationship, and the **object** is what stands on the other side of that relationship. Each part is a term ID. The triple gets an ID of its own, so a second claim can cite the first one.

**Builds on:** [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms).

**Implemented by:** [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol).

## How it works

Read the triple from left to right. In the fictional credit “Night Ferry, by artist, Mira,” the recording is the subject, “by artist” is the predicate, and Mira is the object. The registry key `byArtist` selects the relationship in application code. Its display name is `by artist`. The predicate atom's payload is a serialized definition with that name and a description. Its atom ID occupies the middle slot. [Predicate definition](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/generated/specs/byArtist.ts) · [Predicate atom data and ID](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/standalone/byArtist.ts)

A positive triple identifies that ordered claim. Its counter-triple gives participants a separate term for opposition to **the same claim**. MultiVault stores the same three components on both sides. Swapping the recording and the artist instead asserts that Mira is a work by Night Ferry. That is a different claim with its own positive and counter sides.

## Triples, counter-triples and nested triples - Example

Suppose the liner notes support the credit. Attach the notes to the precise credit they document.

| Term | Subject | Predicate | Object |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Credit | Night Ferry recording atom | by artist | Mira artist atom |
| Source for the credit | **Credit triple ID** | has source | Liner notes atom |

The second row is a nested triple. Follow its subject ID to inspect the precise claim the notes support. The predicate in each row stands for a predicate atom ID. “Credit” is just a local name for the first row's result.

To create the second row on-chain, its three terms must already exist on that MultiVault when the row is processed. The creation check accepts an existing atom or registered triple in each slot, including a registered counter-triple. The contract also checks for a duplicate triple. Computing an inner triple's ID locally supplies a reference, while creating it makes the reference usable on that deployment. [Term existence and triple creation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol) · [Source predicate](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/generated/specs/hasSource.ts)

## Common mistakes

- **Substituting a label for its ID.** Hashing the bare text “by artist” omits the registry definition.
- **Reversing a claim to dispute it.** Use the counter ID derived from the original triple.
- **Attaching evidence to the wrong subject.** A source attached to the recording describes the recording. A source attached to the credit can support that particular attribution.

## Next

- [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids) derives the ID of each side. [Vaults](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults) explains where their positions live.
- [Predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates) covers the registry. [sameAs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as) uses a predicate to link two representations of an entity.

# Vaults, shares and positions

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

A vault holds assets against a particular term under a particular bonding curve. Depositing assets gives the receiver shares in that vault. A position is the number of those shares an account holds. To locate one, identify the deployment, term, curve and account.

**Builds on:** [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms), [Triples, counter-triples and nested triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples).

**Implemented by:** [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk).

## How it works

An atom and a triple are both **terms**. Each term has a default-curve vault at creation. MultiVault keeps separate accounting for each pair of term ID and curve ID. An eligible first deposit can initialize another vault on a registered non-default curve. For a triple, the creation path also initializes the counter-side on the same curve. [Vault initialization and accounting](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol)

**Assets** are amounts of the network’s native token, measured in base units (wei). **Shares** are units of a particular vault. Depositing native assets mints shares to a receiver. Redeeming burns shares and pays native assets after applicable fees. An account can therefore keep the same share balance while the estimated asset value of that balance changes.

The contract's `getVault` returns total assets and total shares for one term and curve. Its `getShares` additionally takes the account. `previewDeposit` estimates shares and assets after fees for a proposed deposit. The minimum output on a reviewed deposit request is denominated in shares, while the minimum on a redemption is denominated in assets. [MultiVault reads and writes](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVault.sol)

## Vaults, shares and positions - Example

For the same recording on one deployment, suppose two initialized linear vaults have the following balances at one block. All amounts are integer base units.

| Curve | Total assets | Total shares | Mira’s shares | Gross asset value of Mira’s shares |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A | 120 | 100 | 10 | 12 |
| B | 200 | 100 | 10 | 20 |

On curve A, 10 shares represent `10 × 120 / 100 = 12` asset units before fees. Curve B has its own ratio and yields 20. Adding the two share counts loses the price information. To estimate the combined gross value, convert each position in its own vault first.

## Common mistakes

- **Reading the sender's balance when someone else received the shares.** Match the receiver, term and curve in the deposit event.
- **Displaying a share count as native currency.** A conversion gives a gross estimate. A payout also depends on fees, rounding, and state at execution.
- **Expecting every curve to have a funded vault.** Term existence and the balances on a selected curve answer different questions.

## Next

- [Bonding curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves) explains conversion and rounding. [Signals](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/signals) explains what the position says about a claim.
- [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards) follows the economic flows. [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) traces the steps from a quote to a receipt.

# Write a classification plugin

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0

Recognize a deliberate input pattern and emit a canonical classification through an explicitly registered plugin.

## Before you start

Read [atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification) for the data a classifier receives and returns. Use Node 22.18 or newer and install the public package:

```sh
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/atom-classification@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

A classifier decides whether it recognizes input; a resolver produces canonical candidates. This example recognizes an explicit `idea:` prefix offline. It does not infer that arbitrary prose names a unique entity, mint an IID, derive an atom ID, or persist a graph record.

## Steps

### 1. Declare the plugin and register its dependencies

A manifest declares identity, version, compatible engine range, runtime, capabilities, permissions, dependencies, provided features, and priority. Lower priorities run earlier. `type-profiles` supplies the type registry used by this resolver; the emitted `DefinedTerm` type must be registered.

```ts
import {
  createClientEngine,
  createTypeProfilesPlugin,
  validatePluginManifest,
  type AtomClassificationPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-classification';

export const ideaPlugin: AtomClassificationPlugin = {
  manifest: {
    id: 'example-idea',
    version: '1.0.0',
    engineRange: '^0.1.0',
    runtime: 'universal',
    priority: 30,
    capabilities: ['classifier:text:idea', 'resolver:lexical:defined-term'],
    permissions: [],
    dependsOn: ['type-profiles'],
    provides: ['example:idea'],
  },
  classifiers: [
    {
      id: 'idea-classifier',
      classify(input) {
        const name = input.startsWith('idea:') ? input.slice(5).trim() : '';
        return name
          ? {
              type: 'text',
              domain: 'lexical',
              subtype: 'idea',
              confidence: 1,
              meta: { name },
            }
          : null;
      },
    },
  ],
  resolvers: [
    {
      id: 'idea-resolver',
      executionMode: 'deterministic',
      canResolve: (classification) =>
        classification.domain === 'lexical' &&
        classification.subtype === 'idea',
      resolve: ({ request }) => ({
        classifications: [
          {
            type: 'DefinedTerm',
            data: {
              '@context': 'https://schema.org/',
              '@type': 'DefinedTerm',
              name: request.input.slice(5).trim(),
            },
          },
        ],
      }),
    },
  ],
};
validatePluginManifest(ideaPlugin.manifest);
const engine = createClientEngine({
  plugins: [createTypeProfilesPlugin(), ideaPlugin],
});
const input = 'idea: semantic grounding';
if (Buffer.byteLength(input, 'utf8') > 4_096)
  throw new Error('Input too large');
export const result = await engine.classify({
  input,
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'docs-plugin',
});
console.log(result.resolved?.publishable);
```

### 2. Keep matching deterministic and output canonical

Return `null` for unrelated input. Set the resolver's `executionMode: 'deterministic'` for this offline client flow: an omitted mode defaults to server enrichment and the client-only policy would skip that resolver. Prefer resolver `classifications` containing `type`, `data`, and optional metadata; the engine supplies missing plugin, provider, timestamp, and confidence metadata. `resolved.publishable` is the identity-oriented projection, while `resolved.classifications` may contain richer detail. Neither is proof of external truth.

The compatibility `atoms` projection still exists in the pinned implementation. If a resolver supplies both forms, the engine checks parity. Avoid introducing new dependencies on legacy-only fields. Declare permissions for capabilities you use; client runtimes cannot execute AI-capable plugins. Keep input byte and collection limits at the host boundary before parsing.

### 3. Test with fixed inputs

Run the complete [plugin helper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/blob/d137b0adacbfb9fda3b0d07d94e695ca4e7abc03/examples/v2/music-catalog/src/classification-plugin.ts) with `node`. Verify that the recognized input produces a `DefinedTerm` with name `semantic grounding`, unrelated input makes the classifier return `null`, and empty `idea:` input is rejected by the classifier. Compare semantic output across repeated runs; default timestamp metadata is time-dependent, so it is not part of a deterministic equality assertion.

Validate the manifest, test missing dependencies, and verify runtime restrictions before registering in a service. Test canonical/legacy parity only if you intentionally emit both forms.

### 4. Register at the host's composition boundary

The snippet passes an explicit plugin set to `createClientEngine`; registration is complete for that engine only. Adding a file to a repository does not install it into other engines.

In a fork of Core, inspect [the service runtime wrapper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/services/atom-services/src/service/runtime.ts). It calls the public package's `createAtomServicesProcessingRuntime`. That package accepts `pluginOverrides.classification`; the pinned Core wrapper's local option type does not expose that override. A fork owner must explicitly wire the chosen plugin set into the wrapper's runtime construction, preserve required built-ins, and rebuild the affected services.

The classification worker also reaches that runtime wrapper through [its engine setup](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/services/workers/src/kg/atom-classification/index.ts). Review both call paths and deploy the rebuilt service and worker processes that should use the plugin. There is no documented directory loader, environment-variable plugin installer, or automatic registration across all running processes. The source setup workflow is [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## Check the result

The offline helper validates the manifest and prints a publishable `DefinedTerm` envelope. This proves the local engine contract; Core registration and service execution require the fork's explicit source change and tests.

## Related

[Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) and [atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification).

Sources: [plugin authoring contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-classification/docs/plugin-authoring.md), [external plugin example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/atom-classification-plugin/src/index.ts), [runtime override contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/src/consumers.ts), and [Core classification guide](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/writing-a-classification-plugin.md).

# Schema-backed atom creation form

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/atom-creation-form

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0

**Time:** 15 minutes · **Steps:** 3

## What you'll build

Build a recording form with a title, artist, album, recording code, and reference URLs. Enter the synthetic title **Paper Moon Demo** and ISRC `US-RC1-26-00001` to preview the exact atom data. Then change the title and remove the recording code to see which edits change the atom ID.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 22.21.0. From the documentation repository root at the revision in **Full source**, install the example workspace once. npm needs registry access for installation. The runner uses only local data.

```sh
cd examples/v2
npm ci --ignore-scripts
```

The React component is optional for the offline run. To integrate it, use a React 19 client application with a TSX build step. See [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) and [representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles).

## Steps

### 1. Generate the controls from the recording profile

In `form-model.ts`, the profile defines the field keys, labels, types, placeholders, and required flags. Track Name is required. Artist, Album, ISRC, and Canonical References are optional.

```ts
import {
  validateClassificationValues,
  type ClassificationValidationIssue,
  type ClassificationValueMap,
} from '@0xintuition/classifications';
import { musicRecordingCreationProfile } from '@0xintuition/classifications/creation/music-recording';
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

export const { fields, classification } = musicRecordingCreationProfile;
type FieldKey = (typeof fields)[number]['key'];
export type RecordingDraft = Partial<Record<FieldKey, string>>;
export const maxFieldLength = 512;
```

Inside the field loop in `creation-form.tsx`, each label points to a unique control. References use a multiline input. Editing any field clears the previous preview so an old ID cannot appear beside a new draft.

```tsx
        const id = prefix + field.key;
        const error = issues.find((issue) => issue.field === field.key);
        const props = {
          id,
          value: draft[field.key] ?? '',
          required: field.required,
          placeholder: field.placeholder,
          maxLength: maxFieldLength,
          'aria-invalid': Boolean(error),
          'aria-describedby': error ? id + '-error' : undefined,
          style: {
            width: '100%',
            boxSizing: 'border-box' as const,
            font: 'inherit',
          },
          onChange: (
            event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement>,
          ) => {
            setDraft({ ...draft, [field.key]: event.currentTarget.value });
            setResult(undefined);
          },
        };
        const control = (
          <div key={field.key} style={{ marginBlockEnd: '1rem' }}>
            <label htmlFor={id}>
              {field.label} ({field.required ? 'required' : 'optional'})
              {field.fieldType === 'string[]' && ' — one web URL per line'}
            </label>
            {field.fieldType === 'string[]' ? (
              <textarea {...props} />
            ) : (
              <input type="text" {...props} />
            )}
            {error && <div id={id + '-error'}>{error.message}</div>}
          </div>
        );
```

### 2. Validate the draft and check the resulting bytes

The form caps each control at 512 characters and accepts up to four HTTP or HTTPS references. These limits belong to this example. Trim empty entries and split the reference list before calling the classification validator. For this form, a supplied ISRC must produce an ISRC anchor.

```ts
export function previewRecording(draft: RecordingDraft) {
  const values: ClassificationValueMap = {};
  const limits: ClassificationValidationIssue[] = [];
  for (const field of fields) {
    const raw = draft[field.key] ?? '';
    if (raw.length > maxFieldLength) {
      limits.push({
        field: field.key,
        message: 'Use 512 characters or fewer.',
      });
      continue;
    }
    if (!raw.trim()) continue;
    if (field.fieldType === 'string[]') {
      const lines = raw
        .split('\n')
        .map((line) => line.trim())
        .filter(Boolean);
      if (lines.length > 4 || !lines.every(isWebUrl)) {
        limits.push({
          field: field.key,
          message: 'Enter up to four web URLs, one per line.',
        });
      }
      values[field.key] = lines;
    } else {
      values[field.key] = raw.trim();
    }
  }
  const issues = [
    ...limits,
    ...validateClassificationValues(classification.slug, values),
  ];
  if (issues.length) return { ok: false as const, issues };

  const result = buildIidAnchor(classification.slug, values);
  if (!result.success) return failure(result.errors.join(' '));
  const anchor = result.value;
  if (values.isrc && !anchor.iid?.startsWith('int:isrc:')) {
    return failure('Check the recording code or leave it empty.', 'isrc');
  }
  if (calculateAtomId(anchor.dataHex) !== anchor.id) {
    return failure('The anchor ID does not match its bytes.');
  }
  return { ok: true as const, anchor };
}
```

The P0 preview hashes the bytes of the bare recording IID. Removing the ISRC selects a different representation for the title-only draft. A missing required title returns a field issue before the builder runs, so there is no preview ID.

### 3. Mount the form in a client application

Copy `creation-form.tsx` and `form-model.ts` together into your React app. Use the React, React DOM, and Intuition dependency versions from the example workspace. In the client entrypoint, import the named `mountCreationForm` export from `./creation-form.tsx` and call it with an empty DOM element after that element exists. Keep its returned cleanup function for when the host removes the form.

```tsx
export function mountCreationForm(container: HTMLElement) {
  const root = createRoot(container);
  root.render(<CreationForm />);
  return () => root.unmount();
}
```
