Select **Preview recording** with an empty title to see the inline error. Enter the title and recording code above and preview again to see the identifier, profile, data, and atom ID. The Node runner below exercises the same model directly. The component itself uses the host’s TSX compiler.

## Run it

From `examples/v2`, run the TypeScript entrypoint.

```sh
node atom-creation-form/src/run-form.ts
```

```text
p0 int:isrc:USRC12600001 0xfdbf117d9e9df5675c5b4f75747598424fc9beb2d2a50e20408f4cd4dfb3d4ed
Title edit keeps ID: true
Without ISRC: p1 0x3d892ed7c6b2aafc2dcd3400f013d0de97e4d773b4ba15ad402dd9b67205a211
Missing required field "name".
```

## Full source

[Recording form, preview model, and offline runner](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/3f47445235983fa93bf22d1d06f0584c6bac84fa/examples/v2/atom-creation-form). The pinned package example shows how to map [Creation Profile fields](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/generated-ui-model.ts) into [React controls](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/GeneratedUiPage.tsx). The [classification validator](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/atom-data.ts), [anchor builder](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/anchor.ts), and [atom ID calculation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/atom-id.ts) define the preview behavior.

## Next steps

Use [Creation Profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles) to choose the fields for another type. To model an artist as a separate atom and connect it to the recording, build the [predicate picker](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/predicate-picker).

# Read the graph from Core's Query API

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/core-query-api

**Time:** 15 minutes · **Steps:** 3

## What you'll build

A Node CLI that reads one page of atoms, one page of triples and the predicate catalog from your own Core node. It prints the number of rows returned and the first record from each collection. Those records expose the atom's processing status, the three terms of a directed claim, and the predicate's human-readable label.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.21.0 and [the pinned example dependencies](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). Fork and build Core at `a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420` using [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Run the CLI on the host with the API at `http://localhost:3000` and the default `public-read` policy. An empty local database is enough to test the client. To read on-chain terms, enable indexing for your deployment and allow projections to catch up. [Pinned Core setup](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/run-your-own-node.md).

## Steps

### 1. Get the complete client

Run these commands in a new directory. The docs checkout contains the client, its CLI and offline tests. Keep the terminal at the docs repository root for the remaining commands.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs.git
cd intuition-docs
git switch --detach bb420395aff3432f1f5da08cb76ac75a99945bff
npm ci --prefix examples/v2 --ignore-scripts
```

### 2. Identify the fields your application needs

Atom rows carry the on-chain flag and parse status. Triple rows name the subject, predicate and object in that order. A catalog row supplies a string slug and label plus a description that can be `null`. The two paginated endpoints report the number of rows in this response. The predicate endpoint returns a single `data` array. [Response schemas](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/openapi.yaml).

```ts
type Atom = { id: string; isOnchain: boolean; parseStatus: string };
type Triple = {
  id: string;
  subjectId: string;
  predicateId: string;
  objectId: string;
};
type Predicate = {
  id: string;
  slug: string;
  label: string;
  description: string | null;
};
type Page<T> = {
  data: T[];
  pagination: { limit: number; offset: number; count: number };
};
```

### 3. Request the three collections

`readGraph` uses a shared five-second deadline and requests ten atoms and ten triples at offset zero. Each response passes through an HTTP status check and a bounded JSON reader. The decoders check the fields in the types above, the requested pagination, and the number of rows returned. The client caps each body at 1 MiB and each predicate catalog at 2,048 rows. A schema mismatch or oversized response fails the CLI.

```ts
export async function readGraph() {
  const options: RequestInit = {
    method: 'GET',
    redirect: 'error',
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000),
  };
  const atoms = page(
    await readJson(
      fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/atoms?limit=10&offset=0', options),
    ),
    atom,
  );
  const triples = page(
    await readJson(
      fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/triples?limit=10&offset=0', options),
    ),
    triple,
  );
  const catalog = record(
    await readJson(fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/predicates', options)),
  );
  const predicates = rows(catalog.data, 2048, predicate);
  return { atoms, triples, predicates };
}
```

Atom and triple IDs can connect rows across requests. These reads happen separately, so concurrent indexing can update the graph between calls. When loading more rows, apply `offset` only to atoms and triples. Core also supports the triple filters `subject_id`, `predicate_id` and `object_id`. [Core API reference](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/api-reference.md).

## Run it

With your node running, execute the CLI from the docs checkout.

```sh
node examples/v2/core-query-api/src/run-query.ts
```

The CLI prints `Atoms on this page`, `Triples on this page` and `Predicates returned`, followed by JSON with sample records. If the graph has no atoms or triples, their counts are zero and their first records are `null`. A seeded predicate catalog can still contain rows. An HTTP 401 indicates that this node requires authorization. A connection error or timeout calls for checking the Core host port, API health and logs.

You can exercise the same decoders offline. These tests supply synthetic HTTP responses for successful, empty, malformed, oversized and unauthorized results, and simulate an expired deadline.

```sh
node --test examples/v2/core-query-api/src/query-client.test.ts
```

## Full source

The [complete Core query project](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/bb420395aff3432f1f5da08cb76ac75a99945bff/examples/v2/core-query-api) includes `query-client.ts`, `run-query.ts` and their response fixtures. The [pinned handler implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/services/api/src/app.ts) shows how Core builds the list envelopes.

## Next steps

[Build a local indexed graph](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/test-locally) and run the client again. [Triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples) explains how to interpret the three term IDs in each claim.

# sameAs identity linking

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/identity-linking

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

**Time:** 15 minutes · **Steps:** 3

## What you'll build

Review three candidates for an archived recording. One carries the same recording identifier, one is a review article, and one has only a matching title. The result is an offline plan containing a directed `sameAs` triple for the approved pair and a reason for each skipped candidate.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 22.21.0. From the documentation repository root at the revision in **Full source**, install the example workspace once. npm needs registry access for installation. The runner uses only local data.

```sh
cd examples/v2
npm ci --ignore-scripts
```

Read [sameAs and identity linking](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as) for the meaning of the claim. See [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) for the pinned packages. All catalog evidence below is synthetic.

## Steps

### 1. Preserve the historical atom bytes

The archive contains an exact UTF-8 JSON string with a reference URL in its `sameAs` property. The newer recording anchor contains a bare IID. The fixtures call `stringToHex` on each original text string. Parsing and serializing the JSON again could change the bytes used to identify that atom. UTF-8 text such as `0x6162` encodes as `0x307836313632`. If your catalog already stores binary bytes in hex, supply them directly. The two bytes `0x6162` identify a different atom.

```ts
import { stringToHex } from 'viem';

const recordingIid = 'int:isrc:USRC12600001';
export const archive = {
  level: 'recording' as const,
  atomData: stringToHex(
    '{"name":"Paper Moon Demo","sameAs":["https://example.org/recordings/17"]}',
  ),
  recordingIid,
};

export const candidates = {
  anchor: {
    level: 'recording',
    atomData: stringToHex(recordingIid),
    recordingIid,
  },
  review: {
    level: 'article',
    atomData: stringToHex('Review of Paper Moon Demo'),
    recordingIid,
  },
  namesake: {
    level: 'recording',
    atomData: stringToHex('{"name":"Paper Moon Demo"}'),
  },
} as const;
```

The URL inside the JSON is part of the archived payload. A graph edge requires a separate predicate atom and two term IDs. Keep the recording-level evidence beside the original data while reviewing candidates.

### 2. Record each decision and its evidence

The fixture editor compared the two catalog records and confirmed the same take and recording code. The critic’s article cites the recording but describes a different entity. The namesake has no recording identifier to distinguish it from a different take.

```ts
  const recording = {
    candidate: 'anchor' as const,
    evidence:
      'The two catalog records credit the same take and list the same recording code.',
  };
  const accepted = reviewLink({ ...recording, approved: true });
  const waiting = reviewLink({ ...recording, approved: false });
  const article = reviewLink({
    candidate: 'review',
    approved: false,
    evidence: 'The critic cites the recording in a review.',
  });
  const namesake = reviewLink({
    candidate: 'namesake',
    approved: false,
    evidence: 'Only the title matches.',
  });
```

The second call for the same recording pair exercises the pending case. A matching identifier supplies evidence. The reviewer supplies approval. This example assigns no confidence score.

### 3. Plan the ordered claim

The review wrapper requires an evidence note and passes the archived bytes, candidate, and explicit decision to `planLink`.

```ts
type Decision = {
  candidate: keyof typeof candidates;
  approved: boolean;
  evidence: string;
};

export function reviewLink({ candidate, approved, evidence }: Decision) {
  if (!evidence.trim())
    return { candidate, reason: 'Record the evidence for review.' };
  const result = planLink(archive, candidates[candidate], approved);
  return { candidate, evidence, ...result };
}
```

The [link planner](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/link-identities) checks the entity level, inspects both IIDs, and requires matching canonical ISRC identifiers for this fixture. After approval it derives each atom ID from the original payload, rejects identical term IDs, and builds the ordered `sameAs` triple. Both original atoms keep their IDs and bytes. This local plan makes no changes to either record and submits no transaction.

## Run it

From `examples/v2`, run the TypeScript entrypoint.

```sh
node identity-linking/src/run-linking.ts
```

```text
Subject 0x70e43f5beab9b630229717d40da0874927cd3cf2a4d9f34979e4e88abb60b4ab
sameAs 0x1908b7994ca437c84c67a4799ae710355591790a726bf5890277f3aa70828c0a
Object 0xfdbf117d9e9df5675c5b4f75747598424fc9beb2d2a50e20408f4cd4dfb3d4ed
Triple 0xc40d319e82c15a049aa3688e2a4cc0fbc51441f05311ad403beaba3382496ef1
anchor Awaiting review
review Different entity level
namesake Missing recording identifier
```

The subject is the archived JSON atom. The object is the bare recording IID atom. The middle ID belongs to the registry’s `sameAs` predicate. The fourth ID identifies the proposed edge itself.

## Full source

[Review fixtures, link planner, and runner](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/84242e8f4399ac758c942e85b343e0512245a6cf/examples/v2/identity-linking). The [canonical equivalence discussion](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/08-equivalence.md) describes the role of reviewed claims. Compare the package’s [identity example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/identity-linking.ts), [review interface](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/IdentityLinkingPage.tsx), [IID inspection](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/src/parse.ts), and [triple builder](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/triple.ts).

## Next steps

Use [Derive IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/derive-ids) to trace a single recording from identifier to term ID, or follow the [music catalog tutorial](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) to model artist and album relationships.

# What you can build

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples

The packages supply shared identities and graph modeling tools. Core supplies storage, processing workers, and queries. Protocol contracts add registration and economic positions. Your application combines these with its own rules for evidence, permissions, and ranking.

- [Create an atom from a schema](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/atom-creation-form) — Generate a form from a Creation Profile.
- [Choose a predicate](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/predicate-picker) — Find a relationship that fits the claim you want to make.
- [Link two identities](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/identity-linking) — Keep each identity distinct while recording a sameAs claim.
- [Read and create an atom in React](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/react-app) — Review a wallet call and read back its confirmed atom.
- [Query your Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/core-query-api) — Retrieve indexed graph records from your own node.
- [Build a music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) — Connect a recording, artist and album with explicit triples.

## Apply the pattern

| Application | Shared building blocks | Decisions your application owns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Media discovery and curation | Identity ladders, Creation Profiles, explicit triples | Duplicate review, ranking, moderation |
| Research and evidence | Stable anchors, shared predicates, provenance | Evidence quality, citations, access control |
| Portable collections | Item IDs and containment relationships | Membership order, permissions, deletion semantics |
| Contextual reputation | Attributed claims and vault positions | Context, scoring, resistance to manipulation |
| Agent-assisted graph building | Offline builders and reviewed action plans | Scope, budget, provenance, authorization |
| Enrichment services | Parser, classifier, provider runtime | Provider terms, credentials, retries, cache policy |

When adapting the music catalog, decide which entity each record identifies, which bytes represent it, and which directed relationship you are asserting. Your application supplies the evidence policy for claims and decides how a position contributes to reputation.

For a smaller starting point, run the [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart). For operational boundaries, read [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits).

Source: [What you can build with the packages](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#what-you-can-build).

# Build a music catalog

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0

**Time:** 15 minutes · **Steps:** 4

## What you'll build

Build three local entity anchors and two directed claims: a recording **byArtist** a performing identity, and a recording **inAlbum** an album release-group. Inspect their exact bytes, IIDs, profiles, and atom IDs before storing anything.

“One More Time”, “Daft Punk”, “Discovery”, and the accompanying identifiers are **synthetic test fixtures** adapted from package tests, not verified real-world records. The separate golden ISRC quickstart does not identify this synthetic recording. A recording is not its composition or remix, a performing identity is not necessarily a legal person, and a release-group is not one specific release edition.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.18 or newer. No wallet, RPC, API key, or running Core node is needed for the offline catalog. See [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) for ESM and peer setup.

## Steps

### 1. Set up the project

```sh
mkdir music-catalog
cd music-catalog
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0 @0xintuition/ids@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

### 2. Choose representations and construct explicit edges

Save the complete example as `catalog.ts`:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { inspectIntuitionId } from '@0xintuition/iid';
import { classificationForIid } from '@0xintuition/iid-registry';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';
import { getPredicateInfo } from '@0xintuition/primitives/predicate';
import { buildTriple } from '@0xintuition/primitives/triple';
import type { BuildResult } from '@0xintuition/primitives';

function unwrap<T>(result: BuildResult<T>): T {
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  return result.value;
}

// Synthetic test identifiers, not verified MusicBrainz records.
const recordingValues = {
  name: 'One More Time',
  sameAs: [
    'https://musicbrainz.org/recording/b1a9c0e9-d987-4042-ae91-78d6a3267d69',
  ],
};
const recording = unwrap(buildIidAnchor('music-recording', recordingValues));
const artist = unwrap(buildIidAnchor('music-group', { name: 'Daft Punk' }));
const album = unwrap(
  buildIidAnchor('music-album', {
    name: 'Discovery',
    sameAs: [
      'https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/41b3f6ea-f7b6-3a6c-9a0a-3f8d6e2a1b55',
    ],
  }),
);
const byArtist = getPredicateInfo('byArtist');
const inAlbum = getPredicateInfo('inAlbum');
assert.ok(byArtist && inAlbum);

const claims = [
  unwrap(buildTriple(recording.id, byArtist.key, artist.id)),
  unwrap(buildTriple(recording.id, inAlbum.key, album.id)),
];
assert.equal(claims[0].predicateId, byArtist.id);
assert.equal(calculateAtomId(byArtist.atomData), byArtist.id);
assert.notEqual(
  unwrap(buildTriple(artist.id, byArtist.key, recording.id)).id,
  claims[0].id,
);

// Companion context travels alongside the atom; it is not atom data.
const withContext = unwrap(
  buildIidAnchor('music-recording', recordingValues, {
    contextUris: ['https://example.org/catalog/recording.json'],
  }),
);
assert.equal(withContext.id, recording.id);
assert.equal(withContext.data, recording.data);
const changedJson = artist.data.replace(
  'https://schema.org/',
  'https://schema.org',
);
assert.notEqual(calculateAtomId(changedJson), artist.id);

const repeated = unwrap(buildIidAnchor('music-recording', recordingValues));
assert.equal(repeated.id, recording.id);
const nameOnly = unwrap(
  buildIidAnchor('music-recording', { name: 'One More Time' }),
);
assert.notEqual(nameOnly.id, recording.id);
assert.equal(nameOnly.profile, 'p1');
assert.equal(inspectIntuitionId(recording.iid!).valid, true);
assert.equal(classificationForIid(recording.iid!)?.slug, 'music-recording');
assert.equal(classificationForIid('int:wd:Q42'), undefined);

const catalog = {
  synthetic: true,
  entities: [recording, artist, album].map(({ data, iid, profile, id }) => ({
    data,
    iid,
    profile,
    id,
  })),
  predicates: [byArtist, inAlbum].map(({ key, atomData, id }) => ({
    key,
    atomData,
    id,
  })),
  claims: claims.map((triple) => ({
    triple,
    source: 'local synthetic fixture',
  })),
};
console.log(JSON.stringify(catalog, null, 2));
console.log('3 entities, 2 predicate atoms, 2 directed claims');
console.log(
  `Profiles: ${catalog.entities.map((entity) => entity.profile).join(', ')}`,
);
console.log(
  'Context unchanged; reversed edge differs; bare Wikidata type unknown',
);
```

The recording and release-group use typed MusicBrainz fixtures and select `p0`, whose data is the bare IID. The artist uses a name-derived `p1` envelope. Its name is ambiguous; deterministic serialization does not establish unique real-world identity. The script's repeated recording import has the same bytes and ID, while the name-only recording uses a different representation and ID.

A predicate key such as `byArtist` selects a registry entry. That entry supplies canonical serialized atom data and its deterministic ID; it is not merely a label to hash. Both predicate atoms belong in the graph. `buildTriple` uses subject, predicate, and object in order. Reversing those roles produces a different claim, as the assertion demonstrates.

### 3. Inspect identity and context boundaries

The printed `entities` array contains exact `data`, `iid`, `profile`, and atom `id` values. The IID describes the selected identifier; the atom ID is derived from the serialized representation's bytes. `predicates` exposes each key, serialized data, and ID. `claims` retains the local fixture attribution.

The code proves that companion `contextUris` leave the data and atom ID unchanged. In contrast, changing JSON-LD `@context` inside the artist's serialized atom changes its bytes and ID. Do not confuse those two kinds of context. Name or label edits in a separate application presentation record need not rewrite existing atom data.

### 4. Plan the next boundary explicitly

Use [creation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles) to inspect fields and allowed relationship targets. A collected `byArtist` string is not the edge; this example creates the edge explicitly.

Follow [classify and enrich](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) for separate parse, classify, provider-plan, fixture-execution, and provenance steps. A name-only input can remain a generic `Thing`; a valid IID can have no mapped type or available provider. Neither classification nor an enrichment artifact proves a real-world match.

To read shared records, [query your Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Choose whether to insert these exact records off-chain or create missing terms on-chain and wait for indexing. Local construction does not persist atoms. Preserve subject, predicate, and object data and verify that the required terms exist before writing triples.

## Run it

```sh
node catalog.ts
```

The script prints the complete catalog JSON and then these measured summary lines:

```text
3 entities, 2 predicate atoms, 2 directed claims
Profiles: p0, p1, p0
Context unchanged; reversed edge differs; bare Wikidata type unknown
```

Assertions check deduplication, profile selection, predicate identity, triple direction, context invariance, and an unmapped classification. These are local checks, not provider or chain verification.

## Full source

[Music catalog source project](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/d137b0adacbfb9fda3b0d07d94e695ca4e7abc03/examples/v2/music-catalog), including processing and plugin helpers. The catalog fixture is grounded in [pinned anchor tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/__tests__/anchor-parity.test.ts) and the [package lifecycle example](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/package-lifecycle.ts).

## Next steps

Explore [representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), [predicate helpers](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates), [action envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans), and [Core reads](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

# Predicate picker with relationship suggestions

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/predicate-picker

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0

**Time:** 15 minutes · **Steps:** 3

## What you'll build

Give a catalog editor two choices for **Paper Moon Demo**. Choosing **by artist** offers the group **Night Shift Trio**. Choosing **in album** offers the album **After Hours**. The preview displays the selected subject, predicate, object, and calculated triple ID.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 22.21.0. From the documentation repository root at the revision in **Full source**, install the example workspace once. npm needs registry access for installation. The runner uses only local data.

```sh
cd examples/v2
npm ci --ignore-scripts
```

For your own host, see [Install the packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). Read [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates) and [triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples) for the role of the middle atom.

## Steps

### 1. Build the menu from the recording profile

The picker supports two profile relationships with classification hints. For `byArtist`, the hints are `music-group` and `person`. For `inAlbum`, the hint is `music-album`. Each entry below contains the exact synthetic text used to derive its atom ID.

```ts
import { musicRecordingCreationProfile } from '@0xintuition/classifications/creation/music-recording';
import { calculateAtomId, calculateTripleId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { getPredicateById, getPredicateId } from '@0xintuition/predicates';

export const recording = {
  name: 'Paper Moon Demo',
  data: 'example:recording:paper-moon',
};
export const catalog = [
  {
    name: 'Night Shift Trio',
    classification: 'music-group',
    data: 'example:group:night-shift',
  },
  {
    name: 'After Hours',
    classification: 'music-album',
    data: 'example:album:after-hours',
  },
];
export const relationships = musicRecordingCreationProfile.relationships.filter(
  ({ predicate }) =>
    predicate.key === 'byArtist' || predicate.key === 'inAlbum',
);

export function objectHints(key: string): string[] {
  const relation = relationships.find(({ predicate }) => predicate.key === key);
  return (
    relation?.expectedObjects.flatMap((hint) =>
      hint.kind === 'classification' ? [hint.slug] : [],
    ) ?? []
  );
}
```

### 2. Resolve the selected terms in order

Look up the profile’s predicate atom ID in the registry and check the key. Apply the classification hints to the selected object. Using the registry’s predicate ID, calculate the triple ID in subject, predicate, object order.

```ts
export function previewTriple(key: string, objectData: string) {
  const relation = relationships.find(({ predicate }) => predicate.key === key);
  if (!relation)
    return { ok: false as const, message: 'Choose a relationship.' };
  const predicate = getPredicateById(relation.predicate.id);
  if (!predicate || predicate.key !== key) {
    return {
      ok: false as const,
      message: 'The predicate is missing from this registry.',
    };
  }
  const target = catalog.find((item) => item.data === objectData);
  if (!target)
    return { ok: false as const, message: 'Choose a catalog entry.' };
  if (!objectHints(key).includes(target.classification)) {
    return {
      ok: false as const,
      message: 'Choose an entry with a suggested classification.',
    };
  }
  const subjectId = calculateAtomId(recording.data);
  const predicateId = getPredicateId(predicate.key);
  const objectId = calculateAtomId(target.data);
  return {
    ok: true as const,
    status: predicate.status,
    subjectId,
    predicateId,
    objectId,
    tripleId: calculateTripleId(subjectId, predicateId, objectId),
  };
}
```

The picker applies a local catalog policy. A matching classification makes a group eligible for selection. The editor still needs evidence that the group performed the recording. The registry status `proposed` describes the predicate definition. Calculating a triple ID neither registers the claim nor attests to it.

### 3. Connect both selections to the preview

In `picker.tsx`, the selected relationship determines the available catalog entries. Switching relationships clears the previous object and result. Selecting **Preview triple** with an incomplete selection displays the model’s feedback.

```tsx
  const [key, setKey] = useState('');
  const [target, setTarget] = useState('');
  const [review, setReview] = useState<ReturnType<typeof previewTriple>>();
  const hints = objectHints(key);
  const candidates = catalog.filter((entry) =>
    hints.includes(entry.classification),
  );
```

Copy `picker.tsx` and `picker-model.ts` together into a React 19 client application with a TSX compiler. Use the dependency versions in the example workspace. In the client entrypoint import `mountPredicatePicker` from `./picker.tsx`, pass it an empty DOM element after mounting that element, and call the returned cleanup when the host removes it.

```tsx
export function mountPredicatePicker(container: HTMLElement) {
  const root = createRoot(container);
  root.render(<PredicatePicker />);
  return () => root.unmount();
}
```

Choose **by artist**, then **Night Shift Trio**, then **Preview triple**. The Node entrypoint exercises the same calculation and also attempts an empty selection and an album in the artist slot.

## Run it

From `examples/v2`, run the TypeScript entrypoint.

```sh
node predicate-picker/src/run-picker.ts
```

```text
byArtist proposed 0x021384b11c429411aaa3ec931394524e5f3e1429b4f903d8719032f71e942445
Choose a relationship.
Choose an entry with a suggested classification.
```

The runner also checks that swapping the group and recording produces a different ID.

## Full source

[Predicate picker component, catalog model, and runner](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/3f47445235983fa93bf22d1d06f0584c6bac84fa/examples/v2/predicate-picker). Compare the [upstream playground](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/examples/hackathon-quickstart/src/Playground.tsx), [profile relationship types](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/creation-profile.ts), [registry lookup](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/predicates.ts), and [ordered triple ID calculation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/triple-id.ts).

## Next steps

Adapt the [relationship suggestion guide](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/suggest-relationships) to your own catalog, or use [identity linking](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/identity-linking) to review two representations of the same recording.

# React app with @0xintuition/react

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/react-app

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0

**Time:** 20 minutes · **Steps:** 4

## What you'll build

Build a page that reads an atom from its testnet term ID. Connect a wallet to create an atom from text, inspect the exact bytes and payment, then read the atom by term ID once the receipt matches the reviewed creation.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.21.0 with npm, Bun 1.3.11 for bundling and Python 3 for a local static server. To use the page, supply a browser-accessible Intuition testnet RPC URL. Have an existing atom term ID for a wallet-free lookup. To create an atom, use an injected browser wallet on chain 13579 funded for native payment and gas. The build and typecheck run offline after dependency installation. [Pinned installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) · [Atom identity](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms)

## Steps

### 1. Install the isolated host

From the documentation checkout containing the full source below, install the example lockfile. This resolves React and React DOM 19.1.0, wagmi 2.15.4, React Query 5.90.2 and viem 2.31.4. Keep the terminal in `examples/v2` for the remaining commands.

```sh
cd examples/v2
npm ci --ignore-scripts
./node_modules/.bin/tsc -p react-app/tsconfig.json --noEmit
```

A successful typecheck exits without output. The HTML host loads the compiled JavaScript module, whose entry point mounts the application.

```tsx
const host = document.getElementById('root');
if (!host) throw new Error('Add an element with id="root" to the host page.');
createRoot(host).render(<App />);
```

### 2. Connect the RPC and read a term

The application checks the chain ID when you select **Use this RPC**. It then mounts `WagmiProvider`, `QueryClientProvider` and `IntuitionProvider` with the testnet deployment. Paste a 32-byte term ID into **Read an atom** to see its bytes, curve ID, total assets in wei and total shares. An incomplete contract response offers a retry. The wallet connection remains optional for this step. [Provider and read hook setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/react)

### 3. Review the wallet call

Connect the intended testnet account. Enter new text whose exact bytes you want to use as the atom’s identity. Spaces and case affect the payload. Select **Review creation** once the contract returns the atom cost. The review encodes one allocation equal to the cost, with no additional stake. Gas is separate.

```ts
export function prepareReview(
  chainId: number,
  sender: Address,
  target: Address,
  text: string,
  atomCost: bigint,
) {
  if (!text.trim()) throw new Error('Enter text for the atom.');
  const data = [stringToHex(text)];
  const assets = [atomCost];
  return {
    chainId,
    sender,
    target,
    data,
    assets,
    value: atomCost,
    calldata: multiVaultCreateAtomsEncode(data, assets),
  };
}
```

Compare the sender, chain ID, MultiVault address, data, assets, total value and calldata with the intended call. Editing the text clears the review. Disconnecting, switching accounts or chains, or observing a changed cost also requires another review. Submission checks the latest cached cost from the hook. The contract still enforces the cost at execution. [MultiVault deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/deployments)

### 4. Submit and read the receipt

Select **Submit to wallet** only if the review matches your intent. In the wallet, verify the account, network, target, payment and gas before approving. The application passes the reviewed arrays to `createAtom` and displays the hash while waiting for the receipt. Stay on Intuition testnet during this wait because the receipt hook follows wagmi’s current chain. A rejected request or reverted transaction surfaces an error. If you received a hash, inspect it before making another attempt.

```tsx
  async function submit(review: Review) {
    setCompleted(undefined);
    const wallet = getAccount(config);
    if (
      !wallet.isConnected ||
      wallet.chainId !== review.chainId ||
      wallet.address !== review.sender ||
      review.target !== multivaultAddress ||
      review.value !== flow.atomCost ||
      cost.isError
    ) {
      setAttempt((value) => value + 1);
      setMessage(
        'The wallet or cost changed. Review the current details again.',
      );
      return;
    }
    setMessage('');
    try {
      const { receipt } = await flow.createAtom({
        data: review.data,
        assets: review.assets,
      });
      setCompleted({ review, receipt });
    } catch (error) {
      setMessage(
        error instanceof Error
          ? error.message
          : 'The wallet or transaction failed.',
      );
    }
  }

  const result =
    completed &&
    flow.status === 'confirmed' &&
    flow.receipt === completed.receipt
      ? verifyCreationReceipt(completed.review, flow.hash, completed.receipt)
      : undefined;
  const verifiedTermId = result?.termId;
  useEffect(() => {
    if (verifiedTermId) {
      setLookup(verifiedTermId);
      void cache.invalidateQueries({ type: 'active' });
    }
  }, [verifiedTermId, cache]);
```

Compare **Submitted hash** with **Mined hash**. If your wallet replaced the transaction, the page shows both hashes for inspection. This also applies to a replacement that only changes the gas price.

For the original hash, the app checks that the receipt succeeded with the reviewed sender and target. It checks a single `AtomCreated` event from that transaction and MultiVault against the creator, reviewed bytes and derived term ID. A match displays the block and fills **Read an atom** with the verified term ID. If a check fails, inspect the receipt before considering another submission.

## Run it

From `examples/v2`, build the browser bundle, copy its HTML host and serve the generated directory on loopback.

```sh
bun build react-app/src/main.tsx --target browser --production --outdir react-app/dist
cp react-app/index.html react-app/dist/index.html
python3 -m http.server 4173 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory react-app/dist
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173`. You should see **Read and create an atom** and a field for your RPC URL. The first RPC request follows **Use this RPC**. To exercise creation, follow the wallet review and approval steps above. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when finished.

## Full source

[React app, HTML host and strict TypeScript project](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/tree/84242e8f4399ac758c942e85b343e0512245a6cf/examples/v2/react-app)

# Choose your packages

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/choose-packages

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

Start with the operation your application needs. Install each package you import directly, even when another package includes it as a dependency. The linked references include exact install commands and supported entry points.

| I want to… | Install | Then read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build an atom or a triple from validated inputs | `@0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0` | [Atom and triple builders](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) |
| Compute a term ID from existing bytes | `@0xintuition/ids@0.1.0` | [Deterministic ID functions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids) |
| Canonicalize an Intuition Identifier | `@0xintuition/iid@0.1.0` | [IID parsing and normalization](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid) |
| Use the packaged IID grammar and test vectors | `@0xintuition/iid-spec@0.1.0` | [IID specification files](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec) |
| Select the strongest available identifier for a record | `@0xintuition/iid-ladder@0.1.0` | [Identity projection](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder) |
| Find classifications and providers for an IID scheme | `@0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0` | [IID registry lookups](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry) |
| Build a form from a Creation Profile | `@0xintuition/classifications@0.1.0` | [Creation Profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications) |
| Look up schema.org types and properties | `@0xintuition/schema-org@0.1.0` | [Schema vocabulary](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org) |
| Choose a predicate for a relationship | `@0xintuition/predicates@0.1.0` | [Predicate registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates) |
| Recognize and normalize incoming atom data | `@0xintuition/atom-parser@0.1.0` | [Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser) |
| Classify parsed data with rules and plugins | `@0xintuition/atom-classification@0.1.0` | [Classification engine](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification) |
| Collect enrichment results from providers | `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment@0.1.0` | [Enrichment adapters](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment) |
| Compose classification and enrichment in one service | `@0xintuition/atom-runtime@0.1.0` | [Runtime composition](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-runtime) |
| Apply cancellation and host policies to provider requests | `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime@0.1.0` | [Pipeline utilities](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime) |
| Find a network, contract address, or ABI | `@0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0` | [Deployment catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments) |
| Read a vault or submit a protocol transaction | `@0xintuition/protocol@4.0.0` | [Contract wrappers](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) |
| Calculate shares and prices from local curve state | `@0xintuition/curves@0.1.0` | [Curve math](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves) |
| Work with periphery contracts and bridge calls | `@0xintuition/periphery@0.1.0` | [Periphery interfaces](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery) |
| Prepare a quote or an unsigned action envelope | `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0` | [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) |
| Discover contract encoders and print calldata in a terminal | `@0xintuition/cli@0.1.0` | [CLI encoders](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/cli) |
| Use protocol hooks in a React application | `@0xintuition/react@0.1.0` | [React hooks](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/react) |

To read the **indexed graph**, run a Core node and use its Query API. For a first local project, the offline quickstart needs just the primitives package. [Query your Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) · [Offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) · [Install compatible packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install)

# Quickstart: your first on-chain write

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/first-write

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0

**Time:** 10 minutes · **Steps:** 8

## What you'll build

Create a named atom and attach a context URI on Intuition Testnet. After its creation receipt arrives, deposit test TRUST into the new vault and read the number of shares your account owns. You review and authorize the two transactions separately.

## Before you start

Use Node 22.18 or newer, npm, and a throwaway **testnet-only** account. You need an interactive terminal and access to the Intuition Testnet RPC. Have the account's public address handy for the faucet. Keep its private key on your machine.

## Steps

### 1. Fund the testnet account

Request tTRUST for your public address at the [Intuition Testnet faucet](https://testnet.hub.intuition.systems/). Leave enough balance for the atom creation cost, your chosen deposit, and gas for both transactions.

### 2. Install the pinned packages

```sh
mkdir intuition-first-write
cd intuition-first-write
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install --save-exact @0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0 @0xintuition/protocol@4.0.0 @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Save the [complete first-write.ts script](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-docs/blob/f181e57eca7eacb34212214d3befe8358470254a/examples/v2/first-write/src/first-write.ts) in this folder. The excerpts below show what it runs.

### 3. Set the throwaway key and deposit

Add `.env` to `.gitignore` before creating it. In a local editor, save the following as `.env` and replace the placeholder with your throwaway key. Set `DEPOSIT_AMOUNT` to the amount you want to deposit, in whole-token units.

```text
TESTNET_PRIVATE_KEY=<your 0x-prefixed testnet private key>
DEPOSIT_AMOUNT=0.001
```

### 4. Read the creation cost and URI limits

Start the script **once** and leave the terminal open for steps 5–7.

```sh
node --env-file=.env first-write.ts
```

The script checks the RPC's chain ID against Intuition Testnet (`13579`). It reads `getAtomCost` and `getAtomUriConfig` from the pinned MultiVault address, then checks your deposit against the current minimum. At the first prompt, find the creation payment, maximum URI count, and maximum byte length per URI. One tTRUST equals 10¹⁸ wei.

### 5. Review and create the atom

Each preparation generates a fresh UUID for the atom's name. The builder returns the serialized data and the ID derived from it. Encoding that exact string produces the bytes sent to MultiVault. The context URI identifies this run and travels alongside those bytes.

```ts
  const uuid = crypto.randomUUID();
  const result = buildThing({ name: 'Intuition docs first write ' + uuid });
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  const { data, id } = result.value;
  const dataHex = stringToHex(data);
  const uri = 'urn:uuid:' + uuid;
  const inputs: CreateAtomsWithUrisInputs = {
    args: [signer, [dataHex], [atomCost], [[stringToHex(uri)]]],
    value: atomCost,
    uriLimits,
  };
  const creation = {
    uuid,
    data,
    dataHex,
    id,
    uri,
    inputs,
    calldata: multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUrisEncode(inputs),
  };
```

Check the chain ID, MultiVault destination, signer and receiver against your intended account and deployment. Inspect the generated name, atom ID, URI, exact calldata, and creation payment. The payment equals the single atom's assets entry. Gas is additional and depends on network fees. Check the [testnet deployment addresses](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/deployments).

Type `CREATE` only to authorize this creation. Any other answer stops before signing. The wrapper simulates, then submits the same prepared inputs. The script prints the transaction link and waits for its successful receipt before preparing a deposit.

```ts
    const createAnswer = await review('CREATE', {
      atomId: atom.id,
      data: atom.data,
      dataHex: atom.dataHex,
      uri: atom.uri,
      maxUriCount,
      maxUriLength,
      calldata: atom.calldata,
      valueWei: cost,
      valueTokens: formatEther(cost),
    });
    const createHash = await afterReview('CREATE', createAnswer, () =>
      multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris(config, atom.inputs),
    );
    await confirm(createHash);
```

### 6. Review and deposit into its vault

Check that the second prompt shows the **same atom ID**, your address as receiver, the default curve ID, and your chosen deposit. The script calls `previewDeposit` on the newly created vault and rounds the minimum shares **up** to 99% of the quote. A price move below that floor causes the deposit to revert.

Type `DEPOSIT` only to authorize the displayed calldata and value. The wrapper simulates the call before sending it. Declining this second prompt leaves the confirmed atom on-chain.

```ts
    const [quotedShares] = await multiVaultPreviewDeposit(config, {
      args: [atom.id, defaultCurveId, deposit],
    });
    if (quotedShares <= 0n) throw new Error('Deposit would mint no shares.');
    const minShares = (quotedShares * 99n + 99n) / 100n;
    const args = [signer, atom.id, defaultCurveId, minShares] as const;
    const depositAnswer = await review('DEPOSIT', {
      atomId: atom.id,
      curveId: defaultCurveId,
      quotedShares,
      minShares,
      calldata: multiVaultDepositEncode(...args),
      valueWei: deposit,
      valueTokens: formatEther(deposit),
    });
    const depositHash = await afterReview('DEPOSIT', depositAnswer, () =>
      multiVaultDeposit(config, { args, value: deposit }),
    );
    await confirm(depositHash);
```

### 7. Read your position

After the deposit receipt succeeds, `getShares` reads your position using the receiver, the reviewed atom ID, and the same curve ID.

```ts
    const shares = await multiVaultGetShares(config, {
      args: [signer, atom.id, defaultCurveId],
    });
```

### 8. Inspect the receipts

Open each transaction link printed by the script in the [testnet explorer](https://testnet.explorer.intuition.systems). Check the sender, MultiVault destination, status, and native value. Keep the creation hash, deposit hash, and atom ID together. If receipt lookup times out, check the printed hash before attempting another transaction.

## Run it

Use the single interactive run started in step 4. Running the command again prepares a different atom. After the two approvals and successful receipts, look for these lines among the review details:

```text
Transaction: https://testnet.explorer.intuition.systems/tx/<creation transaction hash>
Transaction: https://testnet.explorer.intuition.systems/tx/<deposit transaction hash>
Atom ID: <your atom ID>
Position (shares): <your share balance>
```

## Next steps

- [Vaults and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults) explains what those shares represent.
- [Protocol wrappers](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) covers more reads and writes.
- [Prepare action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) shows how to hand unsigned operations to a separate executor.

The [package getting-started guide](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/getting-started.md#move-from-offline-data-to-a-transaction), [URI-aware creation wrapper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/src/core/multivault/create-atoms-with-uris.ts), and [MultiVault contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVault.sol) define the calls used here.

# How the pieces fit

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits

A music catalog can identify a recording, describe its artist, register their relationship, and read it back from a node. Different parts of Intuition handle each step. The packages handle local modeling and protocol operations. Intuition Core builds and serves the indexed graph.

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  primitives["Protocol primitives"] --> identity["Intuition Identifier"] --> processing["Classification and enrichment"] --> writes["Protocol writes"] --> querying["Indexing and querying"]
  semantic["Semantic / data modeling"] -.-> primitives
  builders["Builder helpers"] -.-> primitives
  ids["Identity packages"] -.-> identity
  runtime["Pipeline runtime"] -.-> processing
  atoms["Atom processing"] -.-> processing
  app["Application integration"] -.-> writes
  protocol["Protocol plumbing"] -.-> writes
  core["Intuition Core"] -.-> querying
  core -.-> processing
```

On the concept ladder, Protocol primitives form Tier 1, Intuition Identifier belongs to Tier 2 (Identity), Classification and enrichment span Tiers 3 and 4 (Meaning and Processing), and Protocol writes and Indexing and querying form Tier 5 (Data flow).

### Start with exact data

A recording is an entity. Its atom contains the bytes of a particular representation. A P0 anchor stores canonical IID text, while a contextual representation stores a JSON object. Hashing the exact atom data produces its atom ID. Persist the bytes and ID together so later metadata updates do not silently create a different term.

The catalog represents its relationship as recording → **by artist** → artist. The predicate is itself an atom. Its registry key selects a definition, and its serialized data determines its ID. A field named `artist` in a recording object does not create a triple, and reversing subject and object changes the statement.

### Choose packages by responsibility

| Layer | Packages | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Semantic / data modeling | `schema-org`, `classifications`, `predicates` | Shared vocabulary, input fields, and relationship suggestions |
| Identity | `iid-spec`, `iid`, `iid-registry`, `iid-ladder`, `ids` | Identifier rules, candidate selection, provider plans, and deterministic IDs |
| Builder helpers | `primitives` | Build atom data and explicit triples |
| Pipeline runtime | `pipeline-runtime` | Concurrency, cancellation, and circuit breaking |
| Atom processing | `atom-parser`, `atom-classification`, `atom-enrichment`, `atom-runtime` | Parse inputs, run plugins, and execute configured providers |
| Application integration | `sdk`, `cli` | Prepare actions, serializable envelopes, and calldata |
| Protocol plumbing | `protocol`, `deployments`, `periphery`, `curves`, `react` | Contract calls, deployment metadata, curve math, and hooks |

For a recording, the identity layer can plan a provider lookup from an IID. The atom processing layer executes selected adapters, checks their artifacts, and extracts supported fields. The app decides what evidence to display. See the package relationships in the [runtime dependency graph](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/architecture/dependency-graph.md).

### Add persistence and transactions deliberately

Local modeling needs no chain or Core node. RPC reads inspect a selected contract's current state. Preparing an action may use those reads. Submitting it requires an authorized signer. A transaction hash, a successful receipt, and visibility in an index are three different results.

Fork and clone Intuition Core to build your own node from the pinned source. The default Compose stack starts its off-chain API and processing services. Enable the indexing profile and configure the chain and MultiVault deployment for ingestion and projections. Once projections catch up, read the recording and its relationships from your node's Query API. An authenticated off-chain API insert writes to that node independently of a chain transaction. [Core architecture](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/docs/architecture.md), [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

Keep provider secrets on your server. Your application owns access control, evidence acceptance, ranking, and the meaning it assigns to vault positions. A shared ID or a large position does not establish that a claim is true.

## Related

- [Concept map](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts) links every tier and the shortest reading path to enrichment.
- [Offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) proves identity and companion-context invariance.
- [Package reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages) gives public imports and runtime requirements.
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) separates planning, signing, and observation.
- [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) covers peers, contract artifacts, and the pinned Core source.

Source: [Package layers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#package-layers).

# Migrate from V1

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0

Move an existing integration to the V2 package boundaries without silently changing historical atom bytes, IDs, claims, or positions.

## Before you start

Keep your existing lockfile and a fixture set of stored atom data, atom IDs, and ordered triples. Read [representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles), [compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility), and [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install). Add readers for new representations before enabling new writers.

### What changed

V1 covers the `intuition-ts` packages and `intuition-rs` services. V2 covers the packages in the [release manifest](https://docs.intuition.systems/intuition-release.json) and Intuition Core. The generation label is independent of package semver.

Since the stable release on November 12, 2026, an untagged or `latest` install of the SDK or protocol selects the V2 package. To maintain V1, preserve `@0xintuition/sdk` 3.0.1, `@0xintuition/protocol` 2.0.3, and `@0xintuition/graphql` 3.0.1 in your lockfile. Frozen V1 pages still contain some untagged installs; do not assume every historical install command preserves those versions.

The V2 SDK root no longer exports the entire protocol or ID surface. Atom builders, shared predicates, identity selection, and transaction planning now have focused public packages. Core is a source application you fork and run; it is separate from installing the libraries.

## Steps

### 1. Map your packages

| V1 responsibility | V2 replacement | Migration check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@0xintuition/sdk` | `sdk` plus `ids`, `predicates`, and `primitives` | Replace removed root exports and separate local building from writes |
| `@0xintuition/protocol` | `protocol` plus `deployments`, `periphery`, and `curves` | Select the deployed implementation and its public artifacts |
| `@0xintuition/graphql` | No V2 package counterpart | Read the Query API of [a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) |
| `intuition-cli` | `@0xintuition/cli` | Use encoders; move client-free plans to SDK envelopes |
| Application-local type and predicate maps | `classifications` and `predicates` | Preserve canonical slugs, serialized predicate data, and IDs |
| Upload helper | Application-owned storage provider | Preserve existing content URIs; upload and protocol registration are separate operations |

Install exact versions for the packages you import directly and commit your lockfile. The [package catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages) lists public entry points and peers.

### 2. Update imports

A V1 import can combine broad helpers at the SDK root:

```ts
import { calculateAtomId, createAtomFromString } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

export const legacyHelpers = { calculateAtomId, createAtomFromString };
```

For V2, choose each package's public entry point:

```ts
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { PREDICATE_IDS } from '@0xintuition/predicates';
import { multivaultPrepareDepositTx } from '@0xintuition/sdk/actions';
import { getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId } from '@0xintuition/protocol';

export const migrationImports = {
  calculateAtomId,
  PREDICATE_IDS,
  multivaultPrepareDepositTx,
  getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId,
};
```

The SDK root retains selected ID helpers, but `ids` is the full deterministic-ID package. `sdk/utils` contains formatting utilities. Import low-level protocol APIs from `@0xintuition/protocol`, or use the explicit `@0xintuition/sdk/protocol` escape hatch. Bytecode belongs to `deployments/bytecode` or `protocol/contracts`; curve math belongs to `curves`.

### 3. Replace atom creation

V1 combines creation with a string or uploaded Thing workflow. These functions submit when called:

```ts
import { createAtomFromString, createAtomFromThing } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

type LegacyWriteConfig = Parameters<typeof createAtomFromString>[0];

export function createLegacyText(config: LegacyWriteConfig, text: string) {
  return createAtomFromString(config, text);
}

export function createLegacyThing(
  config: LegacyWriteConfig,
  thing: Parameters<typeof createAtomFromThing>[1],
) {
  return createAtomFromThing(config, thing);
}
```

For new V2 entities, build data first. `buildThing` preserves the descriptive JSON-LD builder pattern; `buildIidAnchor` selects an identity representation. They return a checked `BuildResult`, not a transaction receipt. Neither performs an upload.

The following helper demonstrates the separate write boundary. **Calling it simulates and submits a wallet transaction.** It is a migration reference, not part of the offline quickstart. The caller must choose a compatible deployment and creator, read current creation cost and URI limits, check existence, and supply assets in base units before invocation.

```ts
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';
import { multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import type { AtomUriLimits, WriteConfig } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import { stringToHex, type Address } from 'viem';

// Calling this function simulates and submits a wallet transaction.
export async function createRecording(
  config: WriteConfig,
  creator: Address,
  isrc: string,
  assets: bigint,
  uriLimits: AtomUriLimits,
) {
  const result = buildIidAnchor('music-recording', { isrc });
  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
  const atom = result.value;
  const transactionHash = await multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris(config, {
    args: [
      creator,
      [atom.dataHex],
      [assets],
      [atom.contextUris.map((uri) => stringToHex(uri))],
    ],
    value: assets,
    uriLimits,
  });
  return { atom, transactionHash };
}
```

This helper uses no companion URIs, so its URI list is empty. If your application adds them, pass the builder's normalized `contextUris` through the URI-aware operation. Its `value` must equal the assets sum. A submitted hash still needs a successful receipt and event parsing scoped to the expected emitting contract.

An existing V1 string or IPFS URI is not automatically equivalent to a new IID anchor. Preserve the original bytes and ID; creating an anchor is a separate graph decision.

### 4. Replace triple creation

V1 wraps the contract operation and returns its event state:

```ts
import { createTripleStatement } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

export function createLegacyTriple(
  config: Parameters<typeof createTripleStatement>[0],
  input: Parameters<typeof createTripleStatement>[1],
) {
  return createTripleStatement(config, input);
}
```

V2 can calculate the ID locally and submit through the explicit protocol wrapper. The function below submits when invoked; its subject, predicate, and object atoms must already exist on the selected deployment.

```ts
import { calculateTripleId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import {
  multiVaultCreateTriples,
  type WriteConfig as TripleWriteConfig,
} from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import type { Hex } from 'viem';

// The three atoms must already exist on the selected deployment.
export async function createRelationship(
  config: TripleWriteConfig,
  subject: Hex,
  predicate: Hex,
  object: Hex,
  assets: bigint,
) {
  const id = calculateTripleId(subject, predicate, object);
  const transactionHash = await multiVaultCreateTriples(config, {
    args: [[subject], [predicate], [object], [assets]],
    value: assets,
  });
  return { id, transactionHash };
}
```

Preserve subject–predicate–object order. Use the predicate registry's serialized data and ID; a registry key or display label alone is not the predicate atom. Reversing a triple changes its meaning and ID. Handle a reverted receipt or no matching creation event explicitly.

### 5. Move reads

A V1 read uses `getAtomDetails`:

```ts
import { getAtomDetails } from '@0xintuition/sdk';

export function readLegacyAtom(atomId: string) {
  return getAtomDetails(atomId);
}
```

For V2 indexed graph data, [query a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Keep missing records and indexing delay visible to callers. Contract reads through protocol helpers read chain state, which is a separate data source.

The V2 SDK's `@0xintuition/sdk/api` client and its `atoms.getById` still call the hosted V1 GraphQL API. They are not a V2 read path; [The SDK read client](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/read-with-sdk) documents that boundary. Existing GraphQL queries stay with the supported [V1 API documentation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1/graphql-api/overview).

### 6. Preserve identity

Keep the exact stored string when re-deriving a historical atom ID:

```ts
import { calculateAtomId as atomIdFromData } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { stringToHex as encodeData } from 'viem';

export function preserveAtom(data: string) {
  const dataHex = encodeData(data);
  return { data, dataHex, id: atomIdFromData(dataHex) };
}
```

Compare the result against your stored ID before switching. Do not parse and serialize JSON again just to normalize it: field order, whitespace, schema context strings, and payload changes can alter bytes and IDs. Do not rebuild an existing atom under another profile.

Companion `contextUris` are distinct from JSON-LD `@context` inside atom data. Metadata can be refreshed separately; changing identity-bearing fields creates another representation. Preserve historical claims and positions on their original terms, and model reviewed equivalence with explicit attributed relationships.

### 7. Move agent and CLI plans

Client-free, JSON-serializable envelope builders now live in `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`. For example, the deprecated CLI library name `buildMultiVaultDepositPlan` maps to `multiVaultDepositEnvelope`; `buildFeeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisPlan` maps to `feeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisEnvelope`.

The `intuition` executable exposes encoder commands, not a plan command. Envelope builders consume caller-supplied read context; quote and preparation helpers may perform RPC reads, while execution helpers can submit. See [action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) for the reviewed-plan workflow and the [source alias table](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/docs/action-plans.md) for all mappings.

Require human review of signer, chain, destination, receiver, value, and limits before signing or submission. Keep already mined steps recorded if a multi-step execution later fails.

## Check the result

Your integration should compile against the exact V2 packages, preserve every historical fixture's bytes and ID, and explicitly handle `BuildResult` errors, absent records, reverted receipts, and partial enrichment. Check that indexed reads use your Core adapter and that offline previews cannot invoke write helpers.

Treat compilation and fixture checks as their own evidence. They do not prove a deployment supports every ABI operation or that a transaction was submitted successfully.

# Quickstart: an atom ID and IID offline

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0

**Time:** 10 minutes · **Steps:** 6

## What you'll build

Turn the ISRC spelling `US-RC1-76-07839` into the canonical IID `int:isrc:USRC17607839`, a P0 representation, and a deterministic atom ID. The code also proves that equivalent ISRC spellings and different companion context URIs produce the same atom bytes and ID.

This is the packages' golden canonicalization fixture. It is separate from the synthetic recording identities in the music catalog; no recording title or artist is inferred from it.

## Before you start

Use **Node 22.18 or newer** to run TypeScript directly. Installation needs npm registry access. After installation, the example runs offline with no wallet, RPC, API key, or account. It creates no remote or on-chain record.

## Steps

### 1. Check Node

```sh
node --version
```

Confirm the version is at least `v22.18.0`.

### 2. Create an ESM project

```sh
mkdir intuition-quickstart
cd intuition-quickstart
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
```

### 3. Install the pinned builder

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0
```

Keep the generated lockfile. See [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) for other package combinations and declared peers.

### 4. Save the offline example

Create `quickstart.ts`:

```ts
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

const result = buildIidAnchor(
  'music-recording',
  { isrc: 'US-RC1-76-07839' },
  { contextUris: ['https://example.com/recordings/1'] },
);
if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.errors.join('; '));
const atom = result.value;
assert.equal(atom.iid, 'int:isrc:USRC17607839');
assert.equal(atom.profile, 'p0');
assert.equal(atom.data, atom.iid);

const otherContext = buildIidAnchor(
  'music-recording',
  { isrc: 'USRC17607839' },
  { contextUris: ['https://example.org/alternate-evidence'] },
);
if (!otherContext.success) throw new Error(otherContext.errors.join('; '));
assert.equal(otherContext.value.data, atom.data);
assert.equal(otherContext.value.dataHex, atom.dataHex);
assert.equal(otherContext.value.id, atom.id);

console.log(atom.iid);
console.log(atom.profile);
console.log(atom.dataHex);
console.log(atom.id);
```

`success` distinguishes a valid result from structured errors. `data` is the exact canonical IID text for this P0 atom, `dataHex` encodes those bytes, and `id` is the bytes32 protocol atom ID. Companion `contextUris` are discovery information; this code neither fetches nor uploads them.

### 5. Run the example

```sh
node quickstart.ts
```

Compare the four lines with **Run it** below. Keep the IID, profile, exact data, hex bytes, atom ID, and original identity evidence together. Deriving an ID does not prove that an atom exists on a chain or in a Core node.

### 6. Optionally inspect the IID

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid@0.1.0 @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0
```

Save as `inspect.ts`, then run `node inspect.ts`:

```ts
import { inspectIntuitionId } from '@0xintuition/iid';
import { classificationForIid } from '@0xintuition/iid-registry';

const iid = 'int:isrc:USRC17607839';
const inspection = inspectIntuitionId(iid);
if (!inspection.valid) throw new Error(inspection.reason);
const classification = classificationForIid(iid);
console.log(inspection.valid);
console.log(classification?.slug ?? 'No classification match');
```

This fixture prints `true` and `music-recording`. Other inputs can be invalid or have no unambiguous classification. Inspection and classification lookup do not execute provider requests.

## Run it

```sh
node quickstart.ts
```

Expected output from the pinned packages:

```text
int:isrc:USRC17607839
p0
0x696e743a697372633a555352433137363037383339
0xd3368a8190d3afd5fb05abd01db8141c09a77c3f290bb7a0ef2ffb2b5acab8d8
```

The last line is an atom ID, not an IID string. The assertions run before any output; an assertion failure or builder error stops execution.

## Next steps

- [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles) explains when an IID needs contextual atom data.
- [Build a music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) adds explicit artist and album triples using synthetic fixtures.
- [Your first on-chain write](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/first-write) creates a separate, unique testnet atom and reads your position after a deposit.
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains the separate transaction lifecycle.

Sources: [Getting started](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/getting-started.md), [golden anchor tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/__tests__/anchor.test.ts).

# Versions and release status

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/versions

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

**V2 is a generation, not a package semver.** It covers the packages in the release manifest and Intuition Core. Each npm package has its own version. **V1** covers the `intuition-ts` packages and `intuition-rs` services; those docs remain available at [V1](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1).

The documented package release is published and stable. Install the exact versions below and retain your lockfile. The [release manifest](https://docs.intuition.systems/intuition-release.json) records package versions, entry points, peers, engines, registry integrity, and immutable source provenance.
