## Core source

Core is a repository to fork, clone, build, and run. These docs pin [Core source revision `a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420`](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/README.md). That identifies source code; it does not name an npm distribution or attest to a published container image.

[Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) contains the source setup path. Default startup does not ingest chain events; indexing is an explicitly configured profile. Package installation, Core startup, and chain indexing are separate steps.

## Verified install hazards

At the 2026-11-17 registry check, `@0xintuition/sdk@alpha` selected `4.0.0-alpha.0`, and `@0xintuition/protocol@alpha` selected `3.0.0-alpha.0`, both superseded by the documented pins. Also, `@0xintuition/protocol@3` and `^3.0.0-alpha.0` resolve to the older stable `3.0.0` release. Those selectors do not select the V2 protocol pin. Dist-tags move; prefer exact versions.

The checked `latest` tags match the documented pins. An untagged install still follows a moving tag, so it is unsuitable for preserving a V1 dependency set or reproducing this documentation later.

## Upgrading

Use [Migrate from V1](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1) for breaking changes and identity preservation. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) separates package peers, example runtime pins, contract artifacts, and Core requirements.

Source: [Package release policy](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/release.md).

# Intuition developer docs

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs

Intuition is an identity and knowledge graph protocol. Its packages help applications identify entities consistently, connect them with explicit relationships, and prepare actions through which people signal what they trust.

An **atom** stores a chosen representation as bytes. Its **atom ID** identifies those exact bytes. An **Intuition Identifier (IID)** names the represented entity; the same IID can appear in different representations. A **triple** connects a subject, predicate, and object in that order.

## Choose your path

| I want to… | Start here | Then build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build an application | [Derive an atom ID offline](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart) | [A music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog) with explicit recording, artist, and album relationships |
| Build with agents | [Read the agent contract](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/agents) | [Review action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) before a human authorizes execution |
| Run Core | [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core) | Fork, pin, build, and run the source to own graph storage and reads |
| Extend processing | [Classify and enrich inputs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) | [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin) for your domain |

You can build identities and triples offline before choosing a wallet or backend. Processing, persistence, protocol submission, and indexing each have their own lifecycle; [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits) explains the boundaries.

## Explore the documentation

- [Concepts](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts) introduces representations, directed relationships, and protocol writes.
- [Build guides](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build) cover tasks from modeling an identity to verifying a write.
- [Worked examples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples) walk through creation forms, identity links, React integration, and graph queries.
- [Packages](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages) covers every published library; the [SDK reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk) lists action signatures.
- [Install agent skills](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/agents/skills) for contract-level guidance, or [get help](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/community).

## Versions and source

**V2 names a generation**, covering the packages in the [release manifest](https://docs.intuition.systems/intuition-release.json) and Intuition Core. The packages are published as stable npm releases; each example uses exact pins. See [versions and release status](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/versions).

Core is a source application you fork, build, and run. These docs describe [Core source at the pinned revision](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/README.md). The source pin identifies code, rather than an npm distribution or a released container image. The default source stack requires its indexing profile and chain configuration to start chain ingestion.

The [V1 documentation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1) covers the `intuition-ts` packages and `intuition-rs` services. For agents, use the [V1 documentation index](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/v1/llms.txt). Start with [Migrate from V1](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1) when moving an integration.

Source: [Package concepts and application patterns](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/README.md#core-concepts).

## Runtime requirements

Packages are ESM-only: use named imports and set `"type": "module"` for Node applications. The manifest lists the engines and peers declared by each published package. The documentation's checks use an isolated dependency tree under `examples/v2`; V1 examples use separate V1 dependencies.

| Surface | Requirements or exact documentation pins |
| --- | --- |
| Direct TypeScript quickstart | Node 22.18 or newer |
| Example compiler | TypeScript 5.9.3; strict application checking, library declaration checking skipped |
| Contract clients | viem 2.31.4 in the checked examples; satisfy each package's declared peers |
| React example environment | React and React DOM 19.1.0; wagmi 2.15.4; TanStack Query 5.90.2 |
| Example type packages | Node types 22.20.5; React types 19.1.10; React DOM types 19.1.11 |
| Parser remote inspection | Node-compatible DNS/HTTP transport, Fetch, and Web Streams; choose runtime-compatible entry points |
| Classification and enrichment | Explicit plugins, provider configuration, credentials where needed, and cache policy |
| Core source workflow | Git, Bun 1.3.11, Node 20 or newer, Docker Compose v2 with a running Docker daemon, and curl |

The React package declares React 18+, wagmi 2+, TanStack Query 5+, viem 2, and the manifest's protocol/deployments package lines as peers. Keep your application's React and renderer versions aligned. Provider secrets belong on a backend; local parsing does not imply that remote enrichment works without network access.

## Contract artifacts and deployments

The package artifacts come from `@0xintuition/contracts-v2@1.1.0-alpha.1` and `@0xintuition/contracts-v2-periphery@1.1.0-alpha.0`. Their versioning is separate from the stable library release. [Artifact provenance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/contract-artifacts.md) verifies bundled interfaces and bytecode; it does not deploy or upgrade a contract.

Select addresses and check the implementation on your target chain before enabling URI creation, payable multicall, dynamic-fee, or on-behalf-of operations. The published deployment catalog withholds a TrustSwapAndBridgeRouter address; its lookup throws. See [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments) and [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol).

Ordinary React atom-creation hooks use `createAtoms`. For companion URI registration, use the explicit URI-aware protocol operation and your own transaction flow.

## Core source and package parity

Core source: [a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/README.md). Fork and build that revision following [Query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). The source revision does not imply an npm installation of Core or equivalence with a released image.

At this source revision, [Core's committed lockfile](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-core/blob/a402f880600f92969dc8fb013ca0f69fc9a02420/bun.lock) resolves 17 manifest packages, all at their documented versions. SDK, CLI, React, and periphery are absent from its resolved package graph; absence is not a version mismatch. Separately versioned contract artifacts and Core workspace packages are outside that comparison.

The default stack starts Query API and processing services; it does not start chain ingestion without the indexing profile and chain configuration. API liveness alone does not prove that events have been indexed or external providers have enriched a record.

# Configuration and URI limits

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/configuration

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

Read configuration from the intended MultiVault on the intended chain. A quote based on an earlier block can change before creation.

| Getter | What to read |
| --- | --- |
| `getGeneralConfig()` | `atomDataMaxLength` limits the atom payload in bytes. `minDeposit` is a native asset amount and `minShare` is the share seed for vault creation. `feeDenominator` is the denominator for configured fee rates. |
| `getAtomConfig()` | `atomCreationProtocolFee` is the flat creation fee in native wei. `atomWalletDepositFee` is a rate applied to deposits. |
| `getAtomCost()` | Returns the static cost per atom. The implementation adds the creation fee and one `minShare` seed under its 1:1 default-curve assumption. |
| `getTripleCost()` | Returns the static cost per triple. This includes the triple creation fee and two seeds for the triple and its counter. |
| `getVaultFees()` | Returns `entryFee`, `exitFee`, and `protocolFee` as numerators over `feeDenominator`. |
| `getBondingCurveConfig()` | Returns the curve registry and `defaultCurveId`. |

To estimate a creation that also buys shares, use `previewAtomCreate(termId, assets)` or `previewTripleCreate(subjectId, predicateId, objectId, assets)`. Each returns shares, the asset base used to calculate rate fees, and net assets credited after fees. A static creation cost alone cannot tell you how many shares the creator will receive.

## Check URI inputs

`getAtomUriConfig()` returns two effective limits in order, `maxUriCount` per atom and `maxUriLength` in bytes per URI. The getter applies the implementation's defaults if storage is unset. The timelock can update the limits. Count encoded bytes when validating text, since a character may occupy several bytes.

For a creation with two atoms, supply two URI lists in the same order as the payloads. An empty list attaches no context to that atom. MultiVault emits opaque URI bytes for a nonempty list. It does not fetch a resource, validate its contents, or store its bytes as part of the atom's identity.

The protocol package exposes `multiVaultGetAtomCost` and `multiVaultGetAtomUriConfig` for these reads. [Configuration structures](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/IMultiVaultCore.sol) · [Cost calculations](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVaultCore.sol) · [Effective URI limits](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/MultiVault.sol) · [URI validation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol)

## Match the implementation

The pinned contract repository lists a different mainnet WrappedTrust address in its deployment notes. The table above follows the V2 package used by its lookup helpers. Check the intended deployment before carrying an address over from an older integration. [Contract repository deployment notes](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/deployments.md)

Core lookup helpers accept `AddressOverrides` keyed by contract name and chain ID for historical or custom deployments. An override selects the requested address. For a historical read, also select the block and ABI appropriate to that deployment. The core v1.1.0 ABI describes the published artifact. The deployments package cautions that new functions require the corresponding mainnet upgrade. Confirm implementation compatibility for the network and block before relying on a new method.

[Core addresses](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/src/deployments.ts) · [Periphery and bridge addresses](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/src/periphery-deployments.ts) · [Address overrides](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/src/address-overrides.ts) · [Compatibility notes](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/README.md)

# Events and errors

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/events-and-errors

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

Filter receipt logs by the emitting contract address before decoding them. Indexed fields can be filtered as topics. The remaining fields come from the log data. For example, a FeeProxy deposit can produce both a MultiVault deposit event and a FeeProxy routing event in one receipt.

## Decode events

The fields in each row are in ABI order. For these events the indexed fields come first.

| Contract and event | Indexed fields, in order | Data fields, in order |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MultiVault `AtomCreated` | `creator`, `termId` | `atomData`, `atomWallet` |
| MultiVault `AtomContextRegistered` | `termId`, `registrant` | `uris` |
| MultiVault `TripleCreated` | `creator`, `termId` | `subjectId`, `predicateId`, `objectId` |
| MultiVault `Deposited` | `sender`, `receiver`, `termId` | `curveId`, `assets`, `assetsAfterFees`, `shares`, `receiverSharesAfter`, `vaultType` |
| MultiVault `Redeemed` | `sender`, `account`, `termId` | `curveId`, `shares`, `accountSharesAfter`, `assetsAfterFees`, `totalFees`, `vaultType` |
| TrustBonding `RewardsClaimed` | `user`, `recipient` | `amount` |

Group atom context with the atom using its `termId`. An empty URI list produces no context event. For a vault position, keep its `termId` and `curveId` together. The final share balance in a deposit or redemption event belongs to the named holder. In a rewards claim, the user earned the reward and the recipient received the transfer.

## Interpret a revert

A custom error has a selector and, for errors that take arguments, ABI-encoded data. Decode it against the implementation and call path you used.

| Error | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| `MultiVault_AtomExists(bytes atomData)` | The bytes already identify an existing atom. Reuse that ID when referring to it. |
| `MultiVault_AtomUriCountExceeded()`, `MultiVault_AtomUriLengthExceeded()` | Compare each atom's URI list with the [current limits](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/configuration). |
| `MultiVault_SlippageExceeded()` | Compare the deposit or redemption result with the minimum output on the request. |
| `FeeProxy_BpsExceedsCallerGuard(uint256 configured, uint256 callerMax)` | The affiliate's rate exceeds the caller's maximum. Refresh the quote before deciding whether to proceed. |
| `TrustBonding_RewardsAlreadyClaimedForEpoch()` | Check the caller's claim history for the previous epoch. |

A MultiVault call can also propagate an error from a curve or its registry, such as `BondingCurveRegistry_InvalidCurveId()`. Use `MultiVaultWithRevertsAbi` to decode those cases. The packages library constructs this composite by adding distinct external error signatures to `MultiVaultAbi`. It keeps the published MultiVault ABI available separately.

[MultiVault events](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/IMultiVault.sol) · [FeeProxy errors](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/IFeeProxy.sol) · [TrustBonding events and errors](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/ITrustBonding.sol) · [Composite ABI source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/deployments/src/abis/multivault-reverts-abi.ts)

# FeeProxy

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/fee-proxy

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

FeeProxy lets an affiliate charge a disclosed fee on a MultiVault deposit or creation. The Solidity contract ships in the core contracts artifact. The V2 periphery library provides FeeProxy helpers, and the SDK builds higher-level plans.

## Quote a route

`affiliateConfig(affiliate)` exposes the fee recipient and separate deposit and creation rates. `previewDepositFee(affiliate, grossAssets)` and `previewCreationFee(affiliate, grossAssets)` each return the affiliate fee and the assets available to forward. The fee equals `floor(grossAssets × bps / 10,000) + fixedFee`, in native wei.

For example, a hypothetical deposit of 10,000 wei at 50 basis points with a fixed fee of 3 wei gives the affiliate 53 wei and forwards 9,947 wei. That is the amount entering MultiVault before its own fees. For a batch, FeeProxy calculates one fee over the sum, allocates the forwarded amount in proportion to each gross amount, and assigns the rounding remainder to the last item.

| Operation | Execution requirements |
| --- | --- |
| `registerAffiliate(fees, feeRecipient)` | The calling address becomes the affiliate. It supplies exactly `registrationFee()`, a nonzero recipient, and fee settings within protocol caps. The affiliate can later call `updateAffiliateFees` and `updateFeeRecipient`. |
| `depositVia`, `depositBatchVia` | The receiver must approve FeeProxy for deposits in MultiVault. A receiver distinct from the caller must also approve that caller. Pass the share floor for the net deposit. |
| `createAtomsVia`, `createAtomsWithUrisVia`, `createTriplesVia` | The creator must approve FeeProxy for creation in MultiVault. The forwarded assets still have to cover the underlying creation costs. |

A preview only does fee arithmetic. A route requires an unpaused proxy and a registered, unpaused affiliate. FeeProxy checks the active side's protocol caps and the caller's `FeeGuard` fields, `maxFeeBps` and `maxFixedFee`. It rejects a fee equal to or larger than gross assets.

## Payments and refunds

After the MultiVault call succeeds, FeeProxy pays the affiliate's fee recipient. If that transfer fails, the routed call reverts. Excess native value beyond the declared gross amount goes back to the caller. If the caller cannot receive it, FeeProxy records a credit in `pendingRefund(user)`.

`claimRefund()` pays the caller its credit. `claimRefundTo(recipient)` sends the caller's credit to another payable address and rejects the zero address and FeeProxy itself. The SDK's `feeProxyCreateAtomsWithUrisEnvelope` includes a creation-fee quote and URI bounds for review before execution.

[FeeProxy implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/periphery/FeeProxy.sol) · [FeeProxy interface](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/IFeeProxy.sol) · [SDK plan](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/fee-proxy.ts)

# Contracts

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0

MultiVault records terms and manages vault positions. Applications can call it directly or route supported operations through FeeProxy. Bonding TRUST for epoch rewards uses a separate contract.

| Contract | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| [MultiVault](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/multivault) | Create atoms from bytes and triples from existing term IDs. Deposit native assets or redeem shares in the vault identified by a term and a curve. |
| [FeeProxy](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/fee-proxy) | Attribute a deposit or creation to a registered affiliate, pay the affiliate's fee, and forward the remaining assets to MultiVault. |
| [TrustBonding](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/trust-bonding) | Lock the configured token for voting power and claim eligible rewards for the previous epoch. |
| WrappedTrust | Convert native TRUST into a transferable token with allowances. A payable `deposit()` credits the caller one WTRUST base unit for each native base unit received. `withdraw(amount)` debits the wrapped balance and returns that amount of native currency to the caller. Both use 18 decimals. |

The V2 libraries expose the MultiVault v1.1.0 interface. The core artifact includes FeeProxy and WrappedTrust. The separate periphery artifact supplies the swap-and-bridge router. Before selecting a method, match the chain and contract address to an implementation that supports it. [Contract artifact provenance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/docs/contract-artifacts.md) · [WrappedTrust source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/WrappedTrust.sol)

## Integration references

- [Configuration and URI limits](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/configuration) lists the getters for creation costs, deposit parameters, and context lengths.
- [Deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/deployments) lists contract addresses by chain and asset.
- [Events and errors](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/events-and-errors) explains how to interpret logs and revert data.
- [Audits](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/audits) identifies the contract revisions covered by published assessments.

# MultiVault

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/multivault

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

An atom's input is a byte string. Its `termId` is the 32-byte ID derived from those bytes. A triple combines three existing term IDs in subject, predicate, object order. Vault operations take both a term ID and a curve ID, so keep both when displaying a balance.

## Create and look up terms

| Function | Inputs and result |
| --- | --- |
| `calculateAtomId(data)`, `isTermCreated(termId)` | Derive an ID, then check whether that term already exists. Calculating an ID requires no registration. |
| `createAtoms(data, assets)` | Create one atom per byte string with its corresponding native asset amount. A duplicate atom reverts. |
| `createAtomsWithUris(creator, data, assets, uris)` | Supply one URI list per atom at creation. Nonempty lists appear in `AtomContextRegistered`. These pointers are excluded from the ID and atom storage. Creating on behalf of another address requires its creation approval. |
| `createTriples(subjectIds, predicateIds, objectIds, assets)` | Supply parallel arrays of equal length. Each triple refers to three existing terms. |
| `getAtom(atomId)`, `getTriple(tripleId)` | Read the stored atom bytes or the three component IDs. These getters revert for a missing term. |

Use [configuration and URI limits](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/configuration) for creation costs and input bounds. For a batch creation the native call value must equal the sum of the asset amounts.

## Preview a vault operation

`previewDeposit(termId, curveId, assets)` returns expected shares and assets credited after fees. `getShares(account, termId, curveId)` reads a holder's balance. `redeem(receiver, termId, curveId, shares, minAssets)` burns shares subject to a minimum payout. Its preview, `previewRedeem(termId, curveId, shares)`, has no account argument. On a curve with account-specific fees, a holder's actual redemption can differ from this preview.

## Encode a deposit

Pass the intended share floor as `minShares`. The encoder below produces calldata offline. A payable deposit also needs a target contract and native call value in wei. A preview describes the state read at quote time. Use the confirmed receipt and the target contract's [events](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/events-and-errors) to determine the actual shares issued.

```ts
import { multiVaultDepositEncode } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import type { Address, Hex } from 'viem';

// Caller-supplied values must describe an existing term and chosen curve.
export function encodeDeposit(
  receiver: Address,
  termId: Hex,
  curveId: bigint,
  minShares: bigint,
) {
  return multiVaultDepositEncode(receiver, termId, curveId, minShares);
}
```

[MultiVault interface](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/IMultiVault.sol) · [Term getters](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/interfaces/IMultiVaultCore.sol) · [Creation implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/libraries/MultiVaultLib.sol) · [V2 protocol wrappers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/tree/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/src/core/multivault)

# TrustBonding

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/trust-bonding

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

TrustBonding locks a token balance for a chosen duration. The principal stays locked while its voting power declines toward zero as the unlock time approaches. Rewards use epoch-end voting power and protocol activity.

## Lock and withdraw

`create_lock(_value, _unlock_time)` takes a token amount in base units and a Unix timestamp in seconds. The escrow transfers the configured token from the caller, so the account needs that token and sufficient allowance. For a WrappedTrust position, the amount is in 18-decimal WTRUST units. The SDK's claim-and-restake plan includes separate wrapping and allowance steps when needed.

The contract rounds the requested unlock time down to a whole week and checks it against `MINTIME` and `MAXTIME`. An account can add principal with `increase_amount` or extend an active lock with `increase_unlock_time`. Under normal lock conditions, `withdraw()` returns the underlying principal after expiry. Read `getUserInfo(account)` for the lock end and bonded balance.

## Epochs and claims

| Question | Contract read |
| --- | --- |
| Which epoch is open? | `currentEpoch()` and `epochTimestampEnd(epoch)` identify the epoch and its closing timestamp. |
| What weight did this account contribute? | `userBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd(account, epoch)` gives the account's snapshot. Compare it with `totalBondedBalanceAtEpochEnd(epoch)`. |
| What can this account claim now? | `getUserCurrentClaimableRewards(account)` estimates the previous epoch's claim. `hasClaimedRewardsForEpoch(account, epoch)` checks claim history. |

System utilization determines the epoch emissions available for distribution. The account's fraction of total epoch-end voting power determines its raw share. Personal utilization adjusts that share. A claim also respects the remaining epoch budget.

`claimRewards(recipient)` claims for the caller and sends the reward to the specified nonzero recipient. During epoch 8, for example, it can claim epoch 7 once. There is no claim during epoch 0 and no parameter to claim an older missed epoch. A successful claim emits `RewardsClaimed(user, recipient, amount)`. The SDK exposes `trustBondingGetClaimActionState` for applications deciding whether to show the claim action.

[TrustBonding implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/protocol/emissions/TrustBonding.sol) · [Lock accounting](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-contracts-v2/blob/82cfcdb832c100fd2e53ee3f474289ae14cc6020/src/external/curve/VotingEscrow.sol) · [Protocol wrappers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/tree/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/src/core/trustbonding) · [SDK actions](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/trust-bonding.ts)

# Testnet faucet

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/networks/faucet

The Intuition testnet uses **tTRUST** for gas and native call value. Select chain ID `13579` and copy the public receiving address you want to fund. [Testnet network settings](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/networks)

Open the [Intuition testnet hub](https://testnet.hub.intuition.systems/) and follow its current faucet instructions. Use the amount and eligibility requirements shown there.

After a transfer is confirmed, look up the receiving address in the [testnet explorer](https://testnet.explorer.intuition.systems). If you see a zero balance, check the network and receiving address against the faucet request. Mainnet TRUST balances are tracked separately.

# Networks

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/networks

Select the Intuition chain that holds the state you want to read. The deployments package exports `intuitionMainnet` and `intuitionTestnet` as viem chain definitions. These are the defaults recorded in that package.

| Setting | Intuition mainnet | Intuition testnet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chain ID | `1155` | `13579` |
| Native currency | TRUST, 18 decimals | tTRUST, 18 decimals |
| HTTP RPC | `https://rpc.intuition.systems/http` | `https://testnet.rpc.intuition.systems/http` |

| Block explorer | [Mainnet explorer](https://explorer.intuition.systems) | [Testnet explorer](https://testnet.explorer.intuition.systems) |

Use the explorer for the same chain as the transaction or address. Base (8453) and Base Sepolia (84532) appear in the [deployment tables](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/contracts/deployments) for associated contracts. Use the Intuition chain IDs above for Intuition vault operations.

The [testnet faucet](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/networks/faucet) supplies the entry point for requesting test currency. For application queries against an indexed graph, use the [Query API on your own Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). # @0xintuition/atom-classification

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0

## What it's for

A plugin engine that classifies input and resolves canonical envelopes in client-only, progressive, or server-only modes. It executes classification logic; the classifications package owns the canonical entity specifications.

## When to use it

Use it to turn an input into typed identity data before enrichment or a creation decision. Select plugins explicitly: creating an engine neither installs every provider nor persists output. Use server-compatible plugins for credentialed providers; a provider factory's existence does not guarantee a network response.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-classification@0.1.0
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or Bun for server execution. A client engine needs client-compatible plugins; provider requests require a suitable transport.

## Entry points

| --- | --- |
| `.` | Engines, plugin factories, canonical result contracts, and type registry |
| `./ai` | Optional server AI fallback adapter |
| `./cache` | Resolver cache contracts and adapters |
| `./client` | Client engine factory |
| `./engine` | Shared classification engine |
| `./plugin-factories` | Built-in plugin factories |
| `./plugins` | Plugin manifests, types, and validation |
| `./plugins/amazon` | Amazon plugin and adapters |

| `./plugins/instagram` | Instagram plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/isbn` | ISBN plugin |
| `./plugins/lexical` | Opt-in lexical classification |
| `./plugins/plain-text` | Generic Thing fallback for text |
| `./plugins/spotify` | Spotify plugin and adapters |
| `./plugins/tiktok` | TikTok plugin |
| `./plugins/tmdb` | TMDB plugin |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment), [atom-parser](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser), [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [iid-ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder), [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), [pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime), [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates), [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives), and [schema-org](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org). Peer dependencies: none. `zod` is an additional ordinary dependency in the package manifest.

Classification consumes enrichment helpers; enrichment does not depend on this engine. Your host owns credentials, persistent storage, cache selection, and request policy.

## @0xintuition/atom-classification - Example

An explicit pair of local plugins produces a generic Thing for fixed text. An empty plugin set demonstrates the unmatched-text fallback; the invalid request demonstrates boundary failure without a provider call.

```ts
import {
  classifyOutcome,
  createClientEngine,
  createPlainTextPlugin,
  createTypeProfilesPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-classification';

const engine = createClientEngine({
  plugins: [createTypeProfilesPlugin(), createPlainTextPlugin()],
  now: () => new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'),
});
export const classified = await engine.classify({
  input: 'A synthetic catalog idea',
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'package-reference',
});
console.log(classified.resolved?.publishable[0]?.type);

// Unmatched text remains a candidate Thing, not a verified identity.
export const unmatched = await createClientEngine({ plugins: [] }).classify({
  input: 'Unmatched synthetic catalog label',
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'unmatched-fixture',
});
console.log(unmatched.resolved?.fallbackUsed);

export const invalidRequest = await classifyOutcome(engine, {
  input: '',
  mode: 'client-only',
  classificationSessionId: 'invalid-fixture',
});
console.log(invalidRequest.kind);
```

Read `resolved.classifications` for canonical envelopes and `resolved.publishable` for the identity-safe projection. Identity fields are eligible by default, approved rich fields depend on source policy, and volatile fields are excluded. `resolved.atoms` is a compatibility projection. These are candidate payloads, not proof of an on-chain atom.

A completed response's `ok: true` does not promise full resolution: inspect `status` (`placeholder`, `partial`, or `complete`), optional `resolved`, and `resolverErrors`. Unmatched text falls back to a generic Thing with `resolved.fallbackUsed: true`; that candidate is not a verified entity identity. Invalid requests reject `classify`; `classifyOutcome` captures that rejection as an outcome. Cancellation and resolver deadlines are separate from a successful partial result.

External plugins implement `AtomClassificationPlugin` with a validated manifest, classifiers, and resolvers. Register emitted types, satisfy `dependsOn`, and explicitly set a local resolver's `executionMode: 'deterministic'` when it should run under client-only policy. An omitted mode defaults to server enrichment. Follow [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin) for the complete contract and Core composition boundary.

## Related concepts

- [Atom classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-classification)

See also [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

# @0xintuition/atom-enrichment

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Run provider plugins against classified input and collect typed artifacts with provenance. Extraction can turn those artifacts into classification fields; neither operation changes an existing atom's identity bytes.

## When to use it

Use it when you need provider metadata, a selected provider plan, or normalized fields with missing-field diagnostics. Use the IID registry to plan providers before execution. A plan is not a completed lookup, and an artifact is not evidence that every required classification field was extracted.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-enrichment@0.1.0
```

Use typed ESM on Node 20+ or Bun. Real providers may require HTTP access, credentials, and server-compatible execution; inject those deliberately.

## Entry points

All public modules

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Engine, providers, registries, presets, handoff, and public types |
| `./types` | Inputs, artifacts, results, and request schemas |
| `./handoff` | Adapt classification results into enrichment input |
| `./provider-data` | Normalized provider payload types |
| `./plugins` | Plugin manifests, contracts, and validation |
| `./providers` | Provider factories and request helpers |
| `./presets` | Provider bundles and explicit environment mapping |
| `./engine` | Enrichment execution engine |
| `./plugin-registry` | Register and resolve plugins |
| `./cache` | Cache contracts and memory or HTTP adapters |
| `./testing` | Deterministic fixtures and plugin conformance helpers |
| `./classifications` | Provider artifact classification registry |
| `./classifications/defaults` | Built-in artifact definitions |
| `./classifications/registry` | Artifact registration and validation |
| `./classifications/schemas` | Artifact payload schemas |
| `./provider-external-data` | External provider response schemas |
| `./provider-plan` | Match desired providers against installed capabilities |
| `./slug-aliases` | Canonicalize provider slug aliases |
| `./extraction` | Extract normalized classification fields and provenance |
| `./data-resolved-schema` | Normalized resolved-data boundary |
| `./spotify-client` | Shared Spotify client |
| `./tmdb-request-observer` | Observe TMDB requests |
| `./provider-fetch` | Provider transport helpers |
| `./plugin-api` | Public plugin authoring API |
| `./outcome` | Promise outcome wrapper for enrichment |
| `./adapters/upstash` | Explicit HTTP cache adapter |
| `./ssrf` | Pinned transport and destination policy helpers |
| `./identifier-rung-projection` | Project admissible identifier rungs |
| `./url-hygiene` | URL normalization policy |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [iid-ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder), [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), [pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), and [schema-org](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org). Peer dependencies: none. `zod` is an additional ordinary dependency in the package manifest.

Canonical entity requirements belong to classifications. This package's artifact registry validates provider payloads. `toClassifiedAtomInput` returns usable input or `null`; handle that boundary before calling `enrich`. `createIdentifierProviderPlan` records scheduled, unavailable, and unsupported providers instead of silently treating a missing plugin as completed work.

## @0xintuition/atom-enrichment - Example

These two synthetic plugins exercise the real engine without network access. One returns a valid Open Graph artifact; the other rejects. The example preserves the successful artifact alongside the failure.

```ts
import {
  createEnrichmentEngine,
  type EnrichmentPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-enrichment';

// Synthetic fixtures: no HTTP provider, credentials, or fetched page.
const fixture: EnrichmentPlugin = {
  id: 'catalog-fixture',
  version: '1.0.0',
  runtime: 'universal',
  artifactTypes: ['opengraph'],
  supports: (request) => request.input.atomType === 'thing',
  enrich: async (_request, { now }) => [
    {
      artifact_type: 'opengraph',
      data: { title: 'Synthetic catalog' },
      meta: {
        pluginId: 'catalog-fixture',
        provider: 'offline-fixture',
        fetchedAt: now(),
      },
    },
  ],
};
const unavailable: EnrichmentPlugin = {
  ...fixture,
  id: 'unavailable-fixture',
  enrich: async () => {
    throw new Error('Fixture provider unavailable');
  },
};

const engine = createEnrichmentEngine({
  plugins: [fixture, unavailable],
  now: () => '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',
});
export const enriched = await engine.enrich({
  runtime: 'server',
  input: {
    atomType: 'thing',
    jsonLd: { '@context': 'https://schema.org/', '@type': 'Thing' },
    source: {
      classificationEngine: 'offline-fixture',
      classifiedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',
    },
  },
});
console.log(enriched.status, enriched.artifacts.length, enriched.errors.length);
```

The result is `partial` with one artifact and one error. Inspect `status`, `artifacts`, `errors`, `skipped`, and `timings`; do not discard useful artifacts because a provider failed. Invalid request schemas can still reject before provider execution. Runtime mismatches and unsupported inputs can produce skipped providers.

Preserve each artifact's `meta.pluginId`, `provider`, `fetchedAt`, and optional `sourceUrl`. Here the provider is explicitly an offline fixture, not a scraped page. For real providers, select a small preset and supply approved transports, credentials, timeouts, and cache policy. A keyless service can still make network calls. Spotify's URL-derived fallback, for example, is distinct from a credentialed Web API artifact.

`extractClassificationFields` reports values, provenance, missing required fields, and dropped-field reasons; it may perform additional lookups. The pinned MusicBrainz artifact does not automatically supply extracted music-recording fields. The [processing guide](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich) demonstrates that partial boundary with a fixed fixture. Your application owns retries, queues, persistence, and access control.

## Related concepts

- [Enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/enrichment)

See also [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/README.md), [provider payload documentation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/docs/README.md), [plugin contract](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/src/plugins.ts), and [partial-result tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-enrichment/__tests__/engine.integration.test.ts).

# @0xintuition/atom-parser

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Detect and normalize IIDs, text, JSON objects and arrays, URLs, IPFS URIs, addresses, names, and ISBNs into a `ParseResult`. Parsing identifies the input's shape; it does not resolve the entity, assign a canonical classification, or create an atom on-chain.

## When to use it

Use local detection before choosing a classification plugin or asking a reader to confirm an input. Set `remoteFetch: false` for local processing. URL and IPFS inspection is enabled by default, so a parser call is not inherently offline.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-parser@0.1.0
```

Use ESM with Node 22+ or Bun for the complete parser workflow.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Parser, local detection, IID candidates, remote inspection, and types |
| `./types` | Parse results, options, remote outcomes, and `ParseError` |
| `./detect` | Local input detection |
| `./remote` | Bounded remote inspection and content detection |
| `./parse` | `parseAtom` entry point |
| `./iid` | Inspect IID-shaped candidates |
| `./ssrf` | Destination checks and pinned HTTP transport contracts |
| `./testing/dns` | Inject DNS behavior for isolated tests |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependency: [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid). Peer dependencies: none. The runtime dependency graph lists Intuition packages; the package manifest additionally declares `multiformats` and `viem` as ordinary dependencies.

Pass parsed evidence into an explicitly configured [classification engine](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification). A structured-document candidate can contain schema types and URL hints, but those hints are not a persisted classification.

## @0xintuition/atom-parser - Example

This bounded fixed URL is normalized without fetching a page. Narrow on `kind` before reading variant-specific fields.

```ts
import { parseAtom, ParseError } from '@0xintuition/atom-parser';

export const parsed = await parseAtom('https://example.com/catalog', {
  remoteFetch: false,
  maxInputBytes: 1024,
});
if (parsed.kind === 'url') {
  console.log(parsed.canonicalUrl, parsed.remote === undefined);
}

try {
  await parseAtom('', { remoteFetch: false });
} catch (error) {
  if (!(error instanceof ParseError)) throw error;
  console.log(error.code);
}
```

The URL has no `remote` result, and empty input throws `ParseError` with code `EMPTY_INPUT`. Other input errors include `INPUT_TOO_LARGE` and invalid gateway configuration. `parseIidCandidate` returns `undefined` for non-IID input; an invalid IID-shaped candidate has `valid: false`, a reason, and no canonical IID. Detection is not proof that an identifier belongs to a particular entity.

Default limits are 16,384 input bytes, three redirects, 1 MiB response bytes, and 256 KiB inspected bytes. The request deadline is five seconds, or eight for IPFS; `connectTimeoutMs` does not enforce a separate connection deadline. IPFS inspection requires an explicit gateway. Remote outcomes include success, skipped, denied, timeout, error, oversized, and redirect-limit exhaustion; inspect warnings and the outcome before using remote evidence.

The pinned Node transport resolves and vets destinations, pins the approved address, and repeats checks on redirects. The older transport paragraph in the README does not describe this implementation; the linked source and transport test do. A custom transport must preserve the pinned-request contract, and your host still owns egress controls.

## Related concepts

- [Atom parsing](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-parsing)

See also [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/README.md), [public parser](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/src/parse.ts), and [pinned-transport test](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-parser/__tests__/pinned-transport.test.ts).

# @0xintuition/atom-runtime

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-runtime

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0

## What it's for

A server composition layer for classification and enrichment engines, shared caches, presets, and configuration fingerprints. It does not provide graph storage, worker scheduling, or an automatically offline pipeline.

## When to use it

Use one runtime per intended configuration and application lifecycle to reuse engines and caches. Use the individual parser, classification, or enrichment packages for a single stage. Supplying no graph database removes a persistence prerequisite; it does not prevent selected providers from making requests.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/atom-runtime@0.1.0
```

Use ESM and Promises on Node 20 or newer.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Runtime/cache factories, configuration, presets, and consumer adapters |
| `./presets` | Classification plugins, enrichment factories, and default scopes |
| `./fingerprint` | Compute configuration identity |
| `./consumers` | Atom-services and local application composition adapters |
| `./config` | Resolve configuration and select processing environment keys |
| `./adapters/upstash` | Explicit HTTP cache integration |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [atom-classification](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-classification), [atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment), [atom-parser](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-parser), [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), and [pipeline-runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime). Peer dependencies: none. `zod` is an additional ordinary dependency in the package manifest.

Your host supplies transport, credentials, clock, logging, and persistent storage. Cache providers are `none`, `memory`, and `upstash`; inspect `cacheProvider` and `warnings` after resolution. Consumer adapters have their own cache defaults and fallback policies.

## @0xintuition/atom-runtime - Example

This runtime selects only deterministic text classifiers, an empty default enrichment set, a fixed clock, and memory caching. It performs one classification and proves that repeated engine lookup returns the same instance.

```ts
import {
  createPlainTextPlugin,
  createTypeProfilesPlugin,
} from '@0xintuition/atom-classification';
import { createProcessingRuntime } from '@0xintuition/atom-runtime';

export const runtime = createProcessingRuntime({
  config: { env: {}, cache: { provider: 'memory', memoryMaxEntries: 100 } },
  runtime: { now: () => '2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' },
  overrides: {
    classification: [createTypeProfilesPlugin(), createPlainTextPlugin()],
    enrichment: { default: [] },
  },
});
try {
  const engine = runtime.classification.engine();
  const result = await engine.classify({
    input: 'A synthetic catalog idea',
    mode: 'client-only',
    classificationSessionId: 'runtime-reference',
  });
  console.log(engine === runtime.classification.engine());
  console.log(result.resolved?.publishable[0]?.type);
  console.log(runtime.cacheProvider, runtime.warnings);
} finally {
  runtime.dispose();
}
```

`runtime.fetch` in the composition options configures HTTP cache access; it is not a universal override for provider requests. Configure provider transports in their own options, or inject selected plugins as shown. Enrichment engines are memoized by preset and identity capability, and their published plugin registries are immutable. Change plugin selection when constructing the runtime.

Fingerprints include secret presence rather than secret values. They identify configuration, not the resulting entity or a persisted atom. Pass an explicit `env` map; only named `FromEnv` helpers read the process environment when called.

After `dispose()`, new engine lookups throw. Disposal does not cancel requests already in flight or revoke engine references already obtained. Supply and abort request signals before disposing when shutting down active work. The host owns retries and queues.

## Related concepts

- [Atom runtime and pipelines](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime)

See also [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits), [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich), [Write a classification plugin](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/core/classification-plugin).

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/README.md), [runtime implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/src/runtime.ts), and [public runtime tests](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/atom-runtime/__tests__/public-runtime.test.ts).

# @0xintuition/classifications

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Canonical classification specifications define entity types, recommended fields, identity ladders, and relationship metadata. Creation Profiles package the field labels, schema provenance, predicate IDs, and allowed object targets needed to model a creation form.

## When to use it

Use `/creation/<slug>` for a known creation flow; use root registry helpers for dynamic discovery and validation. A classification slug (`music-recording`), schema type (`MusicRecording`), and display label are different values. Use [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) for identifier-first atom bytes and IDs; filling a field or selecting a relationship never submits a transaction or creates an edge.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/classifications@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath        | Purpose                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`            | Classification discovery, field validation, atom-data builders, identity derivation, and metadata predicate matrix. |
| `./*`          | Generated classification specs by slug, such as `/music-recording`.                                                 |
| `./creation`   | Generated Creation Profile registry.                                                                                |
| `./creation/*` | One generated Creation Profile by slug, such as `/creation/music-recording`.                                        |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/classifications - Example

```ts
import {
  buildAtomData,
  validateClassificationValues,
} from '@0xintuition/classifications';
import { musicRecordingCreationProfile } from '@0xintuition/classifications/creation/music-recording';

const recordingValues = {
  name: 'Example recording',
  byArtist: 'Example artist',
};
const issues = validateClassificationValues('music-recording', recordingValues);
if (issues.length > 0) {
  throw new Error(issues.map((issue) => issue.message).join('; '));
}
const recordingData = buildAtomData('music-recording', recordingValues);
const artistRelationship = musicRecordingCreationProfile.relationships.find(
  (relationship) => relationship.predicate.key === 'byArtist',
);
console.log({
  data: recordingData,
  fields: musicRecordingCreationProfile.fields.map((field) => field.key),
  artistTargets: artistRelationship?.expectedObjects,
});
```

These are synthetic descriptive values. `recordingData` contains a `byArtist` string; a graph assertion still needs a separate subject → predicate → object triple. `artistRelationship.expectedObjects` suggests `music-group` or `person` targets; it does not resolve an artist or create that target.

`validateClassificationValues` returns field issues for known classifications; an unknown slug throws. `buildAtomData` throws on invalid values. `getClassificationByReference` resolves trimmed, case-insensitive references through ordered lookup tiers; an ambiguous tier falls through and an unresolved reference returns `undefined`. A matching label is not evidence that two real-world entities are identical.

## Related concepts

- [Classifications and Creation Profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/classifications)

See also [Build creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles), [music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/README.md).

[Creation Profile types](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/creation-profile.ts) · [Recording profile](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/generated/creation/music-recording.ts) · [Validation and serialization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/classifications/src/atom-data.ts).

# @0xintuition/cli

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/cli

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0

## What it's for

An `intuition` executable for encoder discovery and deterministic calldata generation, plus library exports for encoders and compatibility plan aliases. It does not own public clients, wallets, simulation, or submission.

## When to use it

Use it when a script or agent needs to discover an encoder or prepare a specific contract call. Use [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) for new action-envelope integrations. The executable has no plan command; its library's deprecated `build*Plan` aliases delegate to SDK-owned envelope builders.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/cli@0.1.0
```

Use Node 20+ and ESM for library imports. The executable bundles its protocol, periphery, and SDK code; published types still reference those dependency APIs.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Calldata encoders, envelope schemas, and deprecated plan aliases |

The `intuition` binary is a package executable, not an additional import subpath.

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery), [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol), and [sdk](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk). Peer dependencies: none. `viem` is an ordinary runtime dependency in the package manifest.

An external executor owns deployment compatibility, fresh reads, simulation, approval, and signing. Envelope metadata identifies the SDK as the builder even when called through a deprecated CLI alias.

## @0xintuition/cli - Example

Discover core MultiVault write encoders using the exact package pin:

```sh
npx @0xintuition/cli@0.1.0 encoders list --surface core --contract multivault --kind write --json
```

The command prints the encoder catalog and does not submit a transaction. For `encode`, `--args` must be a JSON array; pass ABI integers as decimal strings to avoid JavaScript number precision loss. Invalid command arguments or unsupported encoders fail instead of producing a usable call.

Target support is contract-specific. Core targets cover the relevant Intuition mainnet/testnet and Base/Base Sepolia contracts; this does not make every contract available on every chain. Canonical bridge targets are mainnet-only, and the router lookup throws while a compatible redeployment is absent from the pinned map. FeeProxy and dynamic-fee curve intents carry explicit addresses and accept Intuition mainnet or testnet; accepting a chain ID does not prove deployment capability.

Review [action plans](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) before handing encoded output to an executor. Encoding is neither execution authorization nor a successful simulation.

## Related concepts

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) separates preparation, approval, and execution.

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/cli/README.md), [network support matrix](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/cli/docs/network-support-matrix.md), and [executable source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/tree/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/cli/src/bin).

# @0xintuition/curves

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Pure math for linear, progressive, and offset-progressive curves, fee calculations, and dynamic-fee distributions. It computes from supplied state and parameters without RPC, wallets, or deployment selection.

## When to use it

Use it for local previews or calculations from a known state snapshot. Use [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) or [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) when you need live contract state. A mathematically valid quote does not prove that a deployment uses those parameters or will execute at that price.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/curves@0.1.0
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser with BigInt support.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Curve factories, conversions, previews, fees, distributions, math, and types |

Source module names such as `linear-curve` and `fees` are not public import subpaths.

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: none. Peer dependencies: none.

The SDK consumes these calculations. Supply compatible current curve configuration, fees, and state from the intended contract; pure math has no way to establish their provenance.

## @0xintuition/curves - Example

This synthetic state has three asset base units and two share base units. Integer deposit conversion rounds down, while minting an exact number of shares rounds the required assets up.

```ts
import { createLinearCurve, type CurveState } from '@0xintuition/curves';

const curve = createLinearCurve();
const state: CurveState = { totalAssets: 3n, totalShares: 2n };
export const preview = {
  depositShares: curve.previewDeposit(2n, state),
  mintAssets: curve.previewMint(2n, state),
};
console.log(preview); // 1n share for a deposit; 3n assets to mint 2n shares.
```

Use `bigint` base units throughout. The example's `2n` means two base units, not two TRUST. `WAD` is the package's fixed-point scale of 10 to the power of 18; fee rates use the supplied denominator or the specific helper's basis-point contract. Avoid converting large values through JavaScript `number`.

Linear deposit and redeem previews round down; mint and withdraw previews round up. Invalid states can throw, such as nonzero shares with zero assets when converting assets to shares. These local previews exclude transaction gas and any fees you have not explicitly included.

Fee helpers include exact-net gross-up for atom/triple creation and deposits. The bounded search returns a quote achieving the requested net amount, but independently rounded fees can permit multiple solutions, so it does not promise the smallest gross debit. Dynamic-fee helpers require current lots, tier occupancy, configuration, and accumulators as applicable; the top tier's unbounded edge and width are `null`.

## Related concepts

- [Bonding curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves)
- [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards)

See also [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits).

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/README.md), [linear math](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/linear-curve.ts), and [fee helpers](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/fees.ts).

# @0xintuition/deployments

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The shared source of contract ABIs, deployment addresses, chain definitions, and bytecode consumed by the protocol packages. Address selection is a local lookup; it does not query or deploy a contract.

## When to use it

Use it when you need metadata without the protocol wrapper layer. Use [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) for contract operations. A configured address proves that the pinned map contains an entry, not that its live implementation has a particular capability.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Contract ABIs, address maps, chain definitions, and lookup helpers |
| `./bytecode` | Separate contract bytecode exports |

Bytecode stays off the root entry point so address and ABI consumers need not include it.

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: none. Peer dependency: `viem ^2.0.0`.

Protocol, periphery, SDK, CLI, and React integrations share this metadata. Core and periphery address maps have different supported contract/chain combinations. The named Intuition chain definitions describe mainnet and testnet; Base and Base Sepolia addresses appear for applicable Base-side contracts.

## @0xintuition/deployments - Example

Select the testnet chain and its pinned MultiVault entry without a request:

```ts
import {
  getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId,
  intuitionTestnet,
} from '@0xintuition/deployments';

export const target = {
  chainId: intuitionTestnet.id,
  address: getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId(intuitionTestnet.id),
};
console.log(target);
```

`getContractAddressFromChainId` and the named core helpers throw when neither an override nor the canonical table supplies an address. Core helpers accept optional `AddressOverrides`; keep overrides specific to the intended deployment. This example reports metadata only, with no claim of a live testnet receipt or current deployment validation.

ABIs and bytecode have distinct uses. Metalayer `MetaERC20Hub`, `MetaERC20Spoke`, and `MetaNativeSpoke` bytecode exports contain deployed runtime code, not creation code. `MultiVaultBytecode` contains an unresolved library link placeholder; link it with the matching contract build's references before any deployment. Do not treat every bytecode export as ready to deploy.

## Related concepts

[Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes) explains why an action needs both a chain and a compatible target.

# @0xintuition/ids

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0

## What it's for

IDs computes deterministic protocol atom, predicate, triple, and counter-triple IDs. The result identifies exact bytes or ordered components; it does not determine whether two descriptions refer to the same real-world entity.

## When to use it

Use it when bytes or component IDs are already known. Use [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid) for entity identifier grammar and [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) for validated construction. Calculating an ID neither registers an atom nor submits a transaction.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/ids@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                              |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Atom, predicate, triple, counter-triple, OAuth and auth-user hashes; salts, hash validation, and formatting helpers. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/ids - Example

```ts
import {
  calculateAtomId,
  calculateCounterTripleId,
  calculateTripleId,
} from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { toHex } from 'viem';

// Synthetic bytes, with no claim about a real recording or artist.
const data = 'example:recording';
const recordingId = calculateAtomId(data);
const artistId = calculateAtomId('example:artist');
const predicateId = calculateAtomId('example:relationship');
const tripleId = calculateTripleId(recordingId, predicateId, artistId);
const reverseId = calculateTripleId(artistId, predicateId, recordingId);
const counterId = calculateCounterTripleId(tripleId);
console.log({
  sameBytes: recordingId === calculateAtomId(toHex(data)),
  changedBytes: recordingId !== calculateAtomId(`${data} `),
  reverseDiffers: reverseId !== tripleId,
  counterDiffersFromReverse: counterId.toString() !== reverseId.toString(),
});
```

`calculateAtomId` accepts a UTF-8 string or hex-encoded bytes. A hex-looking input is treated as bytes, so encode explicitly with `toHex` when the intended data is the literal text `0x...`. A trailing space changes the payload and therefore its atom ID.

Triple hashing uses **subject, predicate, object** in that order. A reversed triple makes a different assertion; a counter-triple instead derives from the original triple ID to identify its negation. Neither operation merges identities. Authentication-related hashes are deterministic public identifiers, not encryption for secrets.

## Related concepts

- [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms)
- [Triples, counter-triples and nested triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples)
- [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids)

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/README.md).
