# @0xintuition/iid-ladder

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The projection ladder selects a primary IID from supplied strong identifiers, provider handles, and canonical URLs. If nothing usable is available, it returns an explicit envelope fallback with a null IID.

## When to use it

Use it before atom construction when imports contain several candidate identifiers. The selection order is strong identifier → registered provider handle → canonical URL → envelope fallback. It does not search by name, prove a unique entity match, serialize atom bytes, record aliases, or fetch provider metadata.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid-ladder@0.1.0
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.`     | Identifier projection, category ordering, matching aliases, bound policy creation, and pinned Wikidata classification helpers. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

Published peers: none.

## @0xintuition/iid-ladder - Example

```ts
import { projectIdentifierLadder } from '@0xintuition/iid-ladder';

const selection = projectIdentifierLadder({
  strongIdentifiers: { isrc: 'US-RC1-76-07839' },
  canonicalUrl: 'https://example.com/recording',
});
if (selection.iid === null) {
  console.log({ needsIdentityEvidence: true, reason: selection.reason });
} else {
  console.log({ iid: selection.iid, selectedFrom: selection.rung });
}
const noIdentifier = projectIdentifierLadder({});
console.log(noIdentifier);
```

The supplied strong ISRC wins over the URL. Empty input returns `iid: null`; inspect `reason` and collect more evidence or use an explicit envelope. A name-only recipe belongs to the declarative IID engine and a classification ladder; identical names can describe different entities.

`strongIdentifierOrder` is an allowlist as well as an order. Category policies distinguish primary identities from aliases used only for matching. Default `providerLocalHandles: 'reject'` leaves unregistered provider namespaces as fallbacks. The optional `'mint'` policy preserves application-local historical strings; it does not make them canonical registered IIDs or P0-eligible. Package-specific identifier additions are disclosed on the [specification page](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec).

## Related concepts

- [The identity ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder)

See also [Primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-ladder/README.md).

[Canonical identity ladders](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/05-identity-ladders.md) · [Canonical gen1 derivation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/06-gen1.md) · [Projection implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-ladder/src/ladder.ts).

# @0xintuition/iid-registry

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The registry maps identifier schemes and values to known classifications, provider capability names, and provider hints. These are pure local lookups, not fetched provider responses.

## When to use it

Use it when a parsed identifier needs semantic meaning or an enrichment plan. A provider name does not mean its client is installed, credentials are available, or a match exists. Use [atom-enrichment](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-enrichment) for provider execution; no HTTP request, cache, or credential handling happens here.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid-registry@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Classification lookups, ordered provider plans, provider names, and typed identifier-hint maps. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/classifications`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid).

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/iid-registry - Example

```ts
import {
  classificationForIid,
  identifierHintsForIid,
  providersForIid,
} from '@0xintuition/iid-registry';

const inputIid = 'int:isrc:USRC17607839';
const classification = classificationForIid(inputIid);
const providerPlan = providersForIid(inputIid);
const hints = identifierHintsForIid(inputIid);
const unmapped = classificationForIid('int:iswc:T0345246801');
console.log({ classification, providerPlan, hints, unmapped });
```

The ISRC maps to `music-recording`, and its plan lists `musicbrainz`, `spotify`, and `apple-music` capabilities in that order. The example performs no search and returns no recording metadata. The valid ISWC example has no mapped classification: the registry has no music-composition classification.

An empty provider plan does not make an IID invalid. Bare polymorphic values can also remain unclassified. Historical spellings that can be canonicalized may resolve through their canonical form; that does not make those spellings eligible new anchors.

## Related concepts

- [The IID registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-registry)

See also [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/README.md).

[Canonical registry governance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/09-registry-governance.md) · [Canonical scheme registry](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/registry.json) · [Classification mapping](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/src/classification.ts) · [Provider plans](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-registry/src/providers.ts).

# @0xintuition/iid-spec

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0

## What it's for

This package distributes IID specification documents and machine-readable conformance fixtures. It has no JavaScript runtime API; the canonical authority for these docs is the separate Intuition Identifier specification.

## When to use it

Use the documents and fixtures to implement or compare identifier producers. Use [iid](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid) for application parsing and derivation, and [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry) for classification and provider planning. The packaged copy differs from the canonical source, so a package fixture alone does not establish canonical-spec conformance.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid-spec@0.1.0
```

The JSON artifacts can be read from Node; there is no root runtime export.

## Entry points

| Subpath                | Purpose                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `./conformance/*.json` | Machine-readable fixture documents, including canonicalization, parsing, validation, normalization, and derivation vectors. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: none.

## @0xintuition/iid-spec - Example

This Node example loads a published data artifact through its exported path; it does not invent a runtime import from the package root.

```ts
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';

const require = createRequire(import.meta.url);
const vectorsPath = require.resolve(
  '@0xintuition/iid-spec/conformance/canonicalization.json',
);
const packagedVectors: unknown = JSON.parse(readFileSync(vectorsPath, 'utf8'));
console.log({ loadedConformanceDocument: typeof packagedVectors === 'object' });
```

For an independent implementation, compare against the canonical [registry](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/registry.json) and [test vectors](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/test-vectors.json) as well as the packaged corpus. Loading the file is not a conformance test.

The canonical specification is version 0.1.0. Its §7.8 distinguishes identity data from companion metadata. The package copy omits §7.8, accepts typed `wd` values and adds the `apple-podcasts`, `letterboxd` and `podcast-index` schemes. Both sources define weak `acct` handles. The package makes that form ineligible for P0 and sets P1 as its minimum profile. The identifier bytes stay the same. Chapters 00, 01, 04, 05 and 09 also differ. [Canonical representation profiles](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md#78-the-atom-creation-model-data-and-companion-metadata) · [Canonical account scheme](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/schemes/acct.md) · [Packaged amendments](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/spec/09-registry-governance.md#97-pre-publication-amendments)

## Related concepts

- [The Intuition Identifier (IID)](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid)
- [Schemes and canonical form](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes)

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/README.md).

[Canonical specification](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/00-overview.md) · [Canonical registry governance](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/09-registry-governance.md) · [Packaged representation profiles](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid-spec/spec/07-representation-profiles.md).

# @0xintuition/iid

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0

## What it's for

IID implements identifier grammar, scheme canonicalization, normalization, recipe hashing, and declarative identity ladders. An IID names an entity; it is not the protocol atom ID of every representation of that entity.

## When to use it

Use `inspectIntuitionId` for a typed validity result and `SCHEMES` for explicit canonicalization. Use [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids) to hash atom bytes, [primitives](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives) to select a representation, and [iid-registry](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry) for meaning and provider plans. Parsing or passing validation does not prove a record exists at an external registry.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/iid@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                             |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Parsing, validation, inspection, scheme canonicalizers, NORM-1, gen1 derivation, and the declarative ladder engine. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/iid - Example

```ts
import { inspectIntuitionId, SCHEMES } from '@0xintuition/iid';

const canonicalIsrc = SCHEMES.isrc.canonicalize('US-RC1-76-07839');
if (canonicalIsrc === undefined) throw new Error('Invalid ISRC');
const identifier = `int:isrc:${canonicalIsrc}`;
const inspection = inspectIntuitionId(identifier);
if (!inspection.valid) throw new Error(inspection.reason);
console.log({ iid: identifier, anchorEligible: inspection.anchorEligible });
```

This separate ISRC conformance example produces `int:isrc:USRC17607839`; it is not an identifier for the synthetic catalog recording. Canonicalization can return `undefined`. Inspection distinguishes a non-canonical spelling from an unknown or invalid scheme; a non-canonical result can offer a `canonical` value, but it is not a valid new anchor.

Validity and bare P0 eligibility are separate. Class C recipe-derived identifiers need P1 evidence. Bare polymorphic identifiers also require a typed envelope. The package implements additional identifier forms beyond the pinned canonical source; see the [specification differences](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-spec).

## Related concepts

- [The Intuition Identifier (IID)](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid)
- [Schemes and canonical form](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/iid-schemes)
- [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles)
- [The identity ladder](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/identity-ladder)

See also [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/README.md).

[Canonical grammar](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/02-grammar.md) · [Canonical normalization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/04-normalization.md) · [Canonical representation profiles](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md) · [Inspection implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/iid/src/parse.ts).

# Packages

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/atom-classification` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-enrichment` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-parser` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/atom-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/classifications` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/cli` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/curves` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/deployments` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/ids` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-ladder` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-registry` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/iid-spec` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

These stable packages separate vocabulary, identity, local construction, processing, and protocol operations. Each reference lists its exact install pin, public entry points, runtime dependencies, and peers. [Choose packages for your task](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/choose-packages), or start with [installation](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install) or the [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart).

An atom ID identifies exact bytes. An IID names an entity. A [triple](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples) records the subject, predicate, and object term IDs in that order. Each position can refer to an atom or an existing triple, including a counter-triple. Local construction does not create on-chain terms. Indexed V2 graph reads use the [Query API of a Core node you run](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## Semantic / data modeling

| Package                                                       | Use it to                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`schema-org`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org)           | Inspect pinned schema vocabulary and inherited properties.      |
| [`classifications`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications) | Select entity specs, creation fields, and relationship targets. |
| [`predicates`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates)           | Select relationship vocabulary and deterministic predicate IDs. |

| [`iid-ladder`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-ladder)     | Select a primary identifier from supplied evidence.    |
| [`ids`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids)                   | Hash atom bytes and ordered triple components.         |

| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |

# @0xintuition/periphery

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/periphery` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Direct wrappers and encoders for FeeProxy, the swap-and-bridge router, and meta-bridge contracts. It also exposes their shared artifacts and address helpers.

## When to use it

Use it for individual periphery calls or deterministic calldata. Use [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) when you need a multi-step plan. WrappedTrust and other core contracts belong to [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol).

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/periphery@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Periphery ABIs, bytecode, deployments, client wrappers, and encoders |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependency: [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments). Peer dependency: `viem ^2.0.0`.

The pinned map provides FeeProxy addresses on Intuition mainnet and testnet. Bridge support is narrower: MetaERC20Hub is Base-mainnet scoped, and MetaERC20Spoke and MetaNativeSpoke are Intuition-mainnet scoped. FeeProxy support does not imply testnet bridge support.

## @0xintuition/periphery - Example

Prepare the target and calldata for a refund claim to a caller-supplied recipient. No refund ledger is read, and no claim is submitted.

```ts
import {
  feeProxyClaimRefundToEncode,
  getFeeProxyAddressFromChainId,
} from '@0xintuition/periphery';
import type { Address as RefundRecipient } from 'viem';

export function encodeRefund(recipient: RefundRecipient) {
  return {
    to: getFeeProxyAddressFromChainId(13579),
    data: feeProxyClaimRefundToEncode(recipient),
    value: 0n,
  };
}
```

Encoding checks ABI argument shape, not the caller's pending refund. A real application first reads the correct account's refund ledger, reviews the recipient and chain, and separately executes with an authorized wallet. RPC reads can reject; write wrappers can simulate and submit transactions according to their specific implementation.

The pinned router address lookup throws because the older Base router does not match the encoded `deadline` argument. Do not invent an address to make the encoder executable. An encoder can exist before a compatible target is available; unsupported bridge combinations and missing deployment lookups must be handled explicitly.

## Related concepts

- [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards)
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes)

See also [Build action plans and envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans).

## Source

# @0xintuition/pipeline-runtime

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/pipeline-runtime

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Promise utilities for bounded concurrency, cancellation, circuit breaking, caching, and provider observation. It supplies shared execution contracts; it does not store a graph or start a processing service.

## When to use it

Use it when a host needs ordered concurrent work or a consistent outcome vocabulary across providers. Use [atom runtime](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/atom-runtime) to compose classification and enrichment engines. Effect services and retry layers belong to your application; these functions accept Promise callbacks.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/pipeline-runtime@0.1.0
```

Use ESM on Node 20 or newer. The documentation examples run on Node 22.21.0.

## Entry points

All public modules

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Shared errors, provider contracts, test helpers, and TMDB endpoint builder |
| `./bounded-text` | Read streaming response text within a byte limit |
| `./cache` | Cancellable cache contract and memory TTL adapter |
| `./errors` | Shared pipeline error vocabulary |
| `./provider-observer` | Provider observation events and contracts |
| `./provider-metrics-contract` | Metric labels, normalization, and series contract |
| `./retry-after` | Parse and bound retry delays |
| `./letterboxd` | Letterboxd host policy and circuit state |
| `./letterboxd-page` | Parse Letterboxd page identity |
| `./tmdb` | TMDB endpoint policy |
| `./testing/prometheus-exposition` | Validate Prometheus exposition; optional Node tool invocation |
| `./outcome` | Outcome union, cancellation, and timeout helpers |
| `./circuit-breaker` | Circuit breaker, snapshots, and admission errors |
| `./concurrency` | Ordered bounded Promise execution |
| `./provider-metrics-contract.expected` | Expected provider metric series counts |
| `./provider-registry` | Provider definitions and operation contracts |
| `./provider-request-observation` | Observe and record provider requests |
| `./request-slot` | Provider request admission contracts |
| `./testing/provider-golden` | Provider golden-fixture helpers |
| `./testing/held-request-slot` | Controlled request-slot test helpers |
| `./testing/virtual-clock` | Deterministic clock for tests |
| `./provider-metrics` | Alias of the provider metrics contract |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: none. Peer dependencies: none.

Classification, enrichment, and atom runtime consume these contracts. A memory cache is process-local; an adapter is not a provisioned database. Provider-specific host policies do not replace your application's complete egress policy.

## @0xintuition/pipeline-runtime - Example

This fixed input needs no network or credentials. The result keeps input order even when callbacks finish in a different order.

```ts
import { forEachBounded } from '@0xintuition/pipeline-runtime/concurrency';

const controller = new AbortController();
export const outcomes = await forEachBounded(
  ['recording', 'artist', 'release'],
  async (label, signal) => {
    signal.throwIfAborted();
    return label.toUpperCase();
  },
  { concurrency: 2, signal: controller.signal },
);

for (const outcome of outcomes) {
  if (outcome.kind === 'success') console.log(outcome.value);
  else console.log(outcome.kind);
}
```

Successful outcomes carry `value`. The full outcome union also includes `failure`, `defect`, `timeout`, and `interrupted`. In `forEachBounded`, a synchronous callback throw is a defect and a returned Promise rejection is a failure. Parent cancellation rejects the batch with its abort reason, prevents queued work, and signals active callbacks; callbacks must honor that signal to stop I/O.

`CircuitBreaker.execute` admits one probe after its reset window. Its failure filter determines whether an admitted failure or cancellation counts toward opening the circuit; cancellation before admission starts no work. Inspect `snapshot()` without changing state.

## Related concepts

- [Atom runtime and pipelines](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atom-runtime)

See also [How the pieces fit](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/how-it-fits), [Classify and enrich atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/classify-enrich).

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/pipeline-runtime/README.md), [public exports](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/pipeline-runtime/package.json), and [concurrency implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/pipeline-runtime/src/concurrency.ts).

# @0xintuition/predicates

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/predicates` 0.1.0

## What it's for

The predicate registry provides reusable relationship vocabulary and the atom data that gives each predicate its deterministic ID. It also supplies semantic flags, display helpers, and optional enrichment-document builders.

## When to use it

Use a known predicate subpath for one relationship, or the root registry for discovery. Use [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications) for classification-specific object targets; legacy `expectedObjectType` strings are descriptive hints. Predicate metadata does not create graph edges, infer inverse edges, or upload an IPFS document.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/predicates@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                         |
| ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`     | Registry, deterministic data and IDs, semantic metadata, display and bootstrap helpers.         |
| `./*`   | Standalone predicate modules keyed by the exact registry key, such as `/byArtist` or `/sameAs`. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/ids`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids).

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/predicates - Example

```ts
import { calculateAtomId, calculateTripleId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import {
  byArtist,
  byArtistAtomData,
  byArtistId,
  byArtistSpec,
} from '@0xintuition/predicates/byArtist';

// Synthetic local fixture atoms; these strings claim no external identity.
const recordingId = calculateAtomId('example:recording');
const artistId = calculateAtomId('example:artist');
const byArtistTripleId = calculateTripleId(recordingId, byArtistId, artistId);
console.log({
  key: byArtistSpec.key,
  label: byArtist.name,
  data: byArtistAtomData,
  predicateId: byArtistId,
  tripleId: byArtistTripleId,
});
```

The key `byArtist` selects a registry entry; the label `by artist` is display text. The data is a compact `DefinedTerm` JSON-LD string containing `@context`, `@type`, `name`, and `description` in that order. The predicate ID hashes that exact data: changing the description changes the ID even if the label stays the same.

The explicit triple above means **recording → by artist → artist**. Reversing subject and object changes the assertion and its ID. This computes a triple locally; it does not establish that any term exists on-chain.

## Related concepts

- [Predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/predicates)
- [sameAs and identity linking](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as)

See also [music catalog](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/examples/music-catalog).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/README.md).

[byArtist specification](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/generated/specs/byArtist.ts) · [Standalone export](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/predicates/src/standalone/byArtist.ts) · [Predicate serialization](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/ids/src/predicate-id.ts).

# @0xintuition/primitives

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/primitives

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/primitives` 0.1.0

## What it's for

Primitives turns classification values into validated atom or triple blueprints. The anchor builder returns the selected representation, exact data bytes, deterministic atom ID, and separate companion URI context.

## When to use it

Use `buildIidAnchor` for identifier-first atoms, descriptive `buildAtom` helpers when descriptive JSON-LD is intentional, and triple builders for explicit relationships. These helpers do not upload URI content, create on-chain terms, call enrichment providers, or submit wallet transactions. Always narrow `BuildResult.success` before reading `value`; failures contain `errors`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/primitives@0.1.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath       | Purpose                                                                               |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.`           | Complete public builder API, with classification and ID helpers re-exported.          |
| `./atom`      | Descriptive JSON-LD atom builders.                                                    |
| `./types`     | TypeScript input, result, blueprint, profile, and URI-limit types; use `import type`. |
| `./anchor`    | IID-first anchor building, candidate validation, and URI policy limits.               |
| `./triple`    | Triple construction by key or name, and counter-triples.                              |
| `./discover`  | Classification discovery and recommended fields.                                      |
| `./validate`  | Atom-data recognition and validation.                                                 |
| `./predicate` | Custom predicate builders and predicate discovery.                                    |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: [`@0xintuition/classifications`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications), [`@0xintuition/ids`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids), [`@0xintuition/iid`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid), [`@0xintuition/iid-registry`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/iid-registry), [`@0xintuition/predicates`](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates).

Published peers: `viem ^2.0.0`.

## @0xintuition/primitives - Example

```ts
import { buildIidAnchor } from '@0xintuition/primitives/anchor';

// Standalone ISRC conformance input; no association with the music catalog fixture.
const values = { isrc: 'US-RC1-76-07839' };
const bare = buildIidAnchor('music-recording', values);
const withContext = buildIidAnchor('music-recording', values, {
  contextUris: ['https://example.com/recording-evidence'],
});
if (!bare.success) throw new Error(bare.errors.join('; '));
if (!withContext.success) throw new Error(withContext.errors.join('; '));

console.log({
  iid: bare.value.iid,
  profile: bare.value.profile,
  data: bare.value.data,
  dataHex: bare.value.dataHex,
  id: bare.value.id,
  sameIdWithContext: bare.value.id === withContext.value.id,
  contextUris: withContext.value.contextUris,
});
```

The golden ISRC fixture stands alone; it is not assigned to the music catalog example. At P0, `data` is the bare IID string, `dataHex` is its UTF-8 encoding, and `id` hashes those bytes. `contextUris` is an ordered companion list outside the payload: adding it leaves `data`, `dataHex`, and `id` unchanged. By contrast, editing JSON-LD `@context` inside an envelope changes the hashed payload. No URI is fetched or uploaded.

```ts
const person = buildIidAnchor('person', {
  givenName: 'Example',
  familyName: 'Person',
});
if (!person.success) throw new Error(person.errors.join('; '));
const forcedBare = buildIidAnchor(
  'person',
  { givenName: 'Example', familyName: 'Person' },
  { profile: 'p0' },
);
console.log({
  derivedProfile: person.value.profile,
  class: person.value.class,
  forcedBareAccepted: forcedBare.success,
});
```

A Class C name recipe needs its evidence in a P1 envelope; forcing P0 fails. A name match is not proof of a unique real-world person. When no identity rung fires, a valid fallback envelope can have `iid`, `scheme`, and `class` set to `null`; do not assume every successful build has an IID.

In this pinned implementation, explicit P1 and P2 requests with a derived IID serialize the same identity envelope bytes. The `profile` label alone does not promise the canonical specification's full descriptive P2 payload. `candidateIid`, when supplied, takes precedence over derivation and determines the profile by eligibility; that path does not consult the requested `profile`. Inspect the returned bytes before storing them.

URI limits are checked locally. Supply `uriLimits` from the intended protocol configuration when preparing writes; the default offline policy is not a live-chain query. A `providerPlan` is only a list of capabilities.

## Related concepts

- [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms)
- [Triples, counter-triples and nested triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples)
- [Deterministic IDs](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/deterministic-ids)
- [Representation profiles](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/representation-profiles)
- [sameAs and identity linking](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/same-as)

See also [Build creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles), [offline quickstart](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/quickstart).

[Canonical representation profiles and companion metadata](https://github.com/0xIntuition/intuition-identifier/blob/3e593247c0e7cb168b37368937167ed146d3868a/spec/07-representation-profiles.md) · [Anchor implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/anchor.ts) · [BuildResult and anchor types](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/primitives/src/types.ts).

# @0xintuition/protocol

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/protocol` 4.0.0

## What it's for

Typed wrappers, encoders, ABIs, and receipt parsers for core contracts including MultiVault, TrustBonding, WrappedTrust, and emissions controllers. It reads and writes chain state; it does not serve the indexed graph from a Core node.

## When to use it

Use a read wrapper for RPC state, an `Encode` helper for calldata, or a write wrapper when your application is ready to request a transaction. Use [SDK actions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk) for higher-level plans and [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery) for FeeProxy and bridges. For indexed graph reads, [query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/protocol@4.0.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser. Configure matching chain, address, public client, and wallet client when needed.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Core wrappers, encoders, ABIs, events, deployments, networks, and types |
| `./contracts` | Named ABI and bytecode re-exports from deployments |

The root does not export deployment bytecode or curve math. Import pure math from [curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves).

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependency: [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments). Peer dependency: `viem ^2.0.0`.

`ReadConfig` contains `address` and `publicClient`; `WriteConfig` also contains `walletClient`. Contract artifacts target MultiVault v1.1.0, but a recorded address alone does not prove that the deployed implementation supports every artifact function. Verify capability on the intended deployment before a write.

## @0xintuition/protocol - Example

This pure function encodes an existing term's deposit call from caller-supplied values. It returns hex calldata without RPC or a wallet request.

```ts
import { multiVaultDepositEncode } from '@0xintuition/protocol';
import type { Address, Hex } from 'viem';

// Caller-supplied values must describe an existing term and chosen curve.
export function encodeDeposit(
  receiver: Address,
  termId: Hex,
  curveId: bigint,
  minShares: bigint,
) {
  return multiVaultDepositEncode(receiver, termId, curveId, minShares);
}
```

`multiVaultDepositEncode` takes receiver, term ID, curve ID, and minimum shares in that order. The deposit assets are the transaction's separate native `value`, not another encoder argument. ABI encoding can reject malformed values; it cannot verify term existence, current fees, available funds, or slippage.

Read wrappers make RPC calls and can fail on transport, address, ABI, or contract errors. Write wrappers have real side effects. For example, `multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris(config, inputs)` accepts `inputs.args` as creator, atom-data array, asset array, and URI arrays, plus `value` equal to the sum of assets; it validates locally, simulates, and then calls the wallet. Optional `uriLimits` validate supplied live limits. Simulation remains authoritative for duplicates, approvals, cost, and live configuration.

Receipt parsers fetch and filter logs. Supply the expected emitter where supported and handle empty results before reading an event. A hash or an encoded call alone is not confirmation.

## Related concepts

- [Atoms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/atoms)
- [Triples, counter-triples and nested triples](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/triples)
- [Vaults, shares and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults)
- [Bonding curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/bonding-curves)
- [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards)
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes)

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/README.md), [root exports](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/src/index.ts), [deposit encoder](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/src/core/multivault/deposit-encode.ts), and [URI-aware creation wrapper](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/protocol/src/core/multivault/create-atoms-with-uris.ts).

# @0xintuition/react

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/react

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/react` 0.1.0

## What it's for

React hooks for protocol reads, writes, and transaction lifecycle state. The hooks query contracts through wagmi; they do not query the indexed graph from Intuition Core.

## When to use it

Use it inside an existing React application that needs atom, triple, vault, or position state and explicit write flows. Use [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) in a framework-independent script. For indexed V2 graph reads, [query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core).

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/react@0.1.0 @0xintuition/protocol@4.0.0 @0xintuition/deployments@0.1.0 react@19.1.0 react-dom@19.1.0 wagmi@2.15.4 @tanstack/react-query@5.90.2 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM. This example uses the release-tested React 19, wagmi 2, and Query 5 combination. The host supplies its renderer; `react-dom` is not a peer declared by this library.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | Providers, read/write/flow hooks, identity hooks, and public types |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime graph edges: [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments), [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids), and [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol). The manifest declares ids as an ordinary dependency and deployments/protocol as peers so the host selects shared copies.

| Peer | Published range |
| --- | --- |
| `@tanstack/react-query` | `>=5` |
| `react` | `>=18` |
| `viem` | `^2.0.0` |
| `wagmi` | `>=2` |
| `@0xintuition/protocol` | `^4.0.0` |
| `@0xintuition/deployments` | `^0.1.0` |

Use `WagmiProvider`, then `QueryClientProvider`, then `IntuitionProvider`. In an existing app, reuse its wagmi and Query providers. The documented TypeScript setup is strict with `skipLibCheck: true`, matching the release consumer checks; checking the entire upstream declaration graph without that option is not verified by this package release.

## @0xintuition/react - Example

Mounting this component performs a testnet RPC read over HTTP. It requires no wallet connector, signing key, or Core node.

```tsx
'use client';

import { intuitionTestnet } from '@0xintuition/deployments';
import { IntuitionProvider, useAtomCost } from '@0xintuition/react';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { createConfig, http, WagmiProvider } from 'wagmi';

const config = createConfig({
  chains: [intuitionTestnet],
  transports: { [intuitionTestnet.id]: http() },
});

function AtomCost() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useAtomCost();
  const message = isLoading
    ? 'Loading atom creation cost…'
    : error
      ? 'Unable to load the cost. Check your RPC connection and reload.'
      : data === undefined
        ? 'No atom creation cost is available. Check your network configuration.'
        : `Atom creation cost: ${data.toString()} wei`;
  return <p role="status">{message}</p>;
}

export function PackageExample() {
  const [queryClient] = useState(() => new QueryClient());
  return (
    <WagmiProvider config={config}>
      <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
        <IntuitionProvider network="testnet">
          <AtomCost />
        </IntuitionProvider>
      </QueryClientProvider>
    </WagmiProvider>
  );
}
```

Loading, missing data, and errors produce readable status text. This is a minimal provider/hook composition, not a complete application. Configure a compatible RPC and deployment through the providers before mounting it.

For writes, supply your application's connected wallet and handle promise rejection. `useTransactionFlow` coordinates submission and receipt confirmation; `reset()` or unmount rejects a pending execution but does not cancel a wallet request or on-chain transaction. Reverted receipts are errors, and only one execution may be active.

`useCreateAtomFlow` uses ordinary `createAtoms` and extracts term IDs only from the configured MultiVault's logs. It does not implicitly register URI context. For URI-aware creation, compose `multiVaultCreateAtomsWithUris` from protocol with `useTransactionFlow`; no dedicated URI-aware creation hook is included in this release.

## Related concepts

- [Signals](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/signals)

## Source

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/README.md), [public exports](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/index.ts), [atom hooks](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/hooks/use-atom.ts), and [creation flow](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/react/src/hooks/use-create-atom-flow.ts).

# @0xintuition/schema-org

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/schema-org

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/schema-org` 0.1.0

## What it's for

A local vocabulary snapshot supplies schema.org type and property records. It describes what a property means and where it is declared; it does not decide which fields an Intuition creation form should collect.

## When to use it

Use a direct type import when the type is known, or root lookup helpers for dynamic schema tooling. The vocabulary is pinned to schema.org V30.0 and never fetched by these lookups. Use [classifications](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/classifications) for recommended creation fields and typed relationship targets; this package does not validate submitted values or create atoms.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/schema-org@0.1.0
```

Use ESM imports. See [installation and peer setup](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/install).

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose                                                                                                            |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.`     | Type lookup, inherited-property lookup, vocabulary registry, and provenance constants.                             |
| `./*`   | Generated type records by exact case-sensitive name, such as `/Book`; only names in the pinned vocabulary resolve. |

## Depends on and works with

Runtime dependencies: none.

Published peers: none.

## @0xintuition/schema-org - Example

```ts
import { getPropertiesFor } from '@0xintuition/schema-org';
import { schemaOrgBook } from '@0xintuition/schema-org/Book';

const titleProperty = getPropertiesFor('Book').find(
  (property) => property.name === 'name',
);
console.log({
  type: schemaOrgBook.name,
  titleOrigin: titleProperty?.originType,
});
```

`schemaOrgBook` selects the generated Book record directly. `getPropertiesFor` resolves inherited properties locally; `name` originates on `Thing`. Unknown types return `undefined` from `getType` and an empty list from `getPropertiesFor`.

## Related concepts

- [schema.org vocabulary](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/schema-org)

See also [Build creation forms](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/creation-profiles).

## Source

[Package README at the pinned release](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/schema-org/README.md).

[Generated Book record](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/schema-org/src/generated/types/Book.ts) · [Lookup implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/schema-org/src/schema-org.ts).

# @0xintuition/sdk

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/sdk

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

## What it's for

Application-level protocol actions, quote preparation, wallet workflows, and JSON-serializable action envelopes. It combines lower-level contracts and math into explicit workflows without owning your application's storage or transaction authorization.

## When to use it

Use actions for a deposit, redemption, creation, FeeProxy, or TrustBonding workflow; use pure envelope builders when another component will review and execute the plan. For indexed V2 graph data, [query a Core node](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/query-core). Use [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol) for individual contract wrappers and [React](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/react) for hooks.

## Install

```sh
npm install @0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0 viem@2.31.4
```

Use ESM on Node 20+ or a compatible browser. There is no CommonJS entry point.

## Entry points

| Subpath | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.` | SDK-owned workflows, actions, utilities, and selected shared types |
| `./api` | Read-client exports; see the V1 boundary below |
| `./actions` | Quotes, transaction preparation, pure envelopes, and envelope schemas |
| `./protocol` | Explicit low-level protocol escape hatch |
| `./trust-swap-and-bridge-router` | Router workflows subject to deployment support |
| `./utils` | SDK formatting helpers |

The `./api` read client calls the V1 GraphQL API; see [The SDK read client](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/read-with-sdk).

## Depends on and works with

Runtime package dependencies: [curves](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/curves), [deployments](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/deployments), [ids](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/ids), [periphery](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/periphery), and [protocol](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/protocol). Peer dependency: `viem ^2.0.0`.

The root no longer re-exports the full protocol or ID packages. Import those APIs from their own packages, and canonical predicate data from [predicates](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/packages/predicates). Your application selects an upload provider and supplies any resulting content URI; the SDK does not upload it for you.

## @0xintuition/sdk - Example

This pure builder accepts a synthetic quote as `readContext` and produces one deposit step. It performs no RPC request, simulation, signing, or submission. The recipient and quote are fixtures, and the computed term ID does not assert that the atom exists on testnet.

```ts
import { multiVaultDepositEnvelope } from '@0xintuition/sdk/actions';
import { calculateAtomId } from '@0xintuition/ids';
import { getMultiVaultAddressFromChainId as getEnvelopeTarget } from '@0xintuition/deployments';

// Synthetic quote and recipient; this atom has not been registered on-chain.
export const envelope = await multiVaultDepositEnvelope({
  chainId: 13579,
  multiVaultAddress: getEnvelopeTarget(13579),
  receiver: '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111',
  termId: calculateAtomId('Synthetic package reference'),
  curveId: 1n,
  assetsIn: 1000n,
  slippageBps: 100n,
  readContext: {
    previewDeposit: { sharesOut: 500n, assetsAfterFees: 990n },
    entryFeeAmount: 5n,
    protocolFeeAmount: 5n,
    currentSharePrice: 2_000_000_000_000_000_000n,
  },
});
export const envelopeJson = JSON.stringify(envelope);
console.log(envelope.action, envelope.steps.length);
```

The result's action is `multivault.deposit`, its steps contain encoded calldata and decimal-string values, and `JSON.stringify` succeeds. Missing required read context rejects the builder. In a real workflow, obtain current context for the intended chain, address, term, and curve, then review and simulate before separately authorizing execution. A valid schema proves the envelope's shape, not its economic outcome or authority to spend.

Distinguish pure `*Envelope` builders from RPC-backed quote/preparation helpers and transaction executors such as `feeProxyExecutePlan`. An encoded plan is not a transaction receipt. [Build action plans and envelopes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/build/action-plans) explains the boundary; the [generated action reference](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/plans-multivault) supplies exact parameter types.

## Related concepts

- [Vaults, shares and positions](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/vaults)
- [Signals](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/signals)
- [Fees, epochs and rewards](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/fees-and-rewards)
- [Protocol writes](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/concepts/protocol-writes)

See also [migration guide](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/get-started/migrate-from-v1).

[Package README](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/README.md), [action plans](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/docs/action-plans.md), [envelope implementation](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/plans/multivault.ts), and [root export migration](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/docs/migration.md). # Dynamic-fee curve actions

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/dynamic-fee-curve

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## dynamicFeeCurveGetTierOverrides

Reads every tier's manual fee override for a curve, in the shape the pure tier maths takes.

The live contract consults `tierFeeOverride[tier]` before falling back to the formulaic rate, so
any off-chain rendering of the ladder or its rates must do the same or it silently disagrees
wherever an override is set. Exported because it is a prerequisite for using `@0xintuition/curves`
directly — without it, every consumer rediscovers both the tier range and the fact that the two
rate fields are `uint16`, which viem decodes as a JS `number` while `DynamicFeeTierOverride`
declares them as `bigint`. An unchecked pass-through type-checks and then throws inside the first
`mulDivUp`.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L180)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveGetTierOverrides(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    config: DynamicFeeConfig;
  },
  deps?: Pick<DynamicFeeCurveDeps, 'tierFeeOverride'>,
): Promise<Map<bigint, DynamicFeeTierOverride>>;
```

- **`config`**: Curve address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The curve's config, which carries the tier count to walk.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The set overrides, keyed by tier. Tiers without an override are absent.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurveGetTierLadder

Resolves a dynamic-fee curve's tier ladder for the current vault state — the tier
math itself is pure (`@0xintuition/curves`), fed by a single on-chain config read.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L218)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveGetTierLadder(
  configs: {
    bondingCurveRegistry: ReadConfig;
    curveReadConfig: Omit<ReadConfig, 'address'>;
  },
  inputs: {
    curveId: bigint;
  },
  deps?: Pick<
    DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
    'curveAddresses' | 'getConfig' | 'tierFeeOverride'
  >,
): Promise<{
  curveAddress: Address;
  config: DynamicFeeConfig;
  overrides: Map<bigint, DynamicFeeTierOverride>;
  tierLadder: DynamicFeeTierLadderEntry[];
}>;
```

- **`configs`**: `bondingCurveRegistry` (to resolve the curve address) and the shared read config the resolved curve is read through.
- **`inputs`**: The curve ID to resolve and quote.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The curve address, its config, its overrides, and the full tier ladder.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurveQuoteDepositPlan

Quotes a deposit into a dynamic-fee vault: resolves the curve from the registry, reads the
on-chain piecewise deposit-fee quote (exact across every band the deposit traverses, not just the
pre-deposit tier), and composes it with the standard MultiVault deposit quote.

Also reports the traversal itself — which tier the vault starts in, which it lands in, and the
per-band split — because a piecewise fee that arrives as a single number cannot be explained to
the person paying it.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L254)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveQuoteDepositPlan(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    bondingCurveRegistry: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    assetsIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurveDepositQuotePlan>;
```

- **`configs`**: `multiVault` and `bondingCurveRegistry` read configs.
- **`inputs`**: The term/curve to deposit into and the gross asset amount.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The combined dynamic-fee-curve and MultiVault deposit quote.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurvePrepareDepositTx

Prepare encoded deposit arguments and minimum shares from a dynamic-fee quote, without submitting a transaction.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L323)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurvePrepareDepositTx(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    bondingCurveRegistry: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    receiver: Address;
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    assetsIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurvePrepareDepositTxResult>;
```

- **`configs`**: `multiVault` and `bondingCurveRegistry` read configs.
- **`inputs`**: The receiver, term/curve to deposit into, and the gross asset amount.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The deposit calldata, args, value, and the quote it was built from.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurveQuoteRedeemPlan

Quotes a redeem out of a dynamic-fee vault for a specific account.

The withdrawal rate on this curve keys on the tiers the ACCOUNT entered at, not on where the vault
sits now, and the two diverge in both directions as the vault moves. A position is a set of lots,
one per band the holder entered through, and a redeem unwinds them highest tier first, so a single
redemption can be priced at several rates at once. This adds that context to the generic
account-aware MultiVault quote: the lots in unwind order, the one the next share out comes from,
where the vault currently is, and whether the account holds any lot at all — an account with none
falls back to the vault's tier, which is the one case where the two coincide by construction.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L364)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveQuoteRedeemPlan(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    bondingCurveRegistry: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    account: Address;
    sharesIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurveRedeemQuotePlan>;
```

- **`configs`**: `multiVault` and `bondingCurveRegistry` read configs.
- **`inputs`**: The term/curve, the redeeming account, the share count and optional slippage.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The account's payout, its fee breakdown, and the tiers behind the withdrawal rate.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurvePrepareRedeemTx

Prepares a redeem transaction out of a dynamic-fee vault, floored against the redeeming account's
own payout rather than a holder-agnostic one.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L438)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurvePrepareRedeemTx(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    bondingCurveRegistry: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    receiver: Address;
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    account: Address;
    sharesIn: bigint;
    slippageBps?: bigint;
  },
  deps?: DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurvePrepareRedeemTxResult>;
```

- **`configs`**: `multiVault` and `bondingCurveRegistry` read configs.
- **`inputs`**: The receiver, term/curve, redeeming account, share count and optional slippage.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The redeem calldata, args, and the quote it was built from.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurveProjectDepositEarnings

Projects what a deposit's curve fee EARNS — for every tier, and optionally for one holder.

This is the other half of a deposit quote. The fee side has always been answerable; the earning
side is what makes an early position worth taking, and it needs the fulcrum kernel: each
traversed band's slice of the fee is spread over the tiers below it by a sliding triangular
window, gated on `minEligibleTierStakeBps`, with the depositor's own landing changing the
denominators between bands. The kernel maths is `dynamicFeeDistributeDeposit` in
`@0xintuition/curves`, a floor-exact mirror of the contract's `recordDeposit`; this function
feeds it the on-chain state it needs (config, overrides, per-tier occupancy and accumulators, the
depositor's lots) and, for a named holder, sums their lots so the projection is wei-exact rather
than approximately pro-rata. A holder with lots at several tiers earns at each of them.

A projection is a statement about the CURRENT state: another deposit landing first changes the
denominators, exactly as it would change a price quote.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L508)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveProjectDepositEarnings(
  configs: {
    multiVault: ReadConfig;
    bondingCurveRegistry: ReadConfig;
  },
  inputs: {
    termId: Hex;
    curveId: bigint;
    assetsIn: bigint;
    depositor?: Address;
    holder?: Address;
  },
  deps?: DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurveEarningsProjection>;
```

- **`configs`**: `multiVault` and `bondingCurveRegistry` read configs.
- **`inputs`**: The term/curve and gross deposit, the depositor (when they hold a position), and optionally a holder to project for.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The per-tier distribution of the deposit's curve fee, and the named holder's exact earning.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurveGetClaimableAcrossTerms

Reads what an account can claim across a set of terms, and where it comes from.

`claimable(account, termId)` is the obvious read and the wrong one for a multi-term total: it
folds in the account's banked (term-independent) balance on every call, so summing or filtering by
it per term double-counts that component, and the error grows with the number of positions held.
`claimableAcross` is the total `claim` would actually pay; `pendingFor` is the additive per-term
part; `bankedEarnings` is the settled remainder. Returning all three is what lets a consumer show
the breakdown without reconstructing it wrongly.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L631)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurveGetClaimableAcrossTerms(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    termIds: Hex[];
  },
  deps?: Pick<
    DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
    'claimableAcross' | 'pendingFor' | 'bankedEarnings'
  >,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurveClaimableAcrossTermsResult>;
```

- **`config`**: Read config for the dynamic-fee curve.
- **`inputs`**: The account and the candidate term IDs to check.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The total claimable across the supplied terms, which of them are non-zero, and the split.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## dynamicFeeCurvePrepareClaimTx

Builds a batched claim transaction for a dynamic-fee curve: discovers which terms hold a claimable
balance for the account, then returns one `claim` calldata settling all of them at once.

Having nothing to claim is an ordinary state, not an error, so it comes back as `isClaimable:
false` rather than as a thrown exception a UI has to catch to render a zero. Term IDs are
de-duplicated because the contract reverts with `DynamicFeeFlatPriceCurve_DuplicateTermIds` on a
repeat.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/dynamic-fee-curve.ts#L675)

```ts
function dynamicFeeCurvePrepareClaimTx(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    account: Address;
    termIds: Hex[];
  },
  deps?: Pick<
    DynamicFeeCurveDeps,
    'claimableAcross' | 'pendingFor' | 'bankedEarnings'
  >,
): Promise<DynamicFeeCurvePrepareClaimTxResult>;
```

- **`config`**: Read config for the dynamic-fee curve.
- **`inputs`**: The account and the candidate term IDs to settle.
- **`deps`**: Injectable protocol read primitives.
- **returns**: The claim calldata, args, the claimable breakdown, and whether it is worth sending.

Defaults: `deps = defaultDynamicFeeCurveDeps`. Dependency arguments are optional test/customization hooks; normal consumers use the built-in dependencies.

## Imported type provenance

Public import locations and the definitions used by these signatures and helper types. Value imports appear where a dependency hook uses `typeof`.

### DynamicFeeDepositDistribution

[Source definition](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/dynamic-fee-distribution.ts#L92)

```ts
export type DynamicFeeDepositDistribution = {
  /** Credited tiers in ascending order. Tiers that received nothing are absent. */
  perTier: DynamicFeeTierPayout[];
  /**
   * Fee no cohort was there to earn at the schedule rate — protocol accrual. A first-tier deposit
   * has no prior tier at all; past that it is the part of a pool the prior ladder's occupancy could
   * not absorb once every tier is paid at the schedule ceiling.
   */
  toProtocol: bigint;
  /** Occupancy as the contract leaves it: fee-independent, with the deposit's stake landed. */
  occupancyAfter: DynamicFeeTierOccupancy;
  /** The accumulators as the contract leaves them, the supplied values plus this deposit's deltas. */
  accFeePerShareAfter: DynamicFeeAccumulators;
  /** The bands the stake traversed, in ascending order, with each band's slice of the fee. */
  bands: DynamicFeeDepositBandLanding[];
  /** The depositor's lots as the contract leaves them. */
  depositorAfter: DynamicFeeLots;
  /** The depositor's highest lot after the deposit, or `DYNAMIC_FEE_NO_LOT` when they hold none. */
  topTierAfter: bigint;
  /**
   * What the replay banked into the account-wide settled balance. A deposit settles only the lots
   * it tops up, so this is non-zero only when a band lands on a lot that had earned something.
   */
  banked: bigint;
};
```

### DynamicFeeTierPayout

[Source definition](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/curves/src/dynamic-fee-distribution.ts#L66)

```ts
export type DynamicFeeTierPayout = {
  tier: bigint;
  /** Assets credited to this tier's cohort in total. */
  amount: bigint;
  /**
   * The exact `accFeePerShare` increment the contract writes for this tier, in `ACC_PRECISION`.
   * A holder's pending delta is `floor(stake * accAfter / ACC) - floor(stake * accBefore / ACC)`,
   * which is what makes wei-exact per-account projection possible.
   */
  accDelta: bigint;
};
```

## Input and result types

Exported declarations are public imports from the SDK subpath above. Module-local helper aliases describe accepted shapes but are not public exports.

### DynamicFeeCurveDepositQuotePlan

Public export.

```ts
export type DynamicFeeCurveDepositQuotePlan = {
  curveId: bigint;
  curveAddress: Address;
  termId: Hex;
  assetsIn: bigint;
  curveFee: bigint;
  tierLadder: DynamicFeeTierLadderEntry[];
  /** Where the vault sits before the deposit, and where this deposit leaves it. */
  startTier: bigint;
  landingTier: bigint;
  vaultStakeBefore: bigint;
  /**
   * The tier bands the FEE quote traverses, and what each one costs — the walk behind `curveFee`,
   * available before the trade.
   *
   * This is the fee walk, not the landing walk: it advances by the fee base net of the CURVE fee
   * only, mirroring the on-chain `quoteDepositFee`, while the shares that actually land are also
   * net of MultiVault's protocol, entry and term fees. The landing (what `DepositBandRecorded`
   * emits, and what `landingTier` reports) can therefore stop a band short of the last band here.
   * Both walks are the contract's own; they answer different questions.
   */
  bands: DynamicFeeDepositBand[];
  multiVaultQuote: MultiVaultDepositQuotePlan;
};
```

### DynamicFeeCurveRedeemQuotePlan

Public export.

```ts
export type DynamicFeeCurveRedeemQuotePlan = {
  curveId: bigint;
  curveAddress: Address;
  termId: Hex;
  account: Address;
  /**
   * The account's lots, highest tier first — the order the redeem unwinds them, and the order the
   * withdrawal fee is priced in: each portion at the rate of the band it entered through.
   */
  lots: Array<{ tier: bigint; stake: bigint }>;
  /**
   * The lot the redeem draws from first, so the rate on the next share out. `DYNAMIC_FEE_NO_LOT`
   * when the account holds no lot at all.
   */
  topTier: bigint;
  /** Where the vault currently sits, which is NOT what a holder's fee keys on. */
  vaultTier: bigint;
  /** True when the account holds no lot, so the vault's tier prices the whole redemption. */
  usesVaultTierFallback: boolean;
  multiVaultQuote: MultiVaultRedeemQuotePlan;
};
```

```ts
type DynamicFeeCurveDeps = {
  curveAddresses: typeof bondingCurveRegistryCurveAddresses;
  getConfig: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveGetConfig;
  tierFeeOverride: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveTierFeeOverride;
  quoteDepositFee: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveQuoteDepositFee;
  claimableAcross: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveClaimableAcross;
  pendingFor: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurvePendingFor;
  bankedEarnings: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveBankedEarnings;
  vaultStake: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveVaultStake;
  userLots: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveUserLots;
  tierStake: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveTierStake;
  accFeePerShare: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveAccFeePerShare;
  /**
   * The depositor's stored lot debts, which decide what a deposit topping up an earning lot banks.
   * Optional so offline callers that inject every read can omit it; without it the projection
   * checkpoints the depositor's lots at the current accumulators and reports nothing banked.
   */
  lotRewardDebt?: typeof dynamicFeeFlatPriceCurveLotRewardDebt;
  quoteDepositPlan: typeof multivaultQuoteDepositPlan;
  quoteRedeemPlan: typeof multivaultQuoteRedeemPlan;
};
```

### DynamicFeeCurveEarningsProjection

Public export.

```ts
export type DynamicFeeCurveEarningsProjection = {
  termId: Hex;
  curveId: bigint;
  curveAddress: Address;
  assetsIn: bigint;
  /** The curve fee this deposit pays, which is exactly what the distribution below hands out. */
  curveFee: bigint;
  /** Where the fee goes: per-tier cohort payouts and the exact accumulator deltas. */
  distribution: DynamicFeeDepositDistribution;
  /** Per-tier occupancy the distribution ran against, for rendering "who earns" honestly. */
  occupancy: DynamicFeeTierOccupancy;
  /** Per-tier accumulators the distribution ran against, the "before" the projection measures from. */
  accFeePerShare: DynamicFeeAccumulators;
  /** Present when a holder was named: their lots, total stake, and wei-exact projected earning. */
  holder?: {
    account: Address;
    lots: Array<{ tier: bigint; stake: bigint }>;
    stake: bigint;
    /** The pending delta the contract will write for this holder if the deposit executes now. */
    projectedEarning: bigint;
  };
};
```

# FeeProxy affiliate profile

Source: https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/sdk/fee-proxy-affiliate-profile

Applies to V2 · `@0xintuition/sdk` 4.0.0

API for `@0xintuition/sdk@4.0.0`. [Compatibility](https://docs.intuition.systems/docs/reference/compatibility) · [Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/fee-proxy-affiliate-profile.ts).

Import from `@0xintuition/sdk/actions`.

Signatures show the exact accepted inputs and return types. Named input/output structures and dependency-injection types are listed below; viem and protocol types come from their respective packages. Preparation and quote functions can perform RPC reads. Envelope builders on the action-envelope pages use caller-supplied read context and perform no RPC reads or signing. **`feeProxyExecutePlan` sends transactions**; the other SDK actions on these pages prepare transactions or read data.

## feeProxyGetAffiliateProfile

Reads everything a builder dashboard shows for one affiliate in one batched read: the registry
row (fees, fee recipient, registration time, pause flag), whether it is active, its aggregate
stats, the protocol caps and the registration fee. Uses the chain's Multicall3 (or the canonical
address); when the batch is unavailable or any leg fails it falls back to individual reads.

[Source](https://github.com/0xIntuition/packages/blob/4e9af1373b81a453d16bc650983138e35afb97d1/packages/sdk/src/actions/fee-proxy-affiliate-profile.ts#L136)

```ts
function feeProxyGetAffiliateProfile(
  config: ReadConfig,
  inputs: {
    affiliate: Address;
  },
): Promise<FeeProxyAffiliateProfile>;
```

- **`config`**: FeeProxy address and public client.
- **`inputs`**: The affiliate to profile.
- **returns**: The normalised profile: raw fees, fees as percentages, and headroom against the caps.
